News.title: Horrifying moment Brit tourists watch on as flames engulf hotel on Croatian island before panicked escape by boats
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment British trippers who escaped a terrifying wildfire watch on as their hotel erupted in a fiery inferno.

Shocking footage has emerged showing a huge crowd of tourists waiting to be rescued as the night sky lit up bright orange and filled with smoke.



Desperate holidaymakers can be seen stood in the dark as their forest retreat burned on the island of Brac, Croatia.

Some even jumped in the water to escape the flames, as burning embers fell on guests.



Scores of Brits fled to a flotilla of around 50 Dunkirk-style rescue boats mustered by local fishermen and boat trip bosses after a general alert was issued.

Holidaymaker Trevor Rwifght, a 62-year-old IT manager at the resort with wife Sharon, 68, from Stevenage, Herts said: “I’ll never forget feeling the heat from the fire closing in as we waited for the rescue boats.”

Brits who fled the woodland retreat then accused staff of abandoning them on the island.

Holidaymakers said they were left to fend for themselves with no evacuation plan as a wall of flame and a firestorm of blazing embers closed in on the Gava Waterman Milna Resort.



They said they were told there was “no further threat” to their Croatian holiday hotel – as it was engulfed by flames.

Angela Turkington, 52, from Grimsby, said: “We were given no help or advice and ran to the shore to wait to be rescued as the flames closed in – it was horrendous.



“But when we got on a boat to escape we finally got a text message telling us there was no threat to the hotel and everything was okay.

“We looked up as we got the text and could see that the hotel was on fire and surrounded by flames – it was unbelievable.”

Angela – travelling with a British travel company with her builder husband Lee, 52 – is currently in another hotel on Brac waiting for a flight home.

She added: “The customer service was nothing short of abysmal.



“People could have been killed by the fire or drowned trying to escape and their people didn’t have a clue what was going on and never contacted us as we escaped.”

Other trippers told The Sun how they fled as flames breached the hotel perimeter after being told to stay in their rooms and “relax with a drink.”

Customers of another travel firm now safe back in the UK revealed today how they received a text message after escaping the inferno telling them: “We’re sorry you decided to curtail your holiday”.



But the UK-based company later sent out a message declaring: “We are so sorry that you experienced this and understand that, following the evacuation, you made the decision to curtail your holiday.”

Trippers still in shock after the drama believe the wording is a legal move aimed at reducing compensation payouts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Josh Robbins, 26, from Dorset, said today: “We want all our money back and compensation for what we’ve been through but we’re being told it was an ‘act of God’ and we should claim insurance.”

A Gava Waterman Hotel spokesman denied guest claims that staff abandoned trippers, insisting some reception staff aided the evacuation.

News.title: Brazen gang smashed into Peppa Pig creator’s £10m mansion and stole £65k of luxury items including handbags & luggage
News.content:
MANSION RAID Brazen gang smashed into Peppa Pig creator’s £10m mansion and stole £65k of luxury items including handbags & luggage

A ROMANIAN burglary gang raided the £10million Surrey mansion of the creator of Peppa Pig, making off with £65,000 of loot.

Radu Dogaru, 41, and Adrian Alempi, 34, broke into Mark Baker’s sprawling home on February 14.



The pair were previously involved in one of Europe’s most brazen art thefts, stealing paintings by Picasso, Gauguin and Matisse from the Kunsthal Museum in Rotterdam, Netherlands, in 2012.

In the latest burglary, they stole 15 designer handbags, along with high-end suitcases and luggage from Mr Baker’s 12,500 sq ft home.



Swanky photographs shared online show the luxury property has a swimming pool, gym and spa complex, staff accommodation, six bedrooms, a cinema and garages for four cars.

Dogaru and Alempi – who was previously deported from the UK once before – successfully escaped after the burglary but were caught a few days later after raiding another home.



Speaking about the burglary at Mr Baker’s home, Recorder Joanne Cecil KC said: “Mr and Mrs Baker left their property at around 7pm but when they came back at 8.30pm they found it had been burgled.

“The value of the stolen items was £65,000 and included jewellery, a Rolex watch, Chanel and other designer handbags and suitcases.



“Prior to the burglary Dogaru and Alempi were seen arriving at Claygate Station at around 5pm.

“Between 7pm and 8.30pm they entered and exited the property through a first floor window.

“They were later seen arriving back at Claygate Station carrying bags. One was a Louis Vuitton suitcase which had been stolen in the burglary.”

Mr Baker and his wife had locked their doors but not properly set up their alarms before leaving their home in the same town that John Terry, Andy Murray and Jamie Redknapp previously lived.

The burglary had a significant impact on the Peppa Pig creator and his wife.



Recorder Cecil added: “Mrs Baker said it affected her badly. She didn’t want to leave the house in case she came back to find it burgled again.

“She has the alarm on all the time now. She said she screamed when her husband came up behind her wearing dark clothes as she thought he was a burglar.

“The stolen items also have a sentimental value as she has memories of where they were bought and things she has done with them.”

Police placed Dogaru and Alempi under surveillance – and just a few days later they struck again.



On February 17 they targeted another wealthy home in Robin Hood Way, Kingston

They lay in wait in a wooded area behind the house for around 30 minutes before breaking into the property at roughly 6.30pm.

Recorder Cecil said: “The victim was away on holiday at the time but he had CCTV and he got a notification on his phone.

“When he opened it he saw a male carrying his safe in his house. There was also a second man behind him.



“The victim contacted his neighbours and the police. His neighbour went around to the house and found several drawers open.

“He asked him to check on the safe but it had been removed and pieces of wood were lying on the floor.

“A number of high value items were in it, including jewellery, gold bars, cash in sterling and dollars, passports and other items.”

Dogaru and Alempi broke open the safe in the wooded area behind the house and stuffed the valuables into their backpacks.

However, they were caught by police after boarding a bus to flee the area.



Several items stolen from Mr Baker’s home were found in a subsequent search of Dogaru’s home.

Alempi – who was deported from the UK once before in 2014 before illegally returning earlier this year – and Dogaru were sentenced to five and four years respectively at Inner London Crown Court on Tuesday.

A third member of the burglary gang was also sentenced for handling stolen goods.

Alexandru Tepelus, 33, fenced stolen designer handbags, jewellery and other items to the same pawnbrokers used by Dogaru and Alempi.

Tepelus was caught selling some of the items stolen during a burglary in Coombe Park, Kingston, in 2024.



Burglars had taken £69,295 worth of goods from victim Amina Bawany.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But she spotted the items for sale on Invaluable.com and reported them to the police. The auction site then informed officers the goods had come from Prestige Pawnbrokers, which in turn gave officers Tepelus’ details.

Tepelus was handed a suspended sentence and told to complete 200 hours of unpaid work.

News.title: Labour’s ‘one in, one out’ costs eye-watering £56,000 to send each small boat arrival back to France
News.content:
SACRE BLEU Labour’s ‘one in, one out’ costs eye-watering £56,000 to send each small boat arrival back to France

LABOUR’s flagship “one in, one out” deal is costing an eye-watering £56,000 for every small boat arrival sent back to France, the Home Secretary has admitted.

Shabana Mahmood revealed the hefty price tag as she was grilled by MPs over whether the scheme is delivering value for taxpayers.



More than 1,400 migrants have been returned across the Channel – but Ms Mahmood conceded the numbers remain “relatively small”.

Asked how much each return had cost, she said: “I’ll need to write to the committee on the most recent figures.



“I think it’s per person for the numbers that have been returned so far, it’s about £56,000.”

She later defended the cost, insisting it was “still cheaper, or just about the same as supporting someone in a hotel for a year”.



Under the deal, Britain sends small boat migrants back to France in exchange for taking asylum seekers through a legal route.

The pilot has already been extended once and is now due to run into October, with its long-term future still up in the air.

France wants the bilateral arrangement eventually replaced by a wider EU-UK returns deal.

But Ms Mahmood slapped down suggestions an EU-wide system would be a “silver bullet” for the Channel crisis.



She boasted one-in-one-out had already returned more migrants than Britain ever managed under the EU’s old Dublin arrangements.

She said: “It is a real mistake to think that that pact is the future. And if we were in that, this problem would go away because I promise you, it would not.”

But the Home Secretary admitted the Government’s own scheme had struggled to get large numbers of migrants out of Britain, saying: “It’s not been without its challenges. Obviously, the numbers are still relatively small.”

She added it had been “operationally difficult” to dramatically ramp up removals because both Britain and France face constraints including detention space.

Ms Mahmood also told the Home Affairs Committee only “relatively small numbers” of failed asylum-seeking families have taken up a separate pilot offering them as much as £40,000 to voluntarily leave Britain.



She said: “If you’re a failed asylum-seeking family, what you’re trading off is an offer of £40,000, which will help you resettle back in your country of origin, versus, you know, access to free healthcare and education for your children.”

Britain is separately shelling out £662million to France over three years to tackle Channel crossings.

Ms Mahmood admitted it was “a lot of money” and “more than we were paying before”, but insisted the new deal allows cash to be targeted at measures that actually work.

News.title: Schoolbus crash leaves 16 children hospitalised after tyre blow out in German forest as mass casualty response activated
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

COACH HORROR Schoolbus crash leaves 16 children hospitalised after tyre blow out in German forest as mass casualty response activated

SIXTEEN schoolchildren have been hospitalised after a bus burst its tire and broke down in Germany.

Around 40 kids had been travelling to school when the driver lost control in Bärenstein, near Germany’s border with the Czech Republic.



The terrifying incident unfolded after the bus driver decided to take a detour off the B95 highway.

While driving through the mountainous Bärenstein region, a tire suddenly burst – and plunged the bus into chaos.



As the panic escalated, the driver managed to bring the bus to a stop – and escaped uninjured.

Nine ambulances raced to the scene and desperately pulled children from the wreckage.

A “mass casualty” incident had been launched as emergency departments initially struggled to piece together what had happened, said local media.

The entire regional fire department was also deployed to help the wounded in the forest area of Bärenstein.

Of the children on board, 24 survived unharmed.

The remaining 16 have been taken to hospital to be treated for “acoustic trauma”, police say.



A replacement bus sped to the accident and transported the uninjured children to Bärenstein primary school.

Police have opened a probe into the heart-stopping incident.

The Ore Mountains – where the bus broke down – has previously been marred by tragedy.

In December 2023, a young boy was killed after a bus smashed into a winter service vehicle.

And over the summer, one schoolboy lost his life in a devastating bus collision.



Dozens more were injured after two buses collided head-on near Hebertshausen in Upper Bavaria, Germany.

All 35 people involved in the smash were injured – many of them children.

The impact occurred on a bend in the road, where speed limits are set at 60 km/h in one direction and 50 km/h in the other.

Police did not know what caused the crash – which they described as “a very grim scene”.

News.title: Sick granddaughter, 32, stole cash from her dying grandad’s pockets as he slept before ransacking his car
News.content:
SICKENING THEFT Sick granddaughter, 32, stole cash from her dying grandad’s pockets as he slept before ransacking his car

A CALLOUS thief preyed on her dying granddad as he slept – before targeting her good Samaritan neighbour twice in three days and stealing her treasured wedding ring.

Faye Knowles, 32, was locked up for more than five years after being condemned by a judge as “wicked” and “beyond contempt”.



Leeds Crown Court heard how the mother-of-one treated terminally-ill Ray Issot as an “easy mark” while he was receiving palliative care in the final stages of his life.

After helping herself to £30 found in the pockets of his jeans, she then grabbed his car keys and ransacked his Ford Kuga looking for more to steal.



Leeds Crown Court heard Mr Issot had since passed away following the theft in April.

Passing sentence, judge Robin Mairs said Knowles’ crimes – in pursuit of funding her class A drug addiction – were “wicked”.



He said: “You stole the key to his address from your mother’s key ring. You entered his premises at night. You rilfed through his clothing and stole £30 from his jeans. That wasn’t sufficient.

“You stole his car keys and went through the car to see if there was anything else to steal. There wasn’t.



“This was an offence that was as utterly shameless as it was wicked.”

Judge Mairs said Knowles, from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, saw her own grandad as an “easy mark”, and told her: “To prey upon the vulnerable within your own family is beneath contempt.”

While on police bail, “shameless” Knowles and two men stole from the home of a “vulnerable” young man with mental illness, taking his Playstation among other personal items from his disability bungalow.

She then twice targeted her kindly neighbour in Wakefield in April this year.

The court heard how she stole £140 kept in a tin at the home of Helen Boughton on April 25 after being invited in.



She returned three days later to admit what she had done – but used the confession as “a ruse” to steal more of Ms Boughton’s possessions.

Judge Mairs said: “That confession wasn’t brought about by regret, or by contrition, for what you had done. That confession was another ruse, another hoax.

“Because you offered with your fake contrition to clean her house.

“You did that so you could get access to the upstairs of the premises. You had cleaned the bathroom, and then rooted and rummaged through her drawers for something to steal.

“You stole two men’s watches. And you stole her wedding ring. An item, I have no doubt, of great sentimental and emotional value.”



He added: “The effect upon her has been profound. She has changed her lifestyle. She now lives behind closed curtains. She has changed her route home to avoid people like you.

“This is what happens when you enter and steal from people’s homes -from where they should, feel safe, protected and secure.

“When you steal from them, what you do is you take that sense of security and safety from them.”

Knowles, who admitted counts of burglary, theft and attempted theft, also stole an electric scooter from the home of another woman.

She sobbed over a video-link from New Hall prison as she was jailed for five years and four months.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The court heard that Knowles’ crimes were as a result of her “difficulty” with class A drugs.

She was said to have made progress while on remand and is kept on a “drug-free” prison wing.

News.title: Shocking moment helicopter spins wildly and crashes onto tarmac as flight instructor loses control – leaving two injured
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment a helicopter crashed on the tarmac after a flight instructor lost control during a lesson.

CCTV footage shows the Bell 206 aircraft spinning uncontrollably before plummeting to the ground nearly vertically at Cedar City Regional Airport in Utah.



The chopper’s tail section is seen smashing into the taxiway as it continues to spiral – just metres away from another aircraft.

Two people are shown getting out of the neighbouring parked helicopter and rushed to the site of the crash.



Miraculously, both the instructor and the student managed to escape the horror with only minor injuries.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) released the video while announcing that the May 23 crash was caused by the 32-year-old teacher losing control, not a mechanical failure.



Incidents involving instructional helicopter flights in the US are extremely rare, averaging at a rate of 4.7 per 100,000 flight hours.

A long-term safety analysis tracked through an NTSB database recorded only 299 incidents in a 12-year period.

Last week, five people were killed after a helicopter crashed into a fireball at an airport on the Malaysian island of Borneo.

It comes after two Brit newlyweds died alongside a Greek pilot in a horror helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos in August.



Alexander Cromie, 31, and Marie Ebert, 30, were on the honeymoon when their chopper exploded into a fireball.

The deadly incident also involved Bell 206, which witnesses described as “spinning out of control” – suggesting a tail rotor failure.

A report filed with Greece’s Civil Aviation Authority said the pilot did not ensure the straps were removed before starting the engine.



Records suggest the chopper stayed in Paros for three days before the incident with the straps.

It was then given an air-worthiness certificate just over a month later, on July 2.

As a precaution, Greece‘s civil aviation authority has ruled that “visual and functional checks” on tail rotors must be carried out before every flight in the country involving a Bell 206 helicopter.

News.title: Dad’s heartbreak as he pulls wife and two children from burning bus but couldn’t reach daughter, 12, trapped in wreckage
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Dad’s heartbreak as he pulls wife and two children from burning bus but couldn’t reach daughter, 12, trapped in wreckage

A DAD has been left heartbroken after he rescued his wife and two children from a burning bus but was unable to reach his daughter trapped in the wreckage.

The horror unfolded at the Isiklar toll booths on the Northern Marmara Motorway in Istanbul, Turkey, on September 13.



Yusra Serac, 12, was one of two people killed in the crash after the bus collided into the barriers and caught fire while on its way to the capital.

The young girl had been travelling with her parents and two siblings on a family trip to the region.



Her father Mesut Serac, who was badly injured in the blaze, managed to pull his wife and two of his children from the burning vehicle – as well as several other passengers.

However, he was tragically unable to rescue his third daughter.

Terrifying CCTV footage shows flames engulfing the bus at the barrier as onlookers watch in horror.

“I spoke to her father and he is in no state to talk at the moment,” relative Kasim Serac said.



“He pulled five or six passengers out by their feet.

“They are a family of five, the mother, father and three children, and they live in Istanbul.”

He added that passengers struggled to escape as smoke billowed inside the bus and the doors failed to open.

“There were other children next to Mesut’s children and he was trying to save them too,” he said.

“They hit the window again and again but could not open it.



“When somebody finally opened the window from outside, the bus was already full of smoke and they could not see anything.

“He saved everyone he could, but sadly his daughter burned inside.”

Mesut was later discharged from hospital and went to the Forensic Medicine Institute to provide a DNA sample.

A family friend added: “A family has been destroyed.

“Her father will not recover from this easily.
