President Donald Trump has alleged that a “Democrat Plot” was behind the 2024 assassination attempt against him and claimed newly discovered information shows key evidence was missing, altered or corrupted.

“Everybody knows the Crooked Joe Biden FBI didn’t do what they should have with respect to the Lunatic who shot me in Butler, PA. By the time I got into Office, on January 20th, most of the information was missing, altered, corrupted, or gone,” Trump posted Tuesday on Truth Social.

The president continued: “New info was just found! Why wasn’t it seen long ago? This was all a Democrat Plot, to get me out of the Election, that failed. Dirty Cop Christopher Wray should pay a price for the way he handled this assassination attempt, and certainly for the things he said.”

There is no evidence that Democrats were involved in the attempted assassination of Trump at a campaign rally on July 13, 2024. After a extensive investigation, the FBI concluded last year that gunman Thomas Matthew Crooks acted alone.

The Independent has contacted the White House, FBI and the Office of Joe and Jill Biden for comment.

open image in gallery Then-Republican candidate Donald Trump is seen with blood on his face, surrounded by Secret Service agents following an attempted assassination in Butler, Pennsylvania, on July 13, 2024 ( AFP/Getty )

Crooks, 20, opened fire on Trump while he was on stage at the Butler Farm Show Grounds, shooting from a nearby rooftop with an AR-15-style rifle.

The gunfire grazed Trump’s right ear, killed rally attendee Corey Comperatore and injured two others. A U.S. Secret Service sniper shot and killed Crooks shortly after he began firing.

Hours after the attack, the FBI took over the investigation. According to the bureau, 485 employees worked on the case, conducting more than 1,000 interviews, reviewing 2,000 tips and executing more than 10 search warrants and 100 subpoenas.

Investigators examined 13 electronic devices connected to Crooks and his family, along with 35 online accounts, including social media, banking and email accounts. The FBI said it accessed all of Crooks’ accounts, including email accounts based in Germany and Belgium, and manually reviewed more than 500,000 electronic files.

open image in gallery A bullet grazed Trump’s right ear, killed rally attendee Corey Comperatore and injured two others ( EPA )

open image in gallery The FBI concluded that Crooks acted alone and found no evidence that a foreign person, government or organization directed or assisted him, FBI Director Kash Patel and former Deputy Director Dan Bongino told Fox News Digital in November 2025 ( Pennsylvania DOT )

The FBI concluded that Crooks acted alone, FBI Director Kash Patel and former Deputy Director Dan Bongino told Fox News Digital in November 2025.

The bureau said it found no evidence that a foreign individual, government or organization directed, inspired or assisted Crooks.

“We fully briefed the president, as a victim of this case, at the White House, providing him with all of the details of our investigation, and the president was satisfied with the results and where we left it,” Patel said.

open image in gallery Thomas Crooks used the white air conditioning unit on the right to climb onto the roof of the building to take aim at Trump ( FBI )

Bongino added: “We have reviewed this case over and over — looked into every nugget. We have spoken to the families, the president — there is no cover-up here.”

Trump’s post about the mishandling of his Butler assassination attempt follows earlier Truth Social rants Monday and Tuesday about AI.

News.title: Liverpool vs Tottenham LIVE: Team news as Andy Robertson on bench for Anfield return in Carabao Cup
News.content:
Andy Robertson is back at Anfield tonight ( Getty Images )

Liverpool welcome struggling Tottenham to Anfield as the Carabao Cup pits two heavyweights against each other in the early rounds.

The Reds begin their Carabao Cup campaign tonight, while Tottenham - without a goal in the Premier League - travel north off the back of their thumping second-round triumph over Charlton.

Andoni Iraola’s start to life as Liverpool boss has been hit and miss, with Saturday’s drab goalless draw at home to Fulham stunting momentum picked up from back-to-back wins over Ipswich and Atletico Madrid.

He finds himself in a less desperate position than Roberto De Zerbi, however, who will hope legendary former Reds left-back Andy Robertson can provide the inside track on Anfield on his emotional return to Merseyside.

News.content:

Donald Trump has again claimed that an end to his war with Iran is within reach. But, not for the first time, the notion has been rapidly debunked.

Indeed, the rapid advance of Houthi rebel forces, so that they can tighten their grip on oil supplies moving through the Red Sea, is evidence that the conflict is spreading and intensifying. The group, closely linked to Tehran, has swept through southern Yemen. This is drawing Saudi Arabia into renewing its long and merciless battle with the Houthis that ended, uneasily, in stalemate a few years ago.

The possibility of all-out direct war between Iran and Saudi Arabia, turning the regional Shia-Sunni schism into one of geopolitical consequence, is one of the many “nightmare scenarios” that are now perilously close to coming to pass. Others include clashes between European powers and Russia, simmering Sino-American tensions and the rivalry between Israel and Iran, which has already erupted. AI and climate change only add an additional terrifying backdrop to the bleak picture.

The upshot is the price of a barrel of oil is back up above the $100 mark, a gallon of diesel in the US has hit an all-time high of $6 a gallon, the world economy teeters on the brink of recession, and the president himself is staring defeat in the mid-term elections in the face.

According to Mr Trump, though, things could hardly be going more to his non-existent plan. His latest social media post on the immediate prospects declares in his usual bombastic style: “The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly. I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage – The concept of which we are open to. Thank you for your attention to this matter!”

A deal would of course be very welcome for a world economy on the edge of recession. Yet, within a matter of hours, Tehran dismissed his claims. So, far from the government of the Islamic Republic being cowed and disabled by President Trump’s “victory” in a war so obviously not yet over, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of Iran, was actually impertinent enough to counter: “The stakes around oil and the straits have changed. Damage control won’t stop what’s coming. No talks until Iran’s conditions are met. Period!”

Mr Rezaei is unfortunately more right than Mr Trump in his assessment of the situation. Talks to open up the Strait of Hormuz have stalled ever since the US-Iran “Memorandum of Understanding” collapsed in July, after less than a month in operation. There have no doubt been many conversations via semi-secret back-channels facilitated by the likes of Oman, but there are as yet no visible signs of progress. Contrary to equally exaggerated claims by Mr Trump, traffic through the Strait is not back to normal.

In short, things are getting worse for America, and rather better for Iran and its increasingly active allies in the Houthi rebel movement. The principal routes for the supply of much of the world’s oil, natural gas, and related commodities such as fertilisers and pharmaceutical precursors are more or less firmly under the control of Iran and its proxies – the Strait of Hormuz, the East-West pipeline used by Saudi Arabia as an alternative route to the Red Sea, is being bombed at will, and the shipping through the Bab al-Mandab Strait is being disrupted.

This is the western counterpart to the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian peninsula, and it is the gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. This is now being menaced ever more by the Houthis, who’ve made startling advances against their enemies – Yemen and Saudi Arabia, which are occasionally humiliated by these guerrillas. For the first time in this phase of their long-running battles, the Saudi civil defence has had to issue an alert of potential danger to Mecca, home to Islam’s holiest site and a place of huge symbolic significance.

That the world’s greatest superpower still finds itself bullied and banjaxed by a badly mauled Iran and a few Houthi fighters armed with pick-up trucks and drones may dismay observers, but it is really no great surprise. It also has many precedents.

The Americans are being systematically beaten in an “asymmetrical” never-ending war they cannot win. The same was true in Iraq, Afghanistan and Vietnam. It was during that earlier disaster that the then president Richard Nixon bemoaned such a plight in these terms: “If, when the chips are down, the world’s most powerful nation, the United States of America, acts like a pitiful, helpless giant, the forces of totalitarianism and anarchy will threaten free nations and free institutions throughout the world.”

He eventually found, just as Mr Trump is doing now, that the only escape from such a trap is to accept reality, declare “peace with honour”, move on with as much dignity as possible, and try to learn the lessons.

Sweden’s left-leaning bloc has crept ahead of the ruling right-wing coalition in a neck-and-neck general election.

Led by former prime minister Magdalena Andersson of the centre-left Social Democrat party, the left bloc, including the Left Party, Centre Party, and Green Party, is projected to win 176 seats in the 349 seat parliament.

But around six per cent of the vote is yet to be counted, as incumbent prime minister Ulf Kristersson - leading a right-wing grouping of the Christian Democrats, Liberal Party, and the hard-right Sweden Democrats - looks to turn the result around.

His governing bloc trails with a projected 173 seats, separated by roughly 20,000 votes, with the results expected to be finalised on Wednesday, the election authority said.

Election maps paint a clear picture of success for the centre left Social Democrats and centre-right Moderates in densely populated and inner-city areas, while the Sweden Democrats, a party with neo-Nazi roots, typically won in more rural areas.

open image in gallery A map by Swedish national broadcaster SVT shows the Social Democrats in control of the country's north and battling with the Moderates for inner-city areas in southern areas. Red = Social Democrats (centre-left); Blue = Moderates (governing centre-right); Yellow = Sweden Democrats (hard right) ( SVT )

The map, from Swedish public broadcaster SVT, presents the Social Democrats as red, the Sweden Democrats as yellow and the Moderates as light blue.

It shows that the capital of Stockholm and major cities including Gothenburg and Malmo lean heavily towards the Social Democrats and the Moderates.

Exit polls from public broadcaster SVT had initially shown the left-wing parties ahead by several percentage points, prompting jubilation at the Social Democrats' election night gathering in Stockholm, though the mood shifted to quiet waiting as the preliminary results proved to be closer.

The projected victory for the left bloc was driven mainly by losses for the far-right Sweden Democrats party, which had helped steer the once-liberal nation towards some of Europe's strictest migration rules.

But final results are not expected before Wednesday, when local election boards count postal votes that arrived too late for polling day, along with ballots cast from abroad.

Sweden elects its parliament through a proportional representation system, with parties needing at least 4 per cent of the vote to win seats. More than 8 million of the country's roughly 10.6 million people were eligible to vote.

​​The country's political landscape is split between two four-party blocs, on the left and the right, meaning the outcome hinges less on any single party's result and more on which side can assemble a majority.

open image in gallery Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson (Moderate Party) leaves the official residence, Sager House, the day after Sweden's very close general election ( Reuters )

Both the Social Democrats (28.1 per cent) and the Sweden Democrats (17.6 per cent), who had been the largest two parties after the 2022 elections, have seen small downswings of 2.3 per cent and 3 percent respectively.

The Moderates, led by Mr Kristersson, have enjoyed a 0.8 per cent uptick and are the second largest party in the preliminary results, 2.3 points above the Sweden Democrats.

In total, preliminary results have the left bloc vote at 49.5 per cent, while the right bloc sits at 49.1 per cent.

Speaking early on Monday, Mr Kristersson said the outcome remained genuinely uncertain, though he pointed to what he described as a broader ideological majority in parliament.

"There is a very clear non-socialist majority, or non-left leaning economic majority in the Swedish parliament," he said.

"When we have the final result it's a good idea to look at possible combinations. I will actually take note of that and at least figure out whether there are any possibilities."

No major media outlet had called the result. Ms Andersson urged her own supporters to wait for the final count.

"We must wait for the final election result," she said. "Right now we are leading, but we have to wait for the final result."

A rare, serious brain condition has been identified in a small number of people taking GLP-1 weight loss and diabetes drugs, a new study revealed.

Some 15 cases of Wernicke encephalopathy were identified between 2023-2024 in an Israeli study’s review of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s adverse event reports and related literature.

Wernicke encephalopathy is a potentially life-threatening neurological disorder caused by a severe deficiency of vitamin B1 that can lead to permanent memory loss and an inability to form new memories.

Experts stressed that this condition is not common.

"Researchers went through adverse event reports and the medical literature and found a small number of cases, 15, of Wernicke encephalopathy in people taking GLP-1 drugs,” Karthik Achari, a Chicago-based clinician who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "That's out of millions of people on these medications. So this is rare."

A small number of people who took GLP-1 drugs developed a rare brain condition - but experts say they can’t prove one caused the other yet ( Reuters )

"But it's real, it's serious, and the mechanism makes sense," he added.

Most of the 15 cases in the study were reported in people suffering gastrointestinal side effects from the drugs, such as vomiting and diarrhea, and loss of appetite.

Vitamin B1, which supports the nervous system and brain health, only comes from food and supplements.

“Most patients [13 of 15] reported gastrointestinal manifestations of either weight loss, vomiting, loss of appetite or malnutrition,” the researchers wrote.

Some 11 percent of U.S. adults - or around 30 million - now take GLP-1 drugs for weight loss, according to a Gallup poll conducted this summer.

The majority of the cases in the study occurred with GLP-1 drugs made with the active ingredient semaglutide, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, or tirzepatide GLP-1s, like in Zepbound.

The Independent has contacted drug makers, Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, for comment.

The findings suggest that patients on the drugs who experience more intense gastrointestinal side effects may be at an increased risk for Wernicke encephalopathy.

However, the researchers noted that FDA reports cannot prove the GLP-1 medications caused the condition. More research is needed to do that and the scientists were clear that patients should not stop taking prescribed GLP-1 drugs based on the study alone.

Past research has also discovered possible links between a small number of GLP-1 drug users and the brain condition.

“We noticed that patients weren't just losing weight; they were also experiencing severe gastroparesis and persistent vomiting,” Dr. Manar Kadhem, from Egypt’s Mansoura University, wrote in the research published in April.

Immediate treatment is necessary to prevent the worst outcomes from Wernicke encephalopathy.

“Emergency treatment with thiamine is essential. It may relieve symptoms and prevent permanent damage to memory and other brain functions,” the Cleveland Clinic explains.

FBI Director Kash Patel was repeatedly forced to clarify during a Senate hearing whether the nation’s top law enforcement agency was employing people who committed acts of bestiality, quickly derailing hotly anticipated testimony under an avalanche of criticism and controversy.

Patel faced pointed questions from both Democratic and Republican members on the Senate Judiciary Committee Tuesday about the apparent staffing crisis at the bureau, including from GOP Senator John Kennedy, who explicitly asked, “You’re not telling us today that if a human being had sex with an animal, that they can still be an FBI agent?”

No, Patel said. He argued that newly loosened hiring standards are meant to protect survivors of human trafficking and people who were forced into acts of bestiality, not open the agency to offenders.

The agency quietly amended its hiring practices earlier this year and will reportedly consider applicants for special agent positions and other bureau roles even if they have paid for sex, though FBI officials have repeatedly stressed that people who committed sex crimes would still be ineligible.

“Applicants who have engaged in bestiality,” said Patel, referencing the hiring language, “means they were victims of bestiality because they were forced to do so.”

open image in gallery FBI Director Kash Patel says loosened hiring practices are designed to protect survivors of bestiality who apply for the bureau, not offenders ( Getty )

Patel grilled over ‘bestiality’

Kennedy, frustrated, repeatedly asked Patel why the FBI would even need to specifically clarify hiring language when it comes to bestiality while the bureau faces intense scrutiny over a mass exodus of agents.

“All of this stuff has really hurt the FBI. It’s really hurt the FBI,” Kennedy said. “Why would you, in light of the context, and what we’re going through — we’re having a hard time attracting agents, good quality agents we all can trust, because so many people, fairly or unfairly, think in order you have to be an FBI agent now, your political point of view matters. Why would you even get into bestiality?”

Patel then tried to answer before the senator offered an example.

“If Joe participated in bestiality, not as the animal but as the human, don’t you think he oughta be disqualified?” Kennedy said.

Patel said that person would be disqualified from the bureau if they “voluntarily” engaged in bestiality, but not if they were trafficked.

“How do you involuntarily do it?” asked Kennedy, who suggested that the hiring language was recommended to Patel by other FBI employees.

“I say this with respect,” Kennedy said. “The person who recommended it, why didn’t you just say, ‘What planet did you parachute from?’”

open image in gallery Republican Senator John Kennedy repeatedly questioned Patel about ‘bestiality’ as the Senate Judiciary Committee heard testimony from the beleaguered hiring director ( Getty )

Applicants also will not be automatically disqualified from the bureau if they stole from an employee, as long as the incident occurred more than three years ago.

It remains unclear what prompted changes to the application process and hiring language, but retired FBI agent Daniel Brunner told the Associated Press that likely indicates a staffing problem at the bureau, which lost more than 1,000 special agents in 2025, according to an analysis of federal personnel data from Justice Connection.

“If they’re moving the bar for sexual encounters to include prostitution, what is that saying about the applicant pool? They’re trying to bring in more people, which to me indicates that the applicant pool is extremely shallow right now,” Brunner told the outlet.

The FBI director defended the mass purge of agents from the bureau, claiming they were “weaponizing” the agency under President Joe Biden.

Agents were removed “for reasons that they basically failed to meet the standards of the FBI,” then claimed that they “were terminated for weaponizing the Federal Bureau of Investigation.”

open image in gallery Patel faced several questions about the FBI’s role in midterm elections and whether agents will be deployed to polling sites on Election Day ( Reuters )

Patel refuses to say FBI won’t ‘interfere’ with elections

Democratic members of the panel repeatedly asked Patel whether he intends to deploy FBI agents to the polls on Election Day after several officials from Donald Trump’s administration refuse to dismiss the idea of federal agents or federalized National Guard troops stationed at polling stations.

“We have election crisis coordinators manned at all 56 field offices,” he told Senator Peter Welch. “The FBI will not shy away from that effort.”

But he refused to answer whether the FBI will “in any way interfere in the will of the American people” when they cast their ballots.

“I pledge unequivocally that I will not participate in your charade of lies,” Patel told Welch.

open image in gallery Members of the panel, including Republican chair Chuck Grassley, have previously sought answers from the FBI director about controversial expenses at the bureau, including a fleet of BMW vehicles ( AFP/Getty )

Patel says he’s the victim of ‘smear campaign’ over questions on spending and drinking

Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit earlier this year against The Atlantic, which is standing by a journalist’s reporting that characterized the FBI director as a deeply paranoid figure prone to drinking to excess. His lawsuit accuses the outlet of publishing a “sweeping, malicious and defamatory hit piece.”

“As a U.S. citizen, I have every right to claim the truth,” Patel told the committee Tuesday. “She printed false material. I am taking her to court.”

He then shot back at Democratic Senator Peter Welch, who was questioning Patel, for “participating” in a “smear campaign” against him.

“You cannot stand the fact that President Trump and this FBI have made America more secure than it’s ever been,” he said. “Your time’s up.”

Asked whether the FBI is investigating the journalist, Patel told Welch: “You hard of hearing? I just said no.”

open image in gallery Patel’s girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, sat behind the FBI director at his hearing, where he faced questions about their alleged use of government resources for personal trips ( AFP/Getty )

Patel is also the subject of several investigations from Democratic members of Congress over his alleged “misuse” of taxpayer funds for “luxury” expenses, including a fleet of BMW vehicles, while jet setting on “official” business that includes jet ski trips and helicopter tours.

The investigation, launched by top Democrats on the House and Senate Judiciary Committees, follows a letter to Patel from Republican Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley, who demanded that the FBI director answer questions about luxury cars, his use of government aircraft and whether he reimbursed taxpayers for personal travel.

In their letter, dated July 8, Rep. Jamie Raskin and Sen. Dick Durbin said Patel has been accused of demanding special “perks” during international travel, including “VIP snorkeling” trips in Hawaii and jet skiing, helicopter tours and other recreational activities while on FBI business.

Grassley — a top Trump ally in the Senate — asked Patel in May to “please explain why you decided to purchase BMW vehicles instead of Chevy Suburbans.”

Pressed by Democratic Senator Cory Booker on whether he enlisted a SWAT detail to protect and drive his girlfriend, Patel accused him of “attacking me and my loved ones.”

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Donald Trump has attacked what he calls a “sick conspiracy” against AI after the head of Anthropic called for a slowdown in the technology’s development.

The US president warned that China would benefit after the bosses of Silicon Valley’s top AI companies backed calls to restrict AI development for safety reasons, calling the concerns a “hoax”.

He also launched a tirade against Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, whom he accused of trying to be a “perfect little angel”.

Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social: “The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so!

“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China.”

Mr Amodei released a letter at the weekend calling for an industry-wide slowdown, endorsed by the US government, to prevent safety issues going “seriously wrong”.

In response, Mr Trump wrote: “Concerning AI, when, in the history of business, did anyone see the leaders of an industry call for regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy.

“AI taking over the world, destroying humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX.”

JD Vance, the US vice-president, echoed Mr Trump’s comments, calling tech leaders’ requests a “Trojan horse”.

He added: “I have to say, just personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them.

“It feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse.”

OpenAI has since called on the UK Government to introduce mandatory safety rules for major AI developers.

Under proposals supported by the company, the UK’s AI Security Institute would play a central role in third-party testing and creating adaptive technical standards.

Tom Duff-Gordon, the company’s head of policy in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told Politico: “OpenAI is in a position to support legislation in the UK to establish durable, mandatory, capability-based requirements for frontier AI that would build on the set of voluntary commitments that we currently have.”

Under the plans, Britain would move from the current system of voluntary agreements with AI companies to enforceable standards, bringing the UK in line with emerging frameworks in the EU and US.

The Government has not yet put forward plans for AI safety legislation, despite pressure from backbench MPs.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Wall Street after AI bosses called for a slowdown, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping by as much as 1.3pc.

Nvidia, the world’s largest listed company and a manufacturer of semiconductors used in the AI race, plunged by 4.2pc while fellow chipmaker AMD dropped 6.2pc.

The main European indexes in France, Germany and Spain were all down sharply on Monday after falls in South Korea and Japan overnight.

News.title: The best boutique hotels in Madrid
News.content:
In Madrid, choosing a boutique hotel gives you the chance to stay in some of the Spanish capital’s most elegant buildings, with smart design and often palatial levels of grandeur. This is a particularly noisy and frantic city, but as soon as you step inside these calm havens, you can relax and get yourself ready for more urban adventures. The people on reception and behind the bar have more time to chat and are usually more than willing to spill their secrets on favourite bars, restaurants and shops.

Although these places are smaller than the chain hotels, they often have spectacular roof terraces as well as attractive spas and great restaurants. This is also an opportunity to stay in some of the smartest neighbourhoods, such as Salesas and Salamanca, where you might find yourself fantasising about living in Madrid as you drift around the boutiques and bakeries near your hotel. News.title: 50 of the most family-friendly hotels in France
News.content:
La belle France promises endless family escapades – by the sea or sand dunes, overlooking horse-ploughed vines or atop a mountain or a clifftop. Natural green space for children of all ages to let off steam is in abundance pretty much all over the hexagon, and as French hoteliers refine their services and facilities to make stays more eco-conscious, there’s never been a greener and more exhilarating choice of places to stay en famille. Château, chalet, hôtel particular (historic mansion), upcycled oil mill or belle epoque seaside villa: all budgets are embraced with signature French panache.

Sophisticated city hotels and resorts entertain with action-packed kids’ clubs, themed treasure hunts, outdoor activities and hands-on workshops like patisserie classes, grape-picking and cheese-making. Mid-range hotels pamper young explorers with traditional games, kitchen-garden visits and old-fashioned fun en plein air. Away from towns and cities, hotels increasingly offer flexible self-catering packages too – a cottage positioned on a rambling estate perhaps – allowing families to mix-and-match hotel dining with their own, memorable market-sourced feasts.

Located in Paris, Provence or pinprick hamlets you’ve probably never heard of: here are 50 of the best family-friendly hotels in France.

JOHN OBI MIKEL says Chelsea are ‘suffering’ because they did not replace Enzo Fernandez.

But that solid form on paper hides a worrying trend.

“We talk about leaking goals. Yes, we can blame the defence, but you need at least two holding players to be able to shield and protect the back-four in that system.

“You need that because you’re going to be exposed. That is one position that the club has failed to strengthen during the transfer window. We failed.

“The likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro… they’re not going to defend as much.

Sports.title: ‘I am really disappointed’ – Howard Webb scolds VAR Matt Donohue as ‘tunnel vision’ sees Haaland goal at Man Utd allowed
Sports.content:
REFS chief Howard Webb blamed “tunnel vision” by VAR Matt Donohue for his shocking Old Trafford blunder.

Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus have both been stood down from officiating duties until next month after failing to recognise Enzo Fernandez was clearly offside ahead of Erling Haaland’s derby winner.



Pro Ref bosses realised the scale of the howler almost instantly, with Webb green-lighting the swift admissions of an “error of judgement” on Sunday night.

The audio of the incident, played out for the first time on the “Mic’d Up” review programme, showed Donohue and the Stockley Park hub crew were swiftly able to confirm Haaland was played 3cm onside by Patrick Dorgu’s toe, relaying that to referee Michael Oliver.



But the officials then focused on the fact that Fernandez had not got a touch on the cross rather than his impact on both Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens.

While Oliver is heard in the background explaining to players of both sides that Haaland was wrongly flagged, Donohue tells his colleagues: “Deflection (by Dorgu). Onside. No touch there, confirm no touch.

“Clear gap. There’s not a touch there, is there? It’s not a touch there? Goal.”

He then switches Oliver’s link back on to say: “Michael, confirming that you need to change your decision to goal. Haaland is in an onside position. Final decision is goal, check complete.”



And now the referees’ boss has conceded the damage done by the error, with Donohue and Antrobus both responsible.

Webb, who confirmed he had apologised to United, said: “I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they’re obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation.

“The VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he’s onside, he thinks that’s a good goal, Haaland’s not offside, as was thought initially.

“But he doesn’t truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez’s position and doesn’t truly evaluate other elements of offside.



“In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it’s down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn’t happen on this occasion.

“When you’re sat in that chair, and you’ve got other things going through your head, you can get that tunnel-vision sort of effect.

“We’ve seen that before and put processes in place that protect us from that, with the assistant VAR, stepping in to pull the VAR out of that tunnel, but it didn’t happen on this occasion.

“This goal should’ve been disallowed.

“Highly unfortunately, it wasn’t, and we’ll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again.”



The other contentious incident on Sunday saw Phil Foden dismissed after a retaliatory kick at United skipper Bruno Fernandes, after the England midfielder had been booted on his backside.

Webb, though, backed ref Michael Oliver’s red card decision for Foden but felt the “petulant kick” by Fernandes only met the threshold for a yellow card, which the VAR is not empowered to recommend.

The Pro Ref boss also supported three more crunch calls, although he admitted the handball Law that meant United defender Harry Maguire’s mishit strike off Ipswich’s Jacob Greaves being allowed to stand as it was an own goal, after the former England centre-half handled was “a bit of a nonsense”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Webb said that VAR Peter Bankes could see the “three stripes” on Neco Williams Nottingham Forest long sleeves rippling before he accidentally nudged over the line for a goal that was eventually chalked off against Spurs, adding: “It’s clear. It’s conclusive, and the goal has to be disallowed.”

And Liverpool’s stoppage time equalising penalty in the opening weekend draw at Newcastle was “a really good call late in the game” and evidence of the push, approved by club chiefs before the season, of the “referee’s call” taking priority unless there has been a major error.

Sports.title: English football competition to be renamed AGAIN midway through season as £5million sponsorship deal struck
Sports.content:
THE EFL Trophy is set to be renamed AGAIN with American fast-food giant Jersey Mike’s closing in on a £5million sponsorship deal.

The five-year agreement is expected to see the competition take on a new title as the US chain prepares to launch its British expansion.



Daily Mail Sport understands the EFL is close to sealing the record partnership, which will also see prize money increased for clubs competing in the tournament.

Officials are hoping to announce the deal before the next round of fixtures in this season’s midweek knockout competition.



The EFL Trophy is contested by all 48 League One and League Two clubs, alongside 16 invited Premier League Under-21 sides.

It was known as the Vertu Trophy for the past three seasons, with that sponsorship deal ending after the 2025/26 campaign.



Jersey Mike’s is relatively unknown in Britain (although the chain is preparing to launch in the UK with its first store expected to open in London later this year), but is already a major name in the US and Canada, where it has around 3,300 branches and annual turnover of roughly $4.2billion.

It hopes to eventually open around 400 outlets across the UK and Ireland.

The deal would provide Jersey Mike’s with a huge marketing platform as it attempts to establish itself in the British market.

And the fast-food giant the TWELFTH different company to put its name on the competition.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The tournament has been renamed repeatedly since sponsorship first became a major part of its identity in the 1980s.

It was the Freight Rover Trophy between 1984 and 1987, before becoming the Sherpa Van Trophy for two seasons.

Leyland DAF then took over, followed by Autoglass and Auto Windscreens.



The competition spent seven seasons as the LDV Vans Trophy before Johnstone’s Paint became the title sponsor for an impressive nine-year spell.

It then became the Checkatrade Trophy, followed by the Leasing.com Trophy and Papa Johns Trophy.

The Bristol Street Motors Trophy was the second most recent incarnation before Vertu took over for the last three seasons.

Now Jersey Mike’s is poised to become the latest name attached to the competition.

The agreement is reportedly worth around £5million over five seasons, with clubs expected to receive an initial £900,000 payment this campaign.

Sports.title: Moment Raheem Sterling is arrested in front passenger seat of his Lambo with canisters and deflated balloon in his lap
Sports.content:
THIS is the moment Raheem Sterling is arrested in his Lambo with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap.

Police bodycam footage shows a cop open his car door and say “you can put that down” to Sterling.



The footballer then takes the items from his lap and puts them behind his seat.

The officer says “can you jump out for me” and asks him who was driving the car when it was involved in a crash.





Sterling doesn’t reply when he’s asked: “Who was the person driving at that time?”

The officer continues: “So you refuse to answer, okay.”



Sterling is then told to get out of the car and asked his name and age at the roadside.

The cop says: “Put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.

“Put your arm behind your back.”



The ex-England winger, 31, is then read his rights as he is arrested.

Further footage, captured before he was pulled over, shows the footballer swerving in and out of lanes on a busy motorway.

Terrifying dash cam footage shows his black SUV-style motor randomly pulling out of the left hand lane in front of an approaching car.

He later swerves all the way across the three lane road and collides briefly with the central reservation.

Sterling continues to drive along the motorway, swaying from lane to lane as other drivers slow down and keep their distance from the driver.



Later, Sterling would crash his Lamborghini before being arrested for his involvement in the collision.

He could get locked up for two years after his £270,000 Lamborghini motorway crash.

Sterling, who is currently without a club, admitted dangerous driving on the M25, M3 and A327, possessing laughing gas and failing to provide a specimen at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court.



Motorists dialled 999 after seeing a black luxury 4×4 swerving across the M3 in Hampshire just before 9am on May 28.

He was seen driving erratically at 1.10am that morning – eight hours before his arrest – at a McDonald’s in Hayes, witnesses described seeing him with a pink balloon in his hand.

Sterling was then seen on the M25 near Watford at 7.45am with a large canister in his hand while driving at 30-40mph and then putting a balloon in his mouth.

The former Liverpool, Man City and Chelsea winger was arrested close to an interchange near Farnborough with six 670g nitrous oxide canisters in his car.

He told custody staff he has a problem with nitrous oxide when he was arrested, prosecutor Simon Jones told the court.



A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman previously said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.”

Witness statements read out to the court described his erratic driving as he quickly and repeatedly swerved between lanes without indicating, accelerated and braked suddenly, and almost crashed into the central reservation.



Nitrous oxide, also known as laughing gas and hippy crack, was made illegal when reclassified as a class C controlled substance in November 2023.

Usage is rife among footballers, despite its dangers including the risk of heart attacks, stroke and brain damage.

It typically comes in supersized canisters used to fill balloons, which are then inhaled repeatedly to give a euphoric, short-lived high.

Sterling was just 15 when he was signed by Liverpool from the QPR academy in 2010.

He became a fans’ favourite at Anfield before a contract dispute saw him move to Manchester City in 2015.



There he enjoyed massive success — winning four Premier League titles, five Carabao Cups and an FA Cup.

However, sources close to Sterling told how his mental health suffered following his £50million transfer from Man City to Chelsea in July 2022.

He was eventually ordered to train separately to the first-team group after then-manager Enzo Maresca — now Man City boss — decided he was surplus to requirements.

A loan deal to Arsenal followed, but did not work out, so in February he joined Dutch club Feyenoord.

That deal ended in the summer and he is now without a club.



Sources also claimed he has been written off and made to feel “worthless” despite gaining 82 England caps.

Since the M3 incident, Sterling has kept a low profile and has rarely been pictured, apart from social media footage of him playing football with his children.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He is engaged to childhood sweetheart Paige Milian, 30, with whom he has two kids.

He also has a daughter from a previous relationship.

Sports.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia

The Leeds United striker has been on top form since his move from Everton and is line for an international recall when Thomas Tuchel names his latest squad

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds United celebrates his goal to make it 3-0 vs Newcastle

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spent nine seasons in the Premier League with Everton and his most productive campaign was 2020/21 when he scored 16 goals in 33 appearances. He also scored twice in the FA Cup and three times in the EFL Cup.

‌



It was the full Covid season, played almost entirely behind closed doors. There was a theory amongst some Evertonians that Calvert-Lewin felt less pressure without the presence of a set of fans who could be highly critical.

‌



That theory seemed ill-founded. He played in nine matches behind closed doors in the restarted 2019/20 season and did not score once.

‌



And he has performed well under pressure many times in his career. But there is no doubt Calvert-Lewin can experience confidence swings.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



And he has spoken honestly and commendably about mental struggles during a career frequently interrupted by injury. Which is why it is fantastic to see Calvert-Lewin full of confidence, loving his football and looking in the form of his life.

He has now scored 16 goals in 34 Premier League appearances for Leeds United. Considering their serious striking issues - Thierno Barry being the only recognised centre-forward - some Everton fans have been lamenting that Calvert-Lewin was allowed to leave on a free transfer at the end of the 2024/25 season.

But realistically, the long-standing relationship - he was at Everton for nine seasons - had run its course and a change of scenery was best for him. And when he went to Elland Road, it was hard not to feel it would go one of two ways.

‌



View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin's last appearance for England was in a friendly against Uruguay in March (Image: Getty Images)

It would be confirmation that physical setbacks had taken a long-term toll on a hugely talented player or it would restart a career that has seemed so promising. It is most definitely the latter.

Calvert-Lewin turns 30 next March but there is every chance we have not seen the best of the Sheffield-born striker. It goes without saying that is fantastic news for Leeds United - it should also be fantastic news for England.

‌



Calvert-Lewin was unlucky not to be taken to the World Cup and Thomas Tuchel, who did give him half an hour in a friendly against Uruguay early in the year, will surely include him in his next squad, which will be announced on Friday. England have four UEFA Nations League matches coming up. They host world champions Spain before travelling to the Czech Republic and Croatia and then returning to Wembley to play the Czechs again.

The Leeds forward - rightly dismayed at having a goal taken away from him after his towering header took a nick off Jayden Bogle - will surely feature in parts of those games. Calvert-Lewin has just run amok against Newcastle in the Premier League, while Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney are content with cheap goals and bumper pay deals in Saudi Arabia.

View 3 Images England are still heavily reliant on captain Harry Kane (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel’s and England’s reliance on Harry Kane remains. And will do up until and throughout Euro 2028.

But Calvert-Lewin still has time to establish himself as a serious alternative, a high-quality back-up. When he came on as a substitute against Uruguay in March, it was his first England appearance in almost five years.

Calvert-Lewin has 12 caps. In the five games he has started, he has scored four goals.

Article continues below

True, the field is thin, but when it comes to the fight to be considered as the main alternative to Kane, Calvert-Lewin should be winning it. And he has not got the confidence to shine on the grandest stages.

Sports.title: Rangers legend Nacho Novo's son dies as he pays tribute to 'my boy'
Sports.content:
Rangers legend Nacho Novo's son dies as he pays tribute to 'my boy'

Rangers legend Nacho Novo, 47, shared on Instagram that nothing "could have prepared him" for the post to say that his "beautiful son" had died and he will be forever in "our hearts"

View 3 Images Nacho Novo said that his son had died (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

Rangers legend Nacho Novo has said he is "absolutely broken" after the death of his "beautiful son".

‌



The former footballer, who is currently the manager of Darvel, wrote on Instagram that nothing "could have prepared him" for his son's death and payed tribute saying he will forever be in "our hearts".

‌



Heartfelt tributes have started pouring in from fellow sportspeople and fans across the world after the devastating news which he confirmed with pictures alongside his stepson Ross.

‌



The 47-year-old wrote: "Nothing in my life could’ve prepared me for this post. We are absolutely broken to share the sad news that our beautiful boy has tragically passed away. Please respect our families privacy during this extremely difficult time. Forever in our hearts my boy".

View 3 Images Novo said he was "absolutely broken" (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

UK weather maps turn volcanic red for next 29C heatwave with 7 regions above 27C READ MORE :

Supreme Court rejects President Donald Trump’s mail ballot restrictions ahead of midterm elections READ MORE :

A Rangers FC comment said: "The thoughts of everyone at Rangers are with you at this sad time Nacho."

‌



Sports broadcaster Laura Woods wrote: "I'm so sorry for your loss Nacho, rest in peace your beautiful boy". While wrestling star Grado commented: "So sorry to hear this Nacho - absolutely heart breaking. My thoughts are with you and your family."

Gers fan page Rangers Til' I Die shared on Facebook : "Our thoughts are with Nacho Novo and his family following the heartbreaking news of the passing of his son. During this incredibly difficult time, the entire Rangers family stands behind you and your loved ones. Sending you strength and love."

Oswalds Bar, a Rangers pub in Glasgow city centre, added: "Our thoughts are with you Nacho". Ex-footballer Nazmi Albadawi scribed: "Sorry for your loss brother".

‌



Nacho, who had a heart attack in 2018, said afterwards that he called his then seven-year-old son from the operating theatre as cardiologists raced to keep him alive.

View 3 Images Novo said his son will forever be in "our hearts" (Image: nnovo10/Instagram)

He was rushed to a Berlin hospital where he underwent emergency surgery following a friendly match with Ibrox legends there. He suffered a stroke just weeks later, leaving him paralysed and unable to speak for two days. He later referred to his son as "my rock, my everything".

‌



Nacho was appointed Darvel FC manager in November last year after a stint coaching at West of Scotland Premier side Drumchapel.

The club said they were 'delighted' to appoint the former Ibrox striker who netted 47 times across 179 appearances for the light blues. In a statement last year on X: "Darvel FC are delighted to announce the appointment of Nacho Novo as the club’s new first team manager.

"Nacho brings a wealth of experience and a passion for developing talented players, and we look forward to working together as we continue to build for the future. Welcome to Darvel FC, Nacho!"

Sports.title: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out

Liverpool underwhelmed at the weekend as they were held to a goalless draw by Fulham with Andoni Iraola demanding considerably more come Tuesday night against Tottenham

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was not overly impressed with Liverpool's display at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Liverpool should be "aiming for higher performance levels" after their lacklustre draw with Fulham at the weekend.

‌



The Reds were held to a goalless draw by the Cottagers at Anfield, Fulham's first point of the season, as they struggled to find a way through the west Londoners.

‌



It means that Liverpool are already six points off the pace set by Arsenal and Manchester City and without a win across their two Premier League games at Anfield this season. Iraola is still very much trying to get his ideas across with his tenure still in its infancy.

‌



Their Carabao Cup clash with Tottenham presents the chance for improvement, but is also their fourth game in 11 games. Iraola refused to see that as any type of excuse, insisting that will happen regularly given the amount of competitions their in, and wants to see forward strides made on Saturday's stalemate.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said in his programme notes: "There is no point making excuses or complaining about the time that we have to recover. This kind of situation is going to happen many times this season, so we have to face it and make the best of it.

"This doesn't necessarily mean I expect us to be at our very best in every single game that we play, but we should certainly be aiming for higher performance levels than we were able to reach at the weekend and we should also be finding ways to win.

"I say this because we want to be playing in the Champions League for as long as we can this season and we also want to be in the cup competitions for as long as we can."

‌



View 2 Images The Reds couldn't find a way past Fulham at Anfield

The former Bournemouth has also hinted as changes, such is the relentlessness of the fixture list. "We have a number of players who deserve more minutes than I have been able to give them up to this point so that will come into my thinking, particularly as we also have players who have already given a lot," he said.

Liverpool's win in Europe over Atletico Madrid last week was their best result of the season so far, coming back from a goal down to beat the Spanish side. Iraola talked up the impact Anfield can have when they host Tottenham on Tuesday night.

Article continues below

The north Londoners have underwhelmed this season, failing to score in their four league outings. Their only success came in the Carabao Cup, where they beat Charlton.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick handed shock Man Utd sack warning and given departure timeline
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick handed shock Man Utd sack warning and given departure timeline

Manchester United have one win from their opening four, and there has been a suggestion that pressure is already building on Michael Carrick after the latest phase of the club's rebuild

View 2 Images A sack claim surrounding Michael Carrick has emerged. (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has claimed Michael Carrick might not survive to January after a difficult start. Butt has argued that the Red Devils boss, who was only given the permanent job in the summer, doesn't have a good enough defence to compete - and that could be his downfall.

‌



Manchester City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford was a second defeat of the season for the former United midfielder after their opening day disappointment at Hull City. United reinforced their midfield during the summer with Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba adding options in the engine room.

‌



Butt has argued that a difference in opinion regarding the squad could be one of the factors behind the end of the 45-year-old's first Premier League role, with question marks over defence, midfield and attack.

‌



Wembley SNUBBED for Champions League final as iconic venue ends 30-year wait READ MORE :

OPINION Daniel Farke and Leeds leading charge of clubs who can upset Premier League old guard by Andy Dunn

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, Butt made clear that he felt Carrick had been left short with the summer recruitment. He said: “I think that's all well and good, saying they're doing it in sections from the club and the recruitment, but if you're a manager, you're thinking, well, the forwards, they think they're sorted, I don't think they are.

"I think they need a number 9, an out-and-out number 9. They've gone and sorted the midfielders out, which is debatable.

‌



“I think they've done a decent job with that, but it could be that Michael could not even get to the next transfer window, and he could be going, 'well, I've lost my job and you're not giving me the tools to go and do my job with the back four'.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“Because certainly whatever you say about that back four, Harry Maguire's been an unbelievable player, top, top player, but he's getting to a certain age now, and he is getting older, and we've all been there, haven't we? You get older and you slow down, or you're not as good, not as quick.

‌



“Martinez is still at the top of his game, he's still a really good player. I love Luke Shaw. When he's fit and playing, he's one of the best in Europe, but it's a fact that he gets a lot of injuries.

“The right-backs, I don't believe either of them are good enough. So you're looking as a manager or as a coach, and you're going, ‘well, I'm desperate to get some players in the back four '.

"But then it looks like the recruitment team and the powers that be at United are going, ‘no, that's our next phase, and that might happen in January, it might even happen, and it's gonna be really hard, or it'll probably be happening in the summer.’ That doesn't help the coaches.”

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United have made a disastrous start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick finds his defensive options depleted with no additions to their backline, leaving the same structure that he had to transform after Ruben Amorim's dismissal.

Luke Shaw was forced to miss Sunday's derby defeat with Patrick Dorgu deputising at the back, while Diogo Dalot was handed his 250th appearance for United.

‌



Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez maintained their place as starting defenders, but among the options off the bench were Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui.

It leaves a dangerous and worrying prospect of options in the event of an injury or suspension to the English or Argentine stoppers, with United facing a hectic schedule due to their participation in the Champions League this season.

Article continues below

Carrick, whose United side are back in action against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night, urged his players to forget the derby day disappointment following their controversial loss to 10-man City.

"We've got two games coming up this week, and it's part of it, moving on quickly," Carrick said.

"We haven't got as many points as we would have liked at this point, for sure. There's no getting away from that. But we don't need [the international] break or a restart. We've just got to move on and get winning again."

Sports.title: UEFA meeting news: Champions League final venues announced as Wembley snubbed
Sports.content:
The Champions League final venues for 2028 and 2029 have been decided

An important meeting to determine the hosts of 2028 and 2029 Champions League final will be taking place in Thessaloniki, Greece, today

Wembley Stadium has been snubbed as a host venue for the 2028 or 2029 Champions League final. UEFA bosses and stakeholders gathered today in Greece to decide if the most glamorous match in club football was heading back to London.

Three Champions League finals have taken place beneath the Wembley arch, the 2011, 2013 and 2024 contests won by Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Real Madrid respectively. But the national stadium was one of many venues hoping to host the 2028 or 2029 showpiece event.

The UEFA Executive Committee gathered in Thessaloniki to discuss the host venue, as well as other important matters in European and world football. However, they decided to snub Wembley. Mirror Football has all the updates from the meeting.

Sports.title: Wembley SNUBBED for Champions League final as iconic venue ends 30-year wait
Sports.content:
Wembley SNUBBED for Champions League final as iconic venue ends 30-year wait

UEFA have handed the 2029 Champions League final to the Nou Camp, overlooking Wembley in the process, as Barcelona's iconic stadium ends a 30-year wait for the event

View 2 Images Wembley had eyed its fourth Champions League final, but has been overlooked

Wembley has missed out on hosting the Champions League final in 2029 with the Nou Camp instead getting the nod for the first time in 30 years.

‌



Wembley, since it was re-opened in 2007, has hosted the European Cup final on three occasions, most recently in 2024. It was seeking to land the marquee event once more but has missed out with Barcelona's revamped stadium picked for the final in three years time.

‌



The Nou Camp is the midst of a facelift and that has seen it picked by UEFA's Executive Committee to host the final, seeing off competition from Wembley and Borussia Dortmund's Westfalenstadion, which has never hosted the event.

‌



Heading back to Barcelona's iconic stadium will evoke memories of the historic 1999 final, which Manchester United won with two goals in the final two minutes against Bayern Munich en route to winning the treble.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The Nou Camp was also the scene of the European Cup final in 1989, won by AC Milan. Barcelona president Joan Laporta said on the decision: "This is an immense source of pride for FC Barcelona and for all Barça supporters.

"This decision is also international recognition for the new Spotify Camp Nou, which is establishing itself as a world-class stadium at the forefront of fan experience, technology, connectivity, accessibility, and services."

Wembley has played a central role in European competitions across the past two decades. As well as the three Champions League finals is also held the final and semi-finals of Euro 2020, which was delayed by 12 months due to the pandemic. It will be the central point of the Euros in 2028, which will be played across the UK.

‌



View 2 Images The Nou Camp will host the 2029 Champions League final

The other final awarded by UEFA's Executive Committee on Thursday was the 2028 edition, which will head to the Allianz Arena. Bayern Munich's stadium held the final only last year, when PSG hammered Inter Milan, but has been given the right to host it for a third time in 16 years.

It means that, since Wembley was re-open, only the London venue and Bayern's Allianz Arena have played host to three Champions League finals.

Article continues below

This season's showpiece event will be held at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. It will be the venues second final having been the scene of Liverpool's triumph over Tottenham in 2019.

Sports.title: Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland which led to Enzo error
Sports.content:
Pro Ref chief Howard Webb says VAR missed Enzo Fernandez being offside for Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby due to "tunnel vision".

Webb says he is "really disappointed" by the decision to award the goal, which was initially ruled out on the field due to Haaland being flagged offside.

VAR then checked the incident and determined the striker was onside but failed to account for Enzo Fernandez impacting play from an offside position.

Fernandez dived for the ball before it was steered home by Haaland, and despite severely hindering Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens, Fernandez's offside position was overlooked once the VAR officials had confirmed he had not touched the ball - even though a player can be offside without touching the ball.

Webb told Mic'd Up: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

"The VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he is onside but when he runs it through the full APP (attacking possession phase), he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez.

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision but it is down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel but unfortunately, that did not happen on this occasion.

"This goal should have been disallowed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was VAR confusion as Erling Haaland fired Man City ahead!

Match officials in Manchester derby Referee: Michael Oliver

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

Assistant referees: Stuart Burt and Tim Wood

What the officials said...

Assistant VAR: Enzo, Enzo.

VAR: Possible offside.

Assistant VAR: I'm going to go offside, Haaland.

Referee: On-field decision is offside.

VAR: Checking the on-field decision of offside against Haaland. He's tight. He's onside, so now we need to check the full attacking possession phase (APP).

Haaland's in an onside position, but I need to check the full APP. Go back to see if [Iliman] Ndiaye is onside when it is flicked. Yes. Go, go, go, so it should be a goal.

No touch there [from Enzo Fernandez], confirm no touch. Clear gap. It's not a touch there is it? Goal.

Michael, confirming that you need to change your decision to goal. Haaland is in an onside position. Final decision is goal; check complete.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville slams VAR's decision to give Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby

Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland and missed Enzo offside

Pro Ref chief operating officer Howard Webb:

"We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in the situation. We know that Erling Haaland was penalised for offside and wasn't in an offside position.

"We also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper.

"I was really disappointed with this outcome; we all were. None more than the officials. They take personal pride in what they do and they are hurting now after falling short in this situation. They will not be officiating until after the international break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick, Lisandro Martinez and Erling Haaland react to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United

"We have reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen and they do not happen often. We want to ensure we are transparent and open.

"We have played the audio and footage to the club to let them know what happened. We will review the situation to understand what elements of the process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome.

"Fernandez doesn't actually touch the ball, so he has not committed what we would call a factual offside offence of interfering with play.

Image: Offside law graphic shown during coverage of Manchester United's match against Man City

"But you can still be penalised even if you do not touch the ball. In this situation, as the ball comes across, we see Fernandez dive towards the ball and he gets close to it.

"That impacts [Lisandro] Martinez; he cannot come and clear the ball. It probably impacts [Senne] Lammens as well, he cannot dive in the way he would or sets himself for potential contact from Fernandez.

"It is impacting the defence in a couple of ways as a result of the actions he makes in the offside position."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher and former Coventry striker Jay Bothroyd dissect the biggest talking point of the weekend and ask how VAR got Erling Haaland's winner for Manchester City against rivals United so wrong

Analysis: If VAR can't get the easy ones right, why are we using it at all?

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

Pro Ref should not get a pardon for simply admitting their mistake on this one. A full-scale review into how is what they owe the players and clubs involved given it determined the outcome of the game.

"VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Enzo Fernandez didn't play the ball," is what the Premier League's match centre posted on X in real time. The offside rule appears to have been forgotten here, or at least the full extent of it.

VAR do confirm "no touch" by Fernandez, but fail to recognise he is live in the move. That element is not subjective. The Man City midfielder clearly impacts both Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens and yet neither are mentioned.

Nor does Michael Oliver question it. Does he communicate with the linesman to determine who was actually flagged offside? Was it Fernandez, Haaland or both?

A chronological check of the incident with the correct laws applied would have simply finished with Fernandez. Instead, the video officials spent nearly three minutes presiding over a goal that most casual observers could determine should not have stood with just one replay.

There are no excuses for such a catastrophic failing, but it's probably worth labouring the point that, if forensic technology cannot stamp out even the most basic of officiating mistakes, should we be using it at all?

'No one is hurting more than VAR officials - they're human'

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"I do have an element of sympathy for the VAR and his assistant - they made a mistake. A lot of football fans, particularly Man Utd supporters, will feel it is an unforgivable mistake.

"If you are a VAR and officiating a game as big as the Manchester derby, you really should not be making mistakes of this magnitude.

"But having said that, human beings are human beings. No one is hurting more than the VAR and his assistant. I imagine they've had sleepless nights over this and are replaying what happened over and over again for weeks and months to come.

"Human beings make mistakes and on this occasion, two human beings made a really big mistake which I'm sure they're going to regret for a long time."

Sports.title: Webb: Foden red justified but Fernandes escaped yellow for 'petulant' kick
Sports.content:
Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send off Phil Foden in the Manchester derby but revealed VAR could not intervene to caution Bruno Fernandes for the "petulant" kick that sparked the altercation.

Foden was sent off for violent conduct in Man City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford after kicking out at Fernandes after he was fouled by the Man Utd captain.

Fernandes escaped punishment after seemingly initiating the incident with a kick on Foden before the City forward reacted.

However, there appeared to be confusion during the VAR review of the incident as the officiating team checked for a possible Man Utd penalty after Enzo Fernandez's challenge on Youri Tielemans.

While referee Michael Oliver was brandishing the red card for Foden, VAR official Matt Donohue can be heard discussing the penalty while also saying: "Who has been sent off and for what?" shortly after.

Donohue is then alerted by his assistants to analyse Fernandes' kick on Foden, which initiated the melee between the two players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phil Foden was sent off after a clash with Bruno Fernandes!

The confusing VAR process surrounding Foden's red card

Referee: No, no. The ball, in my opinion, is played by Enzo Fernandez. Feet are side by side.

VAR: Checking possible penalty. One more angle to prove he's definitely played the ball. It looks like he's played the ball.

Phil Foden then kicks out at Bruno Fernandes after being caught by the Man Utd captain and is sent off shortly after.

So, who has been sent off here and for what?

Assistant VAR: It was for a kick-out. It looks like he's given a foul and then the legs came up.

Referee: Red card, Phil Foden. Kick out into the body of Bruno [Fernandes]. The foul is by Bruno on Phil. I think he's in a tangle and when they are separating, I think Phil kicks him. But they will check.
