View image in fullscreen Promise David scored Canada’s goal against Switzerland at the 2026 World Cup. Photograph: Sarah Stier/FIFA/Getty Images

From Estonia to the World Cup

David parlayed his scoring burst with Valletta into a two-year deal with fellow Maltese club Sirens FC. He left after seven months, six goalless appearances, and just 135 minutes in total before moving to Estonia. He arrived at Nomme Kalju with “some things to work on”, Koppel says. David could outmuscle most defenders, but his defensive effort lapsed. Koppel played him with the reserves, a team of mostly high‑schoolers. “It was like he got pissed off,” Koppel says, “and decided to make his mark.”

David scored 22 goals in 19 matches with the reserves, then added seven more with the first team. He wrote “2026” on his locker and went on a scoring tear that has not ended. In 2024, he notched 14 goals and three assists in just 16 appearances. It earned him a move to Belgium’s Royale Union Saint-Gilloise, where he earned the nickname “Baby Lukaku” for his head-turning finishes. He scored two against Gent to earn Union their first Belgian Pro League title since 1935. He scored at PSV Eindhoven on his Champions League debut. He scored again at Galatasaray, ending a 33-match home unbeaten run for the reigning Turkish champions. He scored with defenders tearing off his shirt.

David’s nose for goal – and his off-the-cuff interviews – made him a fast favorite among Union supporters. In recent years, that same joie de vivre has turned him into one of the emerging faces of Canada’s national team. “It’s his personality that gets you,” Feliciano says. “He’s funny, he’s goofy, he’s always in a good mood.”

David earned his first call-up from Jesse Marsch in 2025. He scored against Ukraine on his debut for Canada and managed to earn a World Cup roster spot despite rupturing a hip tendon months before the tournament.

There, he dispelled any lingering doubts about his abilities. In their opener against Bosnia and Herzegovina, he assisted Cyle Larin on Canada’s lone goal 17 minutes after coming on for Jonathan David. Two matches later against Switzerland, he scored with his first touch of the match, an outside-of-the-boot volley that sent Vancouver’s BC Place into ecstasy. David had achieved one part of his goal. The other was soon to come.

New league, new expectations

Now, David faces his biggest challenge: can he keep scoring goals while playing at the likes of Anfield instead of Anderlecht?

In announcing David’s signing on loan from Union for this season, Brighton’s sporting director, Mike Cave, called the 25-year-old an “out-and-out striker” and a player the club had “been watching for some time”. Brighton hope David’s scoring touch will help fill the void left by Danny Welbeck, who departed for Chelsea in August.

David made his Premier League debut against Welbeck’s Chelsea on 30 August, playing 10 minutes in a 4-3 defeat at Stamford Bridge. He had another short stint off the bench against Leeds in a 1-1 draw. A first start, and a first goal, await. So, too, does the spotlight of the sport’s most demanding league, which forgives little and asks plenty.

Feliciano, for one, believes his former charge is up to the task. “He’s only ever had to endure adversity. He’s never had it easy.”

Sports.title: De Zerbi backs ‘sensitive guy’ Solanke to find form before tricky Anfield trip
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has no doubt Dominic Solanke will rediscover his best levels as the head coach made clear he had left no stone unturned in the mission to solve Tottenham’s goalscoring problem.

Spurs go to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after the 0-0 home draw with Everton in the Premier League on Saturday; they have not found the net in their four matches in the competition. Tottenham did beat Charlton 5-1 at home in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Solanke is the only forward in De Zerbi’s squad to have enjoyed a prolific season in England’s top division; he scored 19 times for Bournemouth in 2023-24, which convinced Tottenham to pay £55m for him. The 29-year-old has 22 additional goals in the Premier League, 12 of them for Spurs. De Zerbi has Omar Marmoush, who scored seven times in the league for Manchester City in the second half of 2024-25 after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt in January. That apart, the pickings for De Zerbi’s attacking players have been slim in the competition.

Solanke, whose pre-season was undermined by an injury sustained on the club’s tour of New Zealand and Australia, was ineffective against Everton and a target for criticism is some quarters. De Zerbi will keep the faith. He remembers being amazed at how well Solanke played for Bournemouth against his Brighton team in September 2023. Brighton won 3-1 but Solanke scored. De Zerbi knows that when Solanke is fully fit the goals and performances will follow. He intends to involve the former Liverpool striker at Anfield, whether from the start or as a substitute.

“Dom is a sensitive guy,” De Zerbi said. “He needs to feel full confidence – and from myself, he has big, big confidence. I believe he can score 10-15 goals, for sure. He’s already scored in Bournemouth so why not he can score in Tottenham? It’s the same sport.

“[He is] sensitive because he’s a smart guy. Sensitive guys are smart. Maybe [he has had] many injuries, maybe he doesn’t feel in the best physical condition, maybe he would like to do something different on the pitch. But now he’s not fit yet. He has to play. It can be important for him [at Anfield]. And then I think he comes back to the player who was in Bournemouth. I remember Brighton v Bournemouth in the Amex Stadium; he was incredible. I said to my assistant: ‘Who is this striker?’”

View image in fullscreen Dominic Solanke scores Tottenham’s second goal in their 5-1 Carabao Cup second round victory over Charlton. Photograph: John Walton/PA

De Zerbi continues to try to bond his players away from the pitch. He said he had again taken them for dinner in Mayfair last week and paid the bill. “As long as I keep some money for my cigarettes, then no problem,” he said with a smile.

De Zerbi is leaning heavily into video analysis, going through clips from matches in team meetings and giving the players individual ones to study. There has been an emphasis in training on attacking crosses in the right way and regaining possession in the final third. The players have also stayed behind for extra shooting practice of their own volition, De Zerbi said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If we want to change from the last two or three seasons we have to be stronger here,” he said, pointing to his head. “We have to believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. Or we change. You can change players or change coaches … change, change, change and nothing changes. Or you stay with the head, stay humble and with the right spirit to work. I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.”

De Zerbi reported that Sandro Tonali would miss the Liverpool game with a knock, and Richarlison will not be involved despite being eligible for the Carabao Cup; the Brazilian forward was omitted from Spurs’ Premier League squad.

Pedro Porro is still out but Destiny Udogie is back, and Mohammed Kudus is ready to start. James Maddison, though, will remain among the substitutes. De Zerbi will make changes and he mentioned Marcos Senesi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Ben Davies, Lucas Bergvall and Mathys Tel as being in contention to come into the XI. Spurs have not won at Anfield in 17 matches.

Sports.title: Moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with balloons and canisters in his £270,000 Lamborghini as he pleads GUILTY to dangerous driving and drug possession after crash while on 'hippy crack'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Raheem Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with laughing gas after submitting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90-minutes of dangerous driving in his Lamborghini while high on the chemical.

Sterling, 31, zigzagged across the M25 and M3 motorways in his powerful black car, forcing other motorists to get out of his way, before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

He was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his car.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment that Sterling is arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap. An officer can be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He can then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Sterling is asked 'can you jump out for me' and who was at the wheel at the time of the crash, but does not reply.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap

Sterling was pictured arriving in court on Tuesday to face charges following a car crash in May

The former Premier League footballer, 31, crashed his £270,000 Lamborghini and was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas

The officer adds: 'So you refuse to answer, okay.'

Sterling is told to get out of the car, asked his name and age at the roadside and to 'put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.'

The ex-England winger, 31, is then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange in Hampshire, happened four weeks after the former England international had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

The court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting. Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white ballon to his mouth and inhaling its contents. For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

It was after Sterling had left the M3 near Farnborough, Hampshire, hit the gate and come to halt with the tyres of his wheels ripped up, that police found him sitting in T-shirt and shirts in the passenger seat of the car.

One officer told him to 'stop tensing up' after he had stepped out of the car. Sterling replied: 'I'm not tensing up.' Sterling provided breath tests, which established he was not under the influence of cannabis, cocaine or alcohol. But he later refused requests for a blood test, insisting that a lawyer of his choosing must be present, having rejected the offer of a duty solicitor. He also refused to answer any police questions.

Mr Jones said of Sterling's conduct: 'He was attempting to impose a condition on provision of a specimen. He was told the investigation could not be delayed for that reason. At the roadside, there was cooperation without the need for legal advice. When the search for the presence of drugs started, the cooperation ended.'

Sterling's barrister, Jason Bartfeld QC, told the court that there was 'extensive personal mitigation, in Sterling's case and that the former Manchester City player had taken 'voluntary steps to mitigate his difficulties.'

Mr Bartfeld agreed that this was a 'top category case' because it was a prolonged period of dangerous driving and Sterling was suffering 'serious impairment.' But he said the nitrous oxide would only have caused impairment in 'short periods' and that the chemical did not pose the same risks as cannabis or alcohol.

He claimed police had left Sterling confused about the blood sample. Sterling later told police in a statement: 'I asked for a solicitor. I did not fully understand I had not slept all night and was tired and confused.'

Sterling could face a maximum two years' imprisonment. The case was adjourned until November for pre-sentencing reports.

Sports.title: 'He went into oblivion mode': Inside Raheem Sterling's terrifying fall from grace as he admits dangerous driving - the controversy he never recovered from, his 'huge mistake' in joining Chelsea and why friends fear he is 'completely lost'
Sports.content:
'He went into oblivion mode': Inside Raheem Sterling's terrifying fall from grace as he admits dangerous driving - the controversy he never recovered from, his 'huge mistake' in joining Chelsea and why friends fear he is 'completely lost'

The look of bleak resignation on Raheem Sterling’s face said everything as he walked through the little court building here in Basingstoke, just before stepping into the dock to answer for 90 minutes of terrifying driving.

It was the cold, bleak solemnity of a 31-year-old who was about to admit driving dangerously while in possession of nitrous oxide and who has truly reached rock bottom.

The police video of his arrest, played to magistrate Kirsty Allman, showed the same apparent fatalism. As officers approach him on that brilliant May morning, he sits motionless in the passenger seat of his sports car in T-shirt and shorts.

‘I have a problem with nitrous oxide,’ he would later tell police. Evidence suggests he had been inhaling the chemical seven hours before multiple motorists, stunned by his vehicle careering across lanes in the rush-hour, see its driver sucking on laughing gas balloons.

When he reached Basingstoke police station, Sterling was disorientated, cold and exhausted by what evidence suggests was a solitary all-nighter. He could barely keep his eyes open.

The wall of silence that some of those closest to him encountered when contacting him in the hours after that arrest pointed to him seeking escape from any vestige of the game which is all he has known; turning his face to the wall and wanting no reminder of football. For days, he flatly refused to respond to some who have kept him going in his bleak past few years. ‘He went into oblivion mode,’ says one friend.

Raheem Sterling arrives at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court, where he admitted to dangerous driving in his Lamborghini Urus

‘I have a problem with nitrous oxide,’ Sterling would later tell police in the wake of his arrest in May of this year

The sport’s capacity to build players up and spit them out cannot mitigate for the 31-year-old’s terrifying pattern of behaviour at the wheel of his black Lamborghini Urus V8 on that brilliant spring morning. Zig-zagging across all three lanes. Forcing motorists to get out of his way. It was a miracle that no other motorist was injured or killed.

Yet his descent to this chaos has been frighteningly steep and provides significant context. Few beyond Sterling’s own family were privy to his thoughts in the hours before he trashed his reputation, but sources point to the madness occurring just four weeks after his attempt to relaunch his career at Feyenoord had ended ignominiously.

His criminal conduct was not the result of a wild night out. The worst of it occurred in the cold light of a Thursday morning.

He had rejected the financial security of a three-year deal which the Rotterdam club offered him, signing up to only 12 months instead, because he feared being marooned without game-time as he had in his wretched last years at Chelsea.

‘Everyone who knows him knows that needs to feel part of a club,’ says one source. But that detail somehow didn’t cohere to an obstinate narrative about Sterling and money which has seen many take immense delight in his latest football failure.

Sterling had not played for nine months preceding his first Feyenoord game, in February, yet his poor first 30-minute run out from the bench became a European-wide sensation. ‘He thought he could escape the scrutiny over there and start again,’ says one source. ‘There was no escape.’

The Sterling who returned from Holland was, one source says, at ‘an all-time low psychologically,’ feeling a sense of ‘worthlessness’, having descended from the ranks of England's best players to a reject in the course of four years. ‘He is lost. Completely lost,’ says the source.

A few days ago he posted a photo on Instagram wearing a dark balaclava obscuring part of his face. 'You're too old for this,' read one of the most-liked comments.

Sterling (pictured alongside his partner Paige Milian) posted a photo of himself sporting a black balaclava last week

The 31-year-old has privately admitted his 2022 move to Chelsea was a 'huge mistake'

The public ridicule has evidently been fundamental to his sense of despair. In most walks of professional life, there would be a wish to relent, though that does not seem to apply to young footballers. Sterling has sought help to cope with the psychological impact of his decline but this kind of onslaught is not normal.

The collective delight in his struggles has its roots in the actions of the agent Sterling chose right back in his Liverpool days - Aidy Ward, who conducted ugly, public contract negotiations for his client.

Ward, who said he ‘didn’t care’ about Liverpool and branded Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher ‘a k**b,’ declared that Sterling wouldn’t be staying at Anfield even if he were offered nearly £1million a week.

It was a scarring look for a teenage player, who has never recovered from it. He took the heaviest criticism when England were eliminated from Euro 2016 by Iceland a year later. At that stage, he had yet to surround himself with the wise influences who might have prevented his hangers-on from posting video of his lavishly furnished home, soon after the Iceland defeat. He was castigated for that.

Sterling dispensed with Ward and grew up at Manchester City, who brought out the best from him. With stronger, wiser influences around, he spoke out against the racial abuse England encountered in Montenegro in 2019 and found the voice to argue against football resuming before it was safe in 2021.

The headline of a Financial Times profile in 2021 described him as 'The England football star who took on the racists.' How distant that all seems now.

When Pep Guardiola and City director of football Txiki Begiristain candidly told Sterling his game time would be limited if he extended his contract and stay for what would be City’s Treble-winning season in 2022-23, he took a career-ending decision which will haunt him for all his days.

New Chelsea owner Todd Boehly was giddy about signing him and desperate to sell him the long-term vision with the offer of £325,000 a week. Thomas Tuchel, always a big fan of Sterling’s, was also part of the appeal for Sterling.

The collective delight in Sterling's struggles has its roots in the actions of the agent he chose right back in his Liverpool days - Aidy Ward, pictured, who conducted ugly, public contract negotiations for his client

Sterling was dumped into the 'bomb squad' at Chelsea by then boss Enzo Maresca

But then BlueCo’s big football experiment at The Bridge played out and he was binned. Graham Potter played him at wing back before Enzo Maresca arrived to do Behdad Eghbali’s dirty work, ditching him two days before the 2024-25 season because the American co-owner didn’t share Boehly’s enthusiasm.

One minute Chelsea's website was proclaiming him ‘a positive influence and setting standards.’ The next, it was expunging all mention of him. One minute, Maresca was proclaiming his ‘importance.’ The next, he was dumping him into the ‘bomb squad.’

Everything unravelled after that. A professional life in the ‘bomb squad’ of unwanted Chelsea players left him training alone at 8pm. By the time he secured a season’s escape to Arsenal, it was quite clear that his power, pace and confidence had gone.

Chelsea have moved on, enjoying better PR under Xabi Alonso but Sterling is the collateral damage. That decision he took to join them weighs heavy on him. ‘It’s the feeling that he made such a huge mistake,’ says the source.

Had money been Sterling's main motivating factor, he would have taken the Saudi Arabia deal which Chelsea cooked up with one of the Gulf state’s clubs, to force him out in 2024. All who know him well say he would play for a fraction of his old salaries if he could just revive what he had.

He’s by no means the only one. The modern pattern of players combusting and their careers going pop prematurely has seen Dele Alli and Kalvin Phillips reduced to the shadows by the age of 30. Aaron Ramsdale is the latest.

In part, it is because they have too many people telling them how wonderful they are and throwing disproportionate sums of money at them.

Sterling's attempt to relaunch his career at Feyenoord ended ignominiously. ‘He thought he could escape the scrutiny over there and start again,’ says one source. ‘There was no escape’

There was the usual morbid fascination with Sterling’s decline here in Basingstoke, on Tuesday.

When he arrived in a chauffeur-driven Mercedes van at midday, members of the public gathered near the photographers to get a view and motorists caused a commotion by slowing in a busy road to rubberneck. Those who didn’t care hammered on their horns. Even at a bland town centre court, there were scenes.

His friends don’t know where he goes from here in a sport which has devoured him and expelled him, and neither, one assumes, does he.

‘He needs to get a foundation and get settled,’ says one friend. ‘He needs to determine whether he loves the game enough to continue within it.’

Sports.title: Howard Webb blames 'tunnel vision' for major VAR blunder that cost Man United in derby clash with City: Refs chief 'really disappointed' as full audio is passed on to Old Trafford bosses
Sports.content:
Howard Webb blames 'tunnel vision' for major VAR blunder that cost Man United in derby clash with City: Refs chief 'really disappointed' as full audio is passed on to Old Trafford bosses

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Refs' boss Howard Webb says that those involved in the Manchester Derby blunder were 'really disappointed' with the 'highly unfortunate' error - and has revealed that a furious United have been provided with the full transcript behind the botched VAR call which cost them the game.

Despite being flagged for offside on the field, City forward Erling Haaland's 60th minute strike was called in for review, with ref Michael Oliver subsequently ordered to overturn the original decision and incorrectly allow what would turn out to be the only goal of the game.

Replays showed that while Haaland was onside, City team-mate Enzo Fernandez - who was clearly interfering with play - was not.

Webb, who previously apologised to United just hours after the final whistle, admitted that Oliver should have been told to review the decision on the screen but, bizarrely, was not thanks to an outbreak of 'tunnel vision' in the review booth.

The decision left United boss Michael Carrick seething, and added to calls for the Premier League to scrap the controversial system.

Speaking for the first time on Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb - who stood down VAR Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus until after the international break - was quick to address the matter.

Enzo Fernandez (right) was incorrectly adjudged to not have been offside for Manchester City's winning goal scored by Erling Haaland during their 1-0 win at rivals Manchester United

Pro Ref's boss Howard Webb has said he is 'really disappointed' with how the error came about

'We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation,' he said. 'We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position. But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.'

Daily Mail Sport previously revealed that Webb, head of Pro Ref, was 'mortified' at what transpired. And he added that he was not the only one.

'I was really disappointed with this outcome,' he told the show, which is broadcast on Sky Sports and TNT Sports.

'We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break.'

Webb added that Pro Ref had held its hands up and shared audio of the blunder with United.

'We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen,' he said.

'They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome.'

When explaining what had happened, Webb seemed to suggest that Donohue and Antrobus had focused only on Haaland, rather than Fernandez, whom he acknowledged was interfering with play despite not touching the ball.

Haaland's (right) goal was given after a VAR review, with it having originally been ruled offside

However, Fernandez was in an offside position and attempted to go for the ball, meaning it should have been disallowed, with Pro Ref later apologising to Man United for the error

'The on-field decision is not against Fernandez, it's against Haaland,' he said.

'You'll hear that clearly on the comms. And when the VAR starts their check, they see through the use of the semi-automated offside technology, that Haaland, when he's played, is actually onside by three centimetres, played on by (United defender Patrick) Dorgu on the far side, and the VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal, Haaland's not offside, as was thought initially.

'But of course, when he then runs it back through the full APP, he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn't touch the ball, but he doesn't truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion.'

Webb, who himself refereed a World Cup Final, admitted a clear error. 'Haaland is onside,' he said, 'and we use the technology, but that's only part of the story and the VAR gets super focused on that particular element and, in that moment, misses the evaluation of Fernandez's position, and this goal should've been disallowed.

'Highly unfortunately, it wasn't, and we'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again.'

Matt Donohue (left) was on VAR for the game alongside his assistant Blake Antrobus (right)

In the first half, City's Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes. The United skipper escaped punishment despite appearing to start the confrontation by kicking his opponent on the backside while he was on the floor.

Webb said he agreed with the red for Foden because he 'kicks out with force into the upper body'. He described Fernandes' kick as 'more petulant than violent'.

'To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements,' Webb added.

'So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence. And the VAR can't step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card.'

Sports.title: Stranded LIV Golfers left in the cold by PGA Tour as commissioner takes robust stance on their lucrative return
Sports.content:
The PGA Tour is not going to lower its drawbridge to the stranded golfers of LIV any time soon.

If the likes of Jon Rahm were hoping for a sweetheart deal in the style of one taken by Brooks Koepka earlier this year, he will have been left disappointed by the robust stance taken by the tour commissioner Brian Rolapp on Tuesday.

Unlike Koepka, who jumped ship in January, Rahm, Cameron Smith and Bryson DeChambeau all rejected the opportunity to return eight months ago and Rolapp has made it clear that will be no repeat of the offer in the wake of LIV filing for bankruptcy.

In outlining the PGA Tour's position, Rolapp said: 'In terms of where we are today, we are not currently contemplating a returning-member program like the one you saw in January. Everyone at the PGA Tour, myself included, has been focused on what is best for the organisation.'

Unless the word 'currently' serves as a precursor to a U-turn, it would seem that any LIV rebels will have a limited choice if they are to find a way back to the sport's prime tour.

Under the PGA Tour's existing rules, that would mean a minimum wait of 12 months since their last LIV start and most likely needing to qualify via the DP World Tour.

American star Bryson DeChambeau is among the LIV Golf stars pondering his next move

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp took a robust stance on defectors coming back to the main tour

Jon Rahm may have to wait a minimum of 12 months and qualify via the DP World Tour

As a member of the European-based circuit, Rahm is expected to take that option, with the understanding that LIV's bankruptcy will allow him to escape the remaining years of his contract on the breakaway league.

He is playing this week at the BMW Championship at Wentworth and indicated on Tuesday that it might be November before there is any clarity on his future.

'Nothing's changed,' he said. 'There's a long legal process they have to go through before a lot of things fall into place. I really can't give you an answer right now.

'Hopefully I'll play good this week, and at the end of the year, whether we play in Abu Dhabi, Dubai or elsewhere, so until this current season is done (in November), I really won't be able to give you an answer.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists his furious Man United stars will use Manchester derby injustice as motivation after dismal start to the season - and gives injury update on Luke Shaw ahead of Carabao Cup clash with Brighton
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insists his furious Man United stars will use Manchester derby injustice as motivation after dismal start to the season - and gives injury update on Luke Shaw ahead of Carabao Cup clash with Brighton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United's players will use their anger over Sunday’s defeat in the Old Trafford derby – and sense of injustice at Erling Haaland’s winning goal – as motivation to overcome a dismal start to the season.

United are still fuming over the decision to allow Haaland’s goal to stand, even though his Manchester City teammate Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position and interfering with play, after referees’ bosses admitted that the VAR officials made a mistake.

Michael Carrick’s side have taken just four points from their opening four Premier League games ahead of Wednesday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Brighton at Old Trafford, and the head coach believes the City controversy will fire up his players to recover from their poor start.

‘It does give you something to use moving forward when something like that happens,’ admitted Carrick.

‘The players have got an edge. I think they’ve shown that to me since I’ve been here. We’ve had setbacks, and they’ve bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results.

‘We’ve got to move on. We’ve still got to look at it for ourselves, and we’ve got to win games. We’ve won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that.

Michael Carrick insists his angry Man United stars will use the Manchester derby as motivation

Manchester City triumphed 1-0 over their rivals on Sunday courtesy of a controversial VAR call

‘I understand it’s a new season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be – I’m not hiding from that. It’s getting that winning feeling, getting the habit. It’s easier said than done, of course, but we’re capable of it.’

First, United are in cup action against Premier League rivals Brighton, who knocked them out of the FA Cup at Old Trafford in the last game before Carrick took over in January.

The United boss may rotate his squad, but admits that he cannot risk another setback by making too many changes after tweaking the line-up against Sabah in the Champions League last week.

‘Obviously, there are decisions that we have to make,’ he added. ‘It’s important for us to win football matches, and it’s important that we manage the squad as well and keep everyone up to speed; keep everyone ready and part of it. But we’re certainly going into Wednesday trying to win the game.’

Carrick is waiting to see if Luke Shaw is available to return at left-back after he was replaced by Patrick Dorgu against Sabah and City, with Amad Diallo and Matthijs De Ligt still working their way back to fitness.

‘He (Shaw) could possibly be fit for Brighton, but it’s not clear-cut,’ said Carrick. ‘It’s a matter of a few days rather than anything else.

‘Pat played fantastically well the other night (against Sabah), and I thought he did a lot of good things (against City). That's why we’ve got the squad, to fill in different things. Injuries aren’t ideal, but we’ve got to deal with them.

‘Amad is not quite close in terms of days, but we’ll see as the week progresses. And Matta’s just working his way back really. Because of how it’s been, I don’t really want to put too much of a timeframe on it.’

Referee body Pro Ref have since admitted they made an error allowing Erling Haaland's winner

Carrick also revealed that Luke Shaw, who was absent for Sunday's derby, is nearing a return

Carlos Baleba has also started training at Carrington after recovering from the ankle injury he sustained before completing a £70million move from Brighton to United in the summer.

Baleba won’t be ready to face his old club, but Carrick said: ‘He’ll be back in and around the group at some point over the next week or so. That means he should be in good shape after the international break.

‘Carlos came here injured and then he’s desperate to get out there and be part of the group and train fully with the boys. He’s a quality player, that’s why we brought him.’

Sports.title: Philippe Coutinho, 34, reunites with Neymar as he signs for Santos six months after dramatically quitting his boyhood club for 'health' reasons
Sports.content:
Philippe Coutinho has signed for Santos and will be reunited with former international team-mate Neymar Jr.

The 34-year-old has joined the Brazilian side for the rest of the season after leaving boyhood club Vasco da Gama back in February.

Coutinho marked the transfer by posing for a picture with Neymar, as the pair recreated an old photograph from their days in the Brazil youth set-up, with a digital camera.

And when speaking for the first time as a Santos player, the former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder confirmed that Neymar had a major part to play in his decision to make the move.

'Neymar certainly played a very important role in my coming here,' Coutinho said on Monday. 'He's a player who needs no introduction, a friend I've had since childhood, and I think he was the first person in football to send me a message when I left Vasco.

'The next day he had already sent me a message, but at that moment I said: "Look Ney, it would be a pleasure to play with you, but I'm not feeling well right now, it's not possible" and it really didn't make sense to me.

Philippe Coutinho has joined Santos for the remainder of the season in the Brazilian league

'Months later he contacted me again, but my answer was the same. Then two weeks ago he sent me another message... Then I stopped, reconsidered... I wanted to go back to playing football and I thought: "Why not?"

'I'm going to a big club, in another city. It would be unfair to me not being able to go back to work and not being able to go back to playing football.

'I wanted to thank the president, Mattos and Ney. I'm happy to accept this challenge.'

Coutinho confirmed his departure from Vasco earlier this year, saying that he is 'mentally exhausted' in an emotional statement on social media.

Coutinho re-joined the Brazilian side on a permanent deal last year, following a short loan spell during his stint at Aston Villa, and seemed likely to extend his stay at the club.

However, after being repeatedly booed by his own fans in his final weeks at the club that, he realised that it was a good time for him 'step back' from playing for a period, which is now over.

In a statement at the time, he said: 'The truth is, I'm very mentally exhausted,' he continued. 'I've always been very reserved, so saying this here isn't easy, but I need to be honest.

'My relationship with Vasco is one of love. And it will continue to be forever. With a heavy heart, I understand that now is the time to take a step back and end this chapter at Vasco.

'I am grateful for everything I experienced here. I will carry Vasco with me forever. In my heart. In my history. In my life. From the bottom of my heart… Thank you for everything.'

The midfielder came through Vasco's youth academy before being scouted by Serie A giants Inter Milan in 2008, returning on loan for a brief spell as a teenager.

He impressed at the San Siro as a youngster ahead of signing for Liverpool in 2013, where he spent another five years before moving to Barcelona in still one of the most expensive transfers of all time.

During his time at Anfield, Coutinho made 152 appearances for the Reds and netted 41 goals.

His sale fee enabled Liverpool to sign a handful of important players under Jurgen Klopp, including Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker.

Sports.title: REVEALED: The club plotting stunning move for JJ Gabriel and the compensation United would receive, the real motivations behind his bombshell request to leave and what Old Trafford insiders will do next - Man United Confidential
Sports.content:
REVEALED: The club plotting stunning move for JJ Gabriel and the compensation United would receive, the real motivations behind his bombshell request to leave and what Old Trafford insiders will do next - Man United Confidential

Real Madrid are plotting a stunning move to land JJ Gabriel with the Spanish giants determined to beat bitter rivals Barcelona to the Manchester United wonderkid’s signature.

United’s hierarchy have been rocked at the breakdown in relations between Gabriel’s family and the club following a bombshell request by the player to leave.

Confidential understands one of the factors behind the move is Gabriel's limited minutes in pre-season – the 15-year-old featured in just one game, coming off the bench against Atletico Madrid – with relatives unhappy that he hasn’t already broken into Michael Carrick’s side this season and made a first-team debut.

It has become a source of real contention although, ironically, Gabriel was set to be included in the squad to face Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night – a move that has now been scrapped.

Respected figures in academy circles have told Confidential that Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are now seen as a major threat to Barcelona’s hopes of signing the youngster, with a number of England’s top clubs aware that it may now come down to a tug-of-war between the two Spanish giants.

Because he owns an Irish passport, Gabriel is eligible to join a team in Europe at the age of 16. English players are only allowed to go abroad at 18 under current rules.

Man United’s hierarchy have been rocked at the breakdown in relations between JJ Gabriel’s family and the club following a bombshell request by the player to leave

Gabriel has been around the United first team at Carrington but his lack of pre-season minutes is understood to be a factor in his desire to depart

That has opened the door for a switch to Spain – long the dream destination for the player and his family.

It would be a huge blow to United, not least because the club would only be due around £300,000 in compensation if he moves abroad, compared to a significantly higher fee if he joins a club in England.

During a tour of Barcelona’s facilities in August 2024, Gabriel was introduced to Lamine Yamal as a sweetener for the visit. Yamal signed a Barcelona shirt and posed for a photo. Bayern Munich have also had scouts at numerous youth games to follow Gabriel’s progress, too.

United have been aware of the threat of Barcelona, and latterly Real Madrid, in poaching their premier talent for some time and took a number of emergency measures.

However, they have no plans to rip up his current contract, which runs until the end of the season, and de-register the player who has started the season in electric form, scoring on his debut for the Under 21s and claiming a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut.

Gabriel, who has been at United since he was 11, was in line to pen a first-year scholarship at 16 and that would have automatically triggered a lucrative professional contract on his 17th birthday.

The cancellation feels like a non-starter on United’s end, but the fine details of his current deal are the least of United’s problems. Losing him to one of the two top clubs in Spain would be a hammer blow for Ineos and their aggressive plans to overhaul United’s academy.

Premier League rules state: ‘During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer).

‘If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request.’

Following Gabriel at close quarters has been fascinating viewing as United have been acutely aware in the past two years that they would need to fight tooth and nail to convince him his long-term future lies in Manchester.

United have been aware of the threat of Barcelona, and latterly Real Madrid, in poaching their premier talent for some time and took a number of emergency measures

They have no plans to rip up his current contract, which runs until the end of the season

As Daily Mail Sport revealed recently, the plan was for him to be included in the matchday squad against Brighton, allowing him to become the club’s youngest-ever player by breaking David Gaskell’s record set in 1956.

That has had to be ripped up in light of his request to leave, and it remains unclear if Gabriel will be available for selection on Friday when the Under 21s host Brentford at Leigh Sports Village. He has not trained either yesterday or today.

Last summer, it was reported that Gabriel and his family looked to have lost faith in the United project and were ready to leave, with Manchester City and Arsenal among the potential landing spots for the youngster. City in particular were at one stage confident they could snag him.

Director of football Jason Wilcox intervened, as did head of negotiations Matt Hargreaves, and they both managed to successfully convince the player there was a route to the first team. Being part of the 2026 pre-season tour was raised then, and United were true to their word this summer.

Carrick’s predecessor, Ruben Amorim, spent countless hours watching footage of Gabriel’s clips on the team plane between destinations during the 2025 tour. Going back even further, the club’s former sporting director Dan Ashworth was a major advocate of fast-tracking Gabriel.

United facilitated a personal introduction with legendary manager Sir Alex Ferguson in December last year and the youngster described it as a ‘great honour’.

In younger age groups, United were also much more relaxed to Gabriel’s schedule, allowing the family to take breaks at various points in the season, including to Spain.

Key figures such as recruitment chief Christopher Vivell also made a conscious effort to make Gabriel feel a focal point for the club’s future.

Gabriel went on all bar one of the trips this pre-season, has received glowing praise from Carrick, who has regularly been to watch him at Leigh Sports Village, and has regularly been in first-team training sessions, leaving a lasting impression on the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Marcus Rashford.

Sources close to the player did not respond to request for comment from Confidential.

Gabriel has received glowing praise from Michael Carrick, who has regularly been to watch him at Leigh Sports Village

No Bruno panic

United bosses are refusing to panic over Bruno Fernandes’ new contract despite concerns that negotiations have reached a stalemate.

United’s captain, who has been nominated for the Ballon d’Or after winning the PFA Player of the Year award, has nine-and-a-half months left on his current £220,000-a-week deal, although the club have the option to extend it by another year.

Insiders have told Confidential that United want Fernandes to stay and are relaxed over the situation given the length of time they have to agree new terms.

While he has been a talismanic figure at Old Trafford since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2020, the Portugal star turned 32 last week and United have been trying to move some of their highest earners off the wage bill.

Last year, they were prepared to accept a bid in excess of £100million from Al-Hilal for Fernandes, who rejected personal terms of around £200m over three years following talks between the Saudi club and his agent Miguel Pinho in Riyadh, and later admitted to feeling ‘hurt’ that United were ready to let him go.

There was fresh speculation in the summer, even though the £56.7m release clause in his contract expired in July, and Galatasaray were understood to be offering to double his wages as well as hand him a £3.5m signing-on fee.

Unless United can offer Fernandes a package to persuade him to stay before the end of the year, he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January, but the club will hope to make a breakthrough in talks before then.

United bosses are refusing to panic over Bruno Fernandes’ new contract despite concerns that negotiations have reached a stalemate

Jarrad back on Reds’ radar

United have renewed an interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite as they prepare to rebuild their defence for next season.

Confidential understands that contact has been made with the 24-year-old's representatives, and United may consider a bid in January or the summer.

The club had two offers of up to £50m for Branthwaite rejected by Everton in 2024, and signed Matthijs de Ligt from Bayern Munich instead.

But De Ligt has been out of action for nearly a year after back surgery, and both Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez will be out of contract next summer – although United have an option to activate a 12-month extension for both players.

With Luke Shaw also set to become a free agent in June, and no indication at the moment that United’s longest-serving player will stay at Old Trafford beyond that, big changes are expected to the back-four after this summer’s midfield rebuild and the new signings made in attack last year.

They may consider offering a player in return for Branthwaite, although it remains to be seen if Everton would be open to letting him leave after banking in excess of £80m for Iliman Ndiaye and Beto this summer.

Contact has been made with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite's representatives, and United may consider a bid in January or the summer

United deny VIP bias

United have strenuously denied suggestions that players have been told not to sign autographs for non-VIP supporters on matchdays.

A video of Noussair Mazraoui being interviewed by TNT Sports as the players arrived for the Sabah game last Thursday went viral after his team-mates were spotted walking to the right of the Moroccan and shaking hands with supporters who purchased VIP packages instead of those standing on the other side of the entrance.

It has led to claims that players have been specifically instructed by club officials to head for the VIP section, but the club have stressed to Confidential that that is wide of the mark.

They say that while hospitality guests have a special viewing area of team arrivals – which was in place last season too – there is no obligation for players to stop for anybody, let alone avoid a certain group of supporters.

Under Carrick, players have a pre-match meeting inside the dressing room, and so the bulk of them don’t stop to sign autographs before the game.

But many do so frequently after matches – with the likes of Diogo Dalot and Bruno Fernandes prominent among them – which is what triggered such an angry response from Under 18s boss Darren Fletcher last week when one fan was directing abuse at him for not granting every single autograph request. Fletcher made it plain that abuse thrown by some supporters dissuades many from stopping at all.

“Three years ago I played against Man United”



Noussair Mazraoui on Manchester United’s return to the Champions League ✨



🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/snfO92uTaY — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) September 10, 2026

No stress over Sesko

Benjamin Sesko has been at the centre of simmering club-versus-country tensions since arriving at Old Trafford in a £74m deal last year, but the Slovenia striker’s national team manager has backed United’s handling of his shin problem – and revealed that it was ‘quite a serious injury’.

Sesko hasn’t played for his country for almost a year since a goalless World Cup qualifier against Switzerland, missing the friendly internationals against Hungary, Montenegro, Cyprus and Croatia.

When the 23-year-old pulled out of the squad in March after United said they had been ‘carefully managing the issue’, Slovenia boss Bostjan Cesar insisted on his medical staff assessing the player in Ljubljana and warned that he would not be pushed around by the club.

However, Cesar has struck a more conciliatory tone after naming Sesko in his squad for the upcoming Nations League games against Scotland, North Macedonia and Switzerland.

‘I’m very happy that he’s back in a competitive rhythm and the injury is finally repaired,’ said Cesar. ‘I have spoken to him and I believe Benjamin Sesko will come to the camp.

‘I’ve been (aware of the) situation with his injury since March. It was quite a serious injury, and I think they handled it altogether in the right way to get him into the training process so slowly.

‘For me as a coach, but also for all of us, for the whole of Slovenia, it is very important that Benjamin is now healthy and that he comes back to the national team after a long time.’

Having recovered from the injury after being given extra time off by United in the summer, Sesko has scored twice in five games and could be in line for a start against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

Benjamin Sesko has scored twice in five games and could be in line for a start against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night

Opportunity knocks for Santos

We’re only a month into the season, but this already feels like a pivotal week for Andrey Santos and his prospects for regular game-time in a United shirt.

United’s £50m summer signing started alongside fellow new arrival Youri Tielemans at Hull City on the opening weekend, but they were exposed by the way United set up and the 2-0 defeat paved the way for Kobbie Mainoo to come into the side at Santos’ expense.

Since playing 67 minutes against Hull, Santos has had a grand total of 16 minutes in the Premier League, and only a further 26 minutes in the win over Sabah, for a total of 42 minutes of action since August 22.

Almost a month on, and with £70m acquisition Carlos Baleba training at Carrington as he prepares for his United debut after the international break, Santos knows that a rare opportunity against Brighton on Wednesday could prove hugely decisive in his bid for regular minutes.

Carrick has shown thus far a preference to play two No 8s together in Mainoo and Tielemans, leaving Santos in reserve.

Brighton at home in the Carabao Cup should give him his opportunity. With Baleba on the comeback trail, it’s paramount Santos takes it.

Since playing 67 minutes against Hull, Andrey Santos has had a grand total of 16 minutes in the Premier League

Fans vow to march on

The protesters who marched against United’s owners before Sunday’s Manchester derby have warned that they will continue to fight back against any ‘bullying’ from the club.

Around 500 fans took part in a demonstration organised by protest group The 1958 outside Old Trafford, while The Red Army took down all the flags and banners in the Stretford End except one that read: ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace.'

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Avram Glazer were there to witness the backlash to United’s recent clampdown on ticket touting, which the protesters claim has targeted innocent fans.

The 1958 are weighing up their next move, and issued a statement telling fans: ‘Whatever this club does to eradicate the time-served match-going Red, you know you have been on the right side of history.

‘We will continue the fight on all fronts. Protecting the culture. Protect the traditions. Protect the match-going fan. Protect what is left for the next generation.

‘We will continue to protest against the way season-ticket holders and match-going Reds have been treated. The club simply can’t get away with this level of bullying again.

‘Our fight has always been for a full sale of the club and a change in owners – this will never change.’

For the Manchester derby, the Red Army took down all the flags and banners in the Stretford End except one that read: ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace'

Noah’s arc

A word on the academy and specifically Noah Ajayi. The 17-year-old, who continues to be closely tracked by teams in his homeland of Germany, has started the season with a bang for United’s Under 18s and Under 19s.

Ajayi was a consideration for the first team’s pre-season tour of Europe, but was sidelined for most of the summer through injury.

Now fit and back in form, the youngster looks a real threat and is set to play a role across the Under 18s, Under 19s and Under 21s as the season progresses.

Those who work closely with Ajayi believe that he is one of the academy’s biggest talents right now. At his current trajectory, he should be involved in first-team training sessions in the coming months – not least because his size and physicality gives him an advantage over other young players.

There are a number of promising youngsters in the pipeline at Carrington right now, and optimism is sky high when it comes to Ajayi.

Those who work closely with Noah Ajayi believe that he is one of the academy’s biggest talents right now

Dalot’s a happy camper

Diogo Dalot made his 250th appearance in the Manchester derby, and after eight years at Old Trafford – including one on loan at AC Milan – the Portugal defender knows how important the Manchester United Foundation is to the club and their supporters.

Dalot recently spent time at one of the foundation’s government-funded holiday camps, taking part in games with young people as part of the holiday activities and food programme.

The foundation puts on three camps during the summer in Salford, Stretford and Partington to make sure children between the ages of eight and 14 stay active out of school time, as well as providing healthy meals and childcare places free of charge.

Speaking at the Partington event, Dalot said: ‘It’s always special to give back to the foundation. It’s great to see the kids enjoying themselves, playing football and having smiles on their faces. Moments like these remind me of being their age and chasing my dream.’

Sports.title: JIMMY MONTGOMERY EXCLUSIVE: Sunderland's FA Cup hero on the hijinks of the Black Cats' last European adventure, having his gloves stolen in Lisbon - and his verdict on Robin Roefs
Sports.content:
In the hall of Jimmy Montgomery’s peaceful house in the Sunderland suburbs is a framed black-and-white photograph of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final for which he will forever be remembered.

It’s a simple picture, an iconic moment beautifully captured.

The players of Sunderland and Leeds are in classic football strips, free of clutter and sponsors' logos. Long hair and black boots. Meanwhile a goalkeeper dives low into history to parry a header wearing a pair of woollen gloves that look like they could have come from a local garden centre.

‘I haven’t got those gloves anymore,’ Montgomery tells the Daily Mail from his seat on the sofa.

‘When we played in Lisbon (against Sporting) in the Cup Winners' Cup the next season, I put them in the back of the net with my cap as I always did. And somebody stole them.

‘Ball boy? Cameraman? I have no idea. So that was one souvenir gone in a flash.

‘Not that it really mattered. I hardly wore them. When they were wet they were about as much use as a chocolate watch!’

Sunderland legend Jimmy Montgomery has fond memories of the club's last European campaign in 1973-74 - apart from having his goalkeeper gloves stolen in Lisbon!

Montgomery has a framed photo of the save in the 1973 FA Cup final against Leeds for which he will forever be remembered

We are here on Wearside to talk, for once, not about that stunning double save that helped second-tier Sunderland win the Cup at Wembley 53 years ago, but about the European campaign that followed.

It was the club’s first foray into Europe and, until today, their last.

As Regis Le Bris’ impressive modern team face AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League tomorrow night, Montgomery will be in the stand that, since the start of last season, carries his name.

‘We played our first tie in Budapest behind the Iron Curtain and it was the exact same XI that had won the cup final,’ recalls Montgomery. ‘I don’t think that was sentiment. I think we deserved it.

‘These days the team will have a dossier on the opponents and take their own chef and staff with them.

‘We had our manager Bob Stokoe, his assistant and maybe the club secretary. That was it.

‘In terms of the opposition (Vasas Budapest) we didn’t know a thing about them apart from what the press men on the plane told us.

‘It took us for ever to get there and even longer to get back. But we won 2-0 and also beat them at home. Marvellous.

‘It ended for us in the next round at Sporting Lisbon. That was a strange night.

‘They had ball-boys throwing the balls on but when they did, the Lisbon players would throw them straight off again, sometimes straight into the crowd.

‘We looked at the ref and he just stared back at us. I guess it was time-wasting. But I have never seen anything like it before or since.’

Sunderland captain Bobby Kerr is held aloft by his team-mates, including Montgomery (fourth from right) after the 1-0 win over Leeds in 1973

Now, at the age of 82, Montgomery is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland

Facing a shot from Newcastle's Jim Scott in the Tyne-Wear derby at Roker Park in 1968

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years. As a boy he would watch his team at Roker Park with his father. As an apprentice, he would later sweep the terraces and paint the seats.

Now, at the age of 82, he is revered to such a degree he literally has his name written throughout the modern Sunderland.

As well as the stand at the Stadium of Light, this year’s goalkeeping jerseys have his signature, number of appearances and even an outline of his famous save embossed in them.

‘It’s hard to believe,' he says. ‘I am just a kid from down the road.’

Montgomery has served Sunderland as player, goalkeeping coach and worked at its centre of excellence.

‘I have actually been let go four times and that was hard,’ he says. ‘Different managers would want different things. So yeah I got kicked out.

‘But I kept getting invited back again!

‘I even had a year coaching at Newcastle with Kevin Keegan and, as hard as it is for Sunderland fans to hear, Pavel Srnicek was perhaps the best I worked with.’

A welcome visitor to Sunderland’s training ground whenever his health allows, Montgomery has talked football with the ever-respectful Le Bris and goalkeeping with current No 1 Robin Roefs.

‘They sometimes bring the goalkeepers over for a chat,’ he explains. ‘I think the young ones want to talk. That’s very humbling and typical of the club now.

Montgomery made a record 627 appearances for his hometown club across 18 years

Montgomery (second left) poses with the Cup alongside (from left) Ian Porterfield, Micky Horswill and Kerr

‘Robin is an excellent keeper, a brilliant keeper. Sometimes I just wish he wouldn't try to play from the back so much. I'm not a great fan of it. I get wound up.

‘It’s a risk. I would much rather goalkeepers get it forward, push the team up, and start from there.

‘I'm a big believer in once the goalkeeper's got the ball, he's in charge of it. He does what he thinks right.

‘If he doesn't want to play it short, he shouldn't have to. Look at the Arsenal goalkeeper on Saturday. He dictated everything. He was fully in charge. I like that.’

If Montgomery was impressed with David Raya, he was less enamoured with Arsenal.

‘I have no time for them,’ he says. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

‘Their manager is complaining like mad about giving the penalty away but if you're going to get mixed up in that, it will go against you eventually.

‘It’s amazing what goes on at corners now. They don’t even look at the ball. We never grappled like that. I just knew that when the ball came over I was gonna get smashed.

‘Wyn Davies of Newcastle and good old Nat Lofthouse. Every time. Bang. There was no protection. You just had to be ready for it.’

At the end of his career, Montgomery spent a season at Nottingham Forest under Brian Clough.

‘I played with Brian and he was brilliant, though he knew it too,’ he smiles. ‘I was playing the day he broke his leg on Boxing Day in 1962. So I was chuffed he thought I was good enough all those years later to be under-study to Shilts (Peter Shilton).

‘I was in my mid-30s and coming towards the end. I never played but was on the bench when Forest won the European Cup in Madrid in 1980. I got a medal.’

Montgomery – who rates the great Pat Jennings as perhaps the best goalkeeper he has known – has a photo of himself with the European Cup and it feels strange to see him in another club’s colours.

‘I have no time for them,’ says Montgomery of Arsenal. ‘Goodness I couldn’t watch that every week. What is that type of football?

But it’s that black-and-white picture of his Wembley save that we return to.

The first effort – the one on the picture – was from Trevor Cherry. The follow-up from five yards from Peter Lorimer was struck so powerfully ITV commentator Brian Moore shouted ‘goal’ before it struck the underside of the bar.

Afterwards, it was the late Jimmy Hill who declared it had been the tips of Montgomery’s fingers that had touched it up on to the woodwork.

Montgomery’s favourite line is to say he wished he had caught the first shot so he wouldn’t have had to spend his life talking about the second.

‘But I don’t mean it,’ he smiles. ‘I love what it still means to people.

‘It was only when standing with my pint of milk afterwards that I realised the significance of it. They just kept showing it.

‘I was lucky it was on TV, mind. I had made one from a lad playing for Hull a few weeks before that was even better…’

Sports.title: Howard Webb points blame for Manchester derby offside controversy as Pro Ref take action
Sports.content:
Refereeing chief Howard Webb has claimed that VAR officials in Stockley Park had 'tunnel vision' before the decision to allow Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the Manchester derby.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have both been stood down for this weekend's Premier League fixtures after wrongly letting Haaland's goal stand.

Initially flagged for offside due to Enzo Fernandez's attempt to play the ball in build-up, the decision was overturned following VAR check. Webb, as head of Pro Ref, wrote to Manchester United officials within hours of full-time to apologise for the error that played a decisive part in their 1-0 defeat to leave Michael Carrick's side on four points after four games.

Haaland's goal wasn't the only moment of drama at Old Trafford either. City star Phil Foden was sent off after kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, a decision which Webb insists was correct.

‌



Appearing on Match Officials Mic'd Up, the former referee admitted: "We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation. We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.

‌



"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen.

"They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome."

Should Phil Foden have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez dived for the ball from an offside position (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Webb added that the officials back in Stockley Park got 'tunnel vision' in focusing on Haaland's part in the goal, with colleagues unable to pull him back out to look at the wider picture.

He added: "And when the VAR starts their check, they see through the use of the semi-automated offside technology, that Haaland, when he's played, is actually onside by three centimetres, played on by [Patrick] Dorgu on the far side, and the VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal, Haaland's not offside, as was thought initially.

"But of course, when he then runs it back through the full APP, he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn't touch the ball, but he doesn't truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion."

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez's role was incorrectly overlooked in the process of allowing the goal, according to Webb

‌



Webb then emphasised: "We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

City took the lead in the derby after they were reduced to 10 men. Tempers flared in the 23rd minute, as Foden reacted to a kick from Fernandes by lashing out himself.

On-field referee Michael Oliver quickly made up his mind and it was the City player who was punished. "I agree with the red card for Phil Foden for violent conduct," Webb concurred. "He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes.

"We saw a player sent off for Aston Villa earlier in the season. [Joao] Gomes was sent off for a very similar thing, kicking with the studs into the body. And that's seen by the referee on the field, and that's the on-field call, a red card for Foden.

‌



"Now, when you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden. It is more petulant than violent.

"To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence. And the VAR can't step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card.

"Of course, if all of this is missed and nothing is given against Foden, then the VAR could step in so the referee could see Foden's actions for a possible red card, and they would capture Fernandes' yellow card action. But because the referee gave the red card on the field, that option is not open to the VAR."

‌

Newsboy's tips for 4 Wednesday meetings including his nap at Sandown Park

Newsboy's Nap selection on Wednesday is the Saffie Osborne-ridden Room Service (3.30) at Sandown. His next best is Yarmouth runner Enoch (4.12)

View 2 Images Newboy's Nap selection for Wednesday, September 16, is Room Service who runs in the 3.30 at Sandown Park (Image: PA)

SAFFIE OSBORNE proved she belongs at the top table with a brilliant win in the St Leger at the weekend.

‌



And she can add to her growing reputation aboard ROOM SERVICE (nap) in the Listed Trainor Stone & Tile Fortune Stakes (3.30) at Sandown Park on Wednesday.

‌



After becoming the first woman to win a British Classic, steering Highwayman to victory in the Doncaster highlight, Osborne was keen to pay tribute to her parents for their support.

‌



Room Service provides an immediate opportunity for more tangible payback given the five-year-old gelding is now trained by her father Jamie.

The gelding was a good servant for Kevin Ryan, winning a valuable £300,000 sales race at Doncaster as a two-year-old, a Listed race at three and being placed at Group Three level last season.

View 2 Images Newboy's Nap selection for Wednesday, September 16, is Room Service who runs in the 3.30 at Sandown Park (Image: PA)

‌



But after starting to lose his focus a little, he was gelded and sent to Osborne for a change of scenery, emerging from a break to win a valuable handicap at Newcastle in June with a tongue tie and first-time blinkers.

This is a first try at a mile but he has been finishing off well over seven furlongs.

First-time blinkers did the trick for EDWIN HUBBLE over course and distance two runs ago and the return to Esher's stiff one mile two furlongs trip in the Trainor Stone & Tile Handicap (4.40) should see him get back in the winning groove.

‌



Brian Meehan's three-year-old was bumped up 3lb for that narrow win and appeared to be anchored by it at Newbury last time but, in a slow-run race, he was caught flat-footed and with ground to make up when the pace quickened before staying on really well for third.

With a stronger pace and a stiffer finish today, he is taken to resume progress.

At Yarmouth, ENOCH (nb) is a confident pick in the Goffs Two Million Series Handicap (4.12).

‌



The Frankel colt who looked a smart prospect when making a winning debut in a 7f Newmarket maiden in September, travelling fluently and quickening up well.

And the charge of John and Thady Gosden did little to alter that view at Lingfield on his reappearance three weeks ago.

There should be plenty more to come.

‌



The Gosdens and Ryan Moore can double up in the Listed EBF Stallions John Musker Fillies' Stakes (3.41) with MORROPHORE .

The five-year-old mare disappointed last time at York finishing down the field behind Prizeland over a mile and a half, a run connections initially put down to the rain-softened ground on the Knavesmire.

On the face of it, a return to soft conditions here at Yarmouth may look puzzling but it suggests another excuse has been found and dropping back in trip back to one mile two furlongs, she is taken to bounce back.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned

Manchester United have received devastating news over the future of teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel after he asked to quit the club immediately

Michael Carrick concerned by Manchester derby goal decision

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel had informed the club that he wants to cancel his registration with them immediately. The 15-year-old prodigy has sent a formal notice of his desire to become a free agent.

‌



The club do not believe the situation is irretrievable and has not yet accepted Gabriel's request. The youngster has played for the club since the age of 11, and United can challenge or reject Gabriel's request to cancel his registration.

‌



Last week, Gabriel wiped all of the images from his Instagram, leading to some concern. The youngster already lays claim to more than 800,000 followers on the social media website.

‌



Gabriel is not able to sign a professional contract until he turns 17, and scholarship agreements are not permitted until players turn 16. He is not currently in line to join another club immediately, despite Manchester City previously trying to tempt him away from Old Trafford.

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Premier League rules require all parties to come to an agreement to end a registration period early. “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer)," they state.

“If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request," the rules add.

Gabriel was part of United's pre-season preparations across the summer and featured against Atletico Madrid. United are said to have planned for the teenager to be part of the squad for Wednesday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Brighton.

‌



The attacker has scored five goals and provided two assists in just three games across Premier League 2 and the UEFA Youth League. At 15, he is already playing amongst his elders on a regular basis.

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel continues to impress at Manchester United and is on the fringes of the first team. (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



United boss Michael Carrick has been impressed by Gabriel's abilities and has frequently attended youth matches to monitor the youngster and other talents. Speaking last month after watching Gabriel, the Carrick said: "I really enjoyed the game. You could see the quality.

"JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we're just continuing his development."

Last term, Gabriel became the youngest winner of United’s Jimmy Murphy young-player-of-the-year award, racking up 23 goals in as many appearances in the under-18 Premier League.

‌



Speaking after Gabriel's immense performance against Sabah this season, under-21s boss Adam Lawrence offered a ringing endorsement of the player's abilities. "Well, I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him," he said.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has previously heaped praise on the teenager (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments.

Article continues below

"Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about.

"But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other teammates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly."

Sports.title: Edu lands surprise new job just days after brutal Nottingham Forest exit
Sports.content:
Edu lands surprise new job just days after brutal Nottingham Forest exit

Former Arsenal technical and sporting director Edu has joined a new club after officially leaving Nottingham Forest last week after 14 months at The City Ground

View 2 Images Edu Gaspar (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

Edu Gaspar has been appointed to the board of directors at Levski Sofia just one week after officially departing Nottingham Forest.

‌



The Brazilian had held the role of head of global football at the Premier League club for around 14 months. He had previously built up an impressive body of work at Arsenal, the same club he enjoyed a successful stint with during his playing career, after initially joining the Gunners as a technical director back in 2019.

‌



Edu was promoted to the role of sporting director in 2022 and his decision to leave Arsenal in November 2024 was an unexpected one given the progress made under the 48-year-old and Mikel Arteta.

‌



But his stint at Forest was less fruitful and he had been absent from games since February before officially leaving the club last week.
