Mrs. Lai’s remarks tied personal history to the day’s cause. She invoked her husband’s own continued academic pursuits — despite already holding two master’s degrees — as evidence that learning doesn’t stop at a diploma.

She also drew on her own background as a former Peace Corps volunteer in Malawi, where she worked on community development and later supported scholarship programs for girls, experience she said convinced her that education reshapes not just individual futures but entire communities.

The Lai family backed that message with a L$200,000 cash contribution to the fund. For residents watching the fund take shape, the appeal was straightforward: a local son, having gone further than his own circumstances once suggested, was funneling resources back into the district that raised him.

Many described the initiative as a meaningful investment in Zota’s children and thanked Dr. Urey-Yarkpawolo and his partners for choosing to give back in this form.

Whether the fund becomes an annual fixture or a one-time gesture remains to be seen — but for the 500-plus students expected to benefit this year, the immediate effect is a lighter financial burden and, organizers hope, one fewer reason to leave school early.

World.title: Strategy, Pressure Or Principle: Nevers Gets Nervous?
World.content:
Former Vice-President Nevers Mumba’s resignation as President of the New Nation Party, and his withdrawal from active politics and the UPND Alliance Council of Presidents, has been received publicly as a personal decision framed around service and calling. Beneath that framing, three competing theories are now circulating over what actually drove the timing, and each points to a different picture of where Mumba sits in Zambia’s political landscape.

Theory one: a strategic exit with a reward attached

One reading holds that Mumba’s departure is less an ending than a repositioning, timed to a role he expects from the UPND in return for services already rendered. Under this theory, Mumba’s presence inside the New Nation Party was never really about building an independent political home. It was about occupying and neutralising a vehicle, the former MMD, that could otherwise have re-emerged as a credible opposition platform.

That reading draws a direct parallel with what happened to the Patriotic Front, where figures inside the party’s own structures were widely seen to have weakened its capacity to function as an effective opposition force following the 2021 transition. Applying the same logic to Mumba, the argument goes that stepping back now, cleanly and publicly, positions him for a reward from the UPND rather than closing the door on his political relevance. Mumba himself gave the theory an opening by describing his move as “a calling to serve the country in a different capacity” rather than a retirement, language critics say leaves the door open for a future government or diplomatic appointment.

Theory two: pressure following a public legal challenge

A second and more immediate theory centres on a direct challenge to Mumba over his conduct, reportedly raised by former ambassador Emmanuel Mwamba in comments shared publicly in the days before the resignation.

According to that account, Mwamba says he cautioned Mumba that he was breaking the Constitution and the Former Presidents’ Benefits Act of 1993, as amended in 2026, by drawing benefits as a former Vice-President while simultaneously holding the partisan position of party president. Mwamba says Mumba dismissed the warning at the time, and that an ally of Mumba’s, George Mtonga, publicly reproduced the dismissive response. Mwamba has since pointed to former President Edgar Lungu as precedent, noting that Lungu voluntarily surrendered his own former-president benefits when he returned to active politics in October 2023.

The Act itself is explicit on the point. Retirement benefits for a former President or Vice-President are withdrawn if the individual is in receipt of a Government salary, is engaged in active politics, vacates office over a constitutional violation or gross misconduct, or is convicted of an offence carrying more than six months’ imprisonment without the option of a fine. Under this theory, Mumba’s resignation was less a redefinition of service than a legally necessary correction, arriving only after the exposure became public and difficult to ignore.

Theory three: principle, and a quieter benefit of its own

The third theory takes Mumba closer to his word, treating the decision as a genuine reflection on what nearly three decades in active politics has done to the office he once held and to the national respect attached to it. Under this account, Mumba’s references to being persistently misunderstood, and to leaning instead on his diplomatic background and religious grounding to offer national guidance, reflect a real discomfort with the tone of Zambian partisan politics rather than a calculated exit.

Even this reading, however, does not fully separate principle from self-interest. Stepping back from active politics restores Mumba’s unambiguous entitlement to his former Vice-President benefits under the Act, regardless of whether reflection or exposure came first. Principle and preservation, in other words, arrive at the same outcome.

What is confirmed, and what is not

What is established is that Mumba has resigned as New Nation Party president, handed interim leadership to vice-president Reuben Sambo pending a party convention, and withdrawn from the UPND Alliance Council of Presidents, and that he consulted President Hakainde Hichilema before making the announcement. What remains unconfirmed is which of the three motivations, if any single one, actually drove the timing. Neither Mumba nor the New Nation Party has directly addressed the benefits question or Mwamba’s account, and no independent confirmation exists of a pending UPND reward.

Sambo now leads a small but strategically positioned UPND alliance partner, with the substantive leadership question left to the next party convention, and the wider question of what comes next for Mumba himself left, for now, unanswered.

World.title: Government launches Digital Learning programme
World.content:
Government in partnership with Ignite Access, have launched a three-year Connectivity and Digital Learning programme, set to benefit 70 schools in the country.

Under the Initiative dubbed “Lynx Zambia Digital Inclusion”, the beneficiary schools will be linked to Starlink satellite internet connectivity, while those off the national electricity grid will be connected to solar power.

Speaking during the launch at Chainda Primary school in Chongwe district, Head of the Presidential Delivery Unit, Kusobile Kamwambi described the programme as a milestone in advancing Zambia’s energy and digital inclusion agenda.

In speech read for her by PDU Delivery Manager for Enhanced Value Chains, Jones Shimbela, Ms Kamwambi noted that the initiative is aimed at directly addressing two national priorities, which are expanding access to reliable electricity and accelerating digital inclusion.

She explained that the government targets to increase electricity access to 66 percent by 2031, while ensuring that 80 percent of the population has access to internet connectivity, with at least 20 percent fully participating in the digital economy by 2031.

Ms Kamwambi stated that these goals form part of the broader Grow Zambia Agenda, which seeks to move the country from stabilisation, to stronger economic growth, increased production, wealth creation and greater citizen participation.

She emphasised that the Lynx Zambia Digital Inclusion programme is therefore not simply about connecting 70 schools to the internet, but about creating opportunities that contribute to Zambia’s future growth.

“That means connectivity can help a small business communicate with customers, allow a farmer or trader to access market information, support young people to explore online work and business opportunities, and enable community members to use services such as mobile money and other digital financial platforms: practical opportunities that can bring more citizens into the digital economy and support the Grow Zambia Agenda”, Ms Kamwambi stressed.

Speaking at the same event, Ministry of Education Permanent Secretary for Administration, Noriana Muneku who was represented by the Ministry’s Director for ICT, Victor Musangu said the support will directly enable the uptake of digital services and improved financial accountability in education institutions.

She explained that the Ministry of Education has been tasked to ensure schools begin using the government-provided financial management solution, noting that without connectivity, directives remain ineffective.

She stressed that with innovation and partner support, the Electronic Government Division, will ensure secure connectivity of terminals to the government-wide area network, thereby realising accountability in schools.

Ms Muneku disclosed that the ministry has already installed equipment in 75 classrooms to transform them into smart classrooms, opening opportunities for teachers to use artificial intelligence for continuous learning.

She emphasised that infrastructure without reliable power and connectivity remains incomplete, underscoring the importance of partner support in achieving the government’s vision.

“This effort is critical. It ensures that accountability systems function, classrooms become truly smart, and the education sector benefits from innovation that supports Zambia’s connectivity, trade, tourism and economic development”, she said.

And Ignite Access Managing Director, Hellen Zulu disclosed that during the first year, the company will provide installation, connectivity, solar systems and data services at no cost to schools.

She added that beyond that, the programme will adopt a sustainable model where schools continue to benefit from free educational access, while surrounding communities gain affordable internet services, at a fee.

“A connected school is no longer a luxury. It is an essential platform for delivering quality education”, Ms Zulu said.

Meanwhile, beneficiaries at Chainda School, in Chongwe have expressed gratitude for the support.

School Head teacher, Stella Lipalile disclosed that over 2600 learners at the school would benefit from the programme, adding that it will also enhance research for staff, while Head girl, Grace Matibenga indicated that the support will improve ICT learning.

World.title: Kabwe court sets marijuana trafficking judgment date
World.content:
The Kabwe Magistrate’s Court has set September 30, 2026 as the date for judgment in a case involving a 39-year-old farmer accused of trafficking in 700 grams of marijuana.

Kabwe Resident Magistrate Sebastian Mwenya set the judgment date after hearing testimonies from both the prosecution and defence teams in the case involving Gerard Sipalo of Shamabanse Compound.

Sipalo is charged with trafficking in psychotropic substances, contrary to Section 6 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, Chapter 96 of the Laws of Zambia, as read with Statutory Instrument Number 119 of 1995.

During the defence hearing, Sipalo called one witness, Perthias Mubanga, who told the court that he was working as a bricklayer at Sipalo’s house on the material day.

The court heard that on June 5, 2026, Sipalo allegedly trafficked 700 grams of marijuana, a herbal product of Cannabis sativa, in Kabwe District without lawful authority.

Sipalo was arrested by a four-member team of Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) officers who raided his premises on the night of June 5, 2026.

Throughout the trial, Sipalo maintained his innocence and denied the charge, alleging that the DEC officers planted the 700 grams of marijuana in his bag.

Sipalo has since closed his defence after calling one witness.

Magistrate Mwenya adjourned the matter to September 30, 2026 for judgment while Sipalo remains in police custody.

World.title: We don’t fear Algeria – Lwandamina
World.content:
Chipolopolo Coach George Lwandamina has declared that Zambia does not fear Algeria and Togo ahead of this month’s back-to-back 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers.

Zambia plays Algeria in Algiers on 25th September and hosts Togo in Ndola on the 29th.

Speaking when he unveiled his 27-man squad in Lusaka, Lwandamina said Zambia has an opportunity to re-write history.

“We have respect for Algeria and Togo, but we cannot fear them. We have an opportunity to rewrite history. Even players as they are coming for these games have to work toward that goal. We have already been drawn against Algeria so we can’t say we won’t play, we will play and win,” Lwandamina said.

He said Chipolopolo understands the task ahead.

“Yes, Algeria played at the World Cup, but we also played against Argentina in a friendly match, so we measured our prowess. We understand what is ahead of us,” Lwandamina said.

The Nchanga Rangers coach said his bench will manage pressure.

“A period does not determine the levels of pressure, it can be a minute, but you are under a pressure, it can be ten years, but you are still under pressure. I’m sure we will be able to resolve the issue of pressure psychologically going into this game,” he said.

Lwandamina is confident Zambia can deliver.

“We demand that players are selfless and perform well for Mother Zambia. Players must come and fight to the bitter end. It won’t be an easy task but collectively I’m sure we can do it,” he said.

Asked about absentees, Lwandamina said selection is bound by rules and need to broaden scope.

“There are various reasons why some players are missing from the squad. I’m not in a position to delve into whatever we do in the bedroom but just know that when a player is not in the squad, they might be injured or suspended. I’m sure I’m confident and they can deliver,” he said.

“There are so many players out there, but we are bound by numbers. We have to follow CAF and FIFA benchmarks. We have limits. I understand where you are coming, they are good players, they have been there, but we have to see even others for us to broaden the scope of selection. We don’t have to confine ourselves to the same people all the time. Zambia is big,” he added.

Zambia is in Group I alongside Algeria, Togo, and Burundi.

The 2027 AFCON will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda under the banner TotalEnergies AFCON Pamoja 2027.

Top two teams in nine of the 12 groups will qualify automatically.

In Groups D, H, L – where the three host nations are – only one slot will be available.

World.title: CWAWUZ condemns threats on public workers
World.content:
The Civil Service and Allied Workers Union of Zambia has expressed concern over social media reports of alleged dismissal of public workers who supported opposition President for National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity Brian Mundubile, in the just ended general election.

CSAWUZ General Secretary Teddy Muyenga says such reported statements have the potential implications on the security, impartiality and professionalism of Zambia’s public service.

Mr Muyenga emphasised that civil servants, just like any other citizen are entitled to exercise their constitutional rights, including political opinions and participate in the democratic process.

He added that the public service is governed by established laws, regulations, codes of ethics and conditions of service, and that if an officer commits misconduct, disciplinary actions are duly undertaken.

“No civil servant should be intimidated, threatened, victimised. Discriminated against or subjected to disciplinary action merely because of their perceived political preference or the candidate they supported,” Mr Muyenga stated.

He therefore called on the relevant public service authorities and political leaders to provide clear reassurance to civil servants that their employment will not be threatened on account of how they voted.

He also assured public workers that CSAWUZ will not stand by while the rights, dignity and job security of civil servants are threatened on the basis of political affiliation or preference.

Mr Muyenga urged civil servants to remain calm and continue discharging their responsibilities with professionalism, integrity and impartiality, while observing the public service code of ethics and conduct, and all other applicable laws and regulations.

World.title: IBA to hold compliance hearings on election coverage
World.content:
The Independent Broadcasting authority (IBA) has called five broadcasting stations for compliance hearings, following its monitoring and regulatory assessment of the coverage of the 2026 general election.

In a statement issued to the media IBA Director General Webster Malido revealed that the Authority identified instances of non-compliance involving, among others, broadcasting of unsubstantiated allegations and unverified or potentially misleading information.

Mr Malido added broadcasts of hate speech and tribal content and inadequate editorial challenge of allegations and claims made by guests, including members of the public.

The IBA Director General disclosed that the affected stations have been called for compliance hearings scheduled for Wednesday, September 16 2026.

“The hearing will provide the stations with an opportunity to respond to the findings before the Authority determines the appropriate action,” Mr Malido indicated.

And he reaffirmed the Authorities commitment to promoting responsible broadcasting, while upholding the principles of media freedom and the right to freedom of expression, in accordance with the law and applicable broadcasting standards.

World.title: Mbala residents happy with Munyazi-Ntenda road works
World.content:
Mbala Municipal Council has outlined the scope of works for the Munyazi-Ntenda road.

The road project is expected to improve connectivity and facilitate the movement of goods and services in the area.

The project is being funded through the 2025 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) fuel allocation, with K1,075, 000 earmarked for works covering a 25-kilometre stretch of the road.

Mbala Municipal Council Director of Engineering, Chipa Mbewe, said the works will include bush clearing, road formation and spot gravelling.

Mr Mbewe said the project is important as the road connects key farming communities and that once completed, it will make it easier for farmers to transport their produce and access essential goods and services.

He added that improved road infrastructure will also contribute to increased economic activity by strengthening connectivity between communities and markets.

“The Munyazi-Ntenda road is important to the local farming communities because it will help improve the movement of agricultural produce and access to essential goods and services, which is key in district like ours,” Mr Mbewe said.

He said the road is expected to play an important role in supporting local farmers and facilitating the movement of agricultural produce and other goods.

And residents are expectant of the benefit from improved accessibility once the works are completed.

One of the residents, Evans Sinyangwe has expressed happiness with the progress of works carried out so far.

“We want to see this road completed, we have suffered for a long time, we now want to be moving quicker into town and come back,” he said.

“Transport has been expensive due to the bad road because only a few vehicles could come here, we that once completed more transporters will come thereby reducing transport costs,” he added

The Mbala Town Council through CDF has worked on number projects which include roads and school infrastructure among others.

World.title: DRMD aids 247 Kalumbila households
World.content:
Government, through the Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) has distributed relief food to 247 households in Chovwe of Kalumbila District whose crops were destroyed by elephants earlier this year.

Relief food is aimed at cushioning the affected households and reducing the burden caused by the human-wildlife conflict.

Speaking during the distribution of the food items, Kalumbila District Commissioner (DC), Brenda Sankisa commended Government for responding to the needs of the affected communities.

Ms Sankisa said the relief food should not be regarded as compensation but as Government support to cushion households affected by the disaster.

She said human-wildlife conflict is a natural disaster and that the elephants are state property, requiring collective efforts to find lasting solutions.

Ms Sankisa said the relief will help lighten the burden on families whose crops were destroyed

And District Disaster Management Officer, Mumba Chilangwa said the consignment includes 360 bags by 25-kilograms mealie meal, 147 by 20 kilograms sugar, 94 bags by three-kilograms soya chunks and 18 bags by 50-kilograms beans.

The other consignment includes 49 bags by 50-kilograms salt, 14 bags by 50-kilograms kapenta and 360 liters of Cooking oil.

Beneficiaries have thanked Government for the relief food, saying it will help ease the impact of crop losses.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 15, 2026
World.content:
press review

Dangote Petroleum Refinery Launches Record $1.6bn IPO

Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has launched what is expected to become Africa's biggest initial public offering, seeking to raise about $1.6 billion to expand his Lagos-based refinery. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery, which began operating in 2024. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery aims to raise funds to double its capacity to 1.4 million barrels a day by 2028, which would make it the world's largest refinery, surpassing Jamnagar in India. Dangote said the IPO was "not simply about listing a company; it is about listing a new possibility for Nigeria, and for Africa". Dangote is encouraging ordinary Nigerians to participate, with shares available in small quantities, saying the listing could broaden public ownership while reducing Africa's dependence on imported refined fuel. The company also has ambitions to expand into other African countries.

UN Warns Sudan Humanitarian Aid Could Run Out Within Weeks

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

United Nations aid agencies have warned that humanitarian assistance in Sudan could be significantly reduced within weeks because of severe funding shortages, despite the country facing one of the world's worst hunger and displacement crises. About 8.6 million people remain internally displaced and 19.5 million face crisis levels of food insecurity. The International Organization for Migration says essential shelter, sanitation and emergency relief supplies could run out by the end of September. The World Food Programme is only about one-third funded. Continued fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces is displacing thousands more people, while aid workers face major access challenges. The United Nations is calling for increased funding, protection of civilians and safe humanitarian access across the country.

Uganda Reverses Invictus Games Withdrawal

Uganda has reversed its decision to withdraw from the 2027 Invictus Games in Birmingham after receiving clarification from Buckingham Palace that King Charles III has no objection to the country's participation. The decision followed a call between Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, and the King's principal private secretary. Uganda had announced its withdrawal over concerns about taking part in the games. Gen Muhoozi welcomed the clarification and said preparations for Uganda's participation in the competition would resume. The Invictus Games, founded by Prince Harry in 2014, brings together wounded, injured and sick serving military personnel and veterans to compete in adaptive sports. Uganda joined the Invictus Games this year as the 26th participating nation, becoming the first East African country to take part in the international sporting event.

M23 Rebels Establish Parallel Rule in Eastern DR Congo

Rwanda-backed M23 rebels have established a parallel system of governance and taxation across areas they control in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, using income from businesses, transport, cross-border trade and minerals to finance their administration and military operations. The rebels have taken control of major cities including Goma and Bukavu and impose fees on residents, businesses, transporters and humanitarian organisations. Mineral resources, particularly coltan from the Rubaya mining area, provide another major source of revenue, with minerals reportedly moving through Rwanda and into international markets. However, the taxation system is placing further pressure on an economy already damaged by war. The closure of banks and Goma airport has disrupted trade and left many residents struggling to access money, jobs and basic services.

Close 

Ruto Warns Kenya Leaders Against Divisive Politics

Kenyan President William Ruto has warned political leaders against using violence, tribalism and division to pursue their political interests ahead of the 2027 General Election. Speaking in Kisumu during his development tour of Nyanza, Ruto called on opposition parties to present clear political programmes rather than relying on what he described as outdated politics. He also highlighted government investments in Kisumu, including billions of shillings for roads, affordable housing, water and sanitation, police housing and aviation infrastructure. Ruto commissioned a major Lake Victoria water and sanitation project and launched road construction projects, saying the investments would improve connectivity, expand services and support economic activity in the region.

World.title: South Africa: Durban Refugees Relocated to Gauteng - South African News Briefs - September 15, 2026
World.content:
A refugee shows the papers permitting her to be in South Africa in the hope of avoiding harassment by March and March.

press review

Durban Migrants Relocated to Gauteng After Months in Camps

Refugees and asylum seekers who have been camping outside the Home Affairs offices in Durban since May are being relocated to Gauteng, reports EWN. They were forced from their homes and businesses ahead of the 30 June anti-illegal immigration protests, with tensions around the makeshift camp escalating in recent weeks. Home Affairs says it will transport 278 people to the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp, prompting mixed emotions. Some migrants, including Ghanaian hairdresser Princess Adjei and Congolese refugee Robert Bhabi, said they were hopeful about starting again elsewhere, despite finding it difficult to leave Durban. Some refugees, however, have chosen to remain in the city.

Madlanga Probe Resumes After Two-Week Break

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Madlanga Commission of Inquiry is resuming its hearings with testimony focusing on the Johannesburg Metro Police Department (JMPD), reports SABC News. The commission, established by President Cyril Ramaphosa to investigate alleged political interference, corruption and criminal infiltration of the criminal justice system. It will examine claims that criminal networks have infiltrated the JMPD and that some officers have colluded with criminal syndicates. Commission spokesperson Jeremy Michaels said Tuesday marked the 173rd day of hearings, with the inquiry now turning to one of the law enforcement agencies covered by its terms of reference.

EFF Demands Action Over Women's Deaths

The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) has accused police of failing to respond urgently to the disappearance and deaths of women in the Kempton Park area, reports EWN. The criticism follows the discovery of a fifth woman's body in Olifantsfontein, after four other women with similar profiles were previously found dead. The party said police only raised the possibility of a serial killer after the disappearance of a missing runner attracted widespread public attention. EFF spokesperson Nthabiseng Tshivhenga said the repeated discoveries point to a failure by the State to protect women and called for a comprehensive investigation into the deaths, previous missing-person reports and the police response.

World.title: Egypt: Sudanese Journalist Arrested Over Alleged Social Media Post
World.content:
press release

It has been a week since Attaf Mohamed Mokhtar was arrested and still no allegations against him have been made public by the Egyptian authorities.

Mokhtar, the editor-in-chief of the newspaper Al-Sudani, fled Sudan with his family and settled down in Cairo after the civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary group, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), began in April 2023. He is known for being a vocal critic of the role of external powers supporting the RSF and interfering in Sudan's internal affairs.

He was reportedly arrested in connection with a social media post criticising Sudan's internal affairs, but the Egyptian authorities have neither confirmed nor denied this information.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The SJU issued a statement calling for the immediate release of Mokhtar and pointing out that they had contacted senior officials from Sudan's government to call for his freedom. "The union is deeply concerned about the fate of Attaf, given the absence of information regarding his health or the circumstances that led to his detention from his apartment in Cairo. We hope for his immediate release and for clarification of the reasons behind his arrest [...]".

IFJ General Secretary Anthony Bellanger demanded Mokhtar's immediate release and warned that his arrest would have a chilling effect on exiled journalists in Egypt, who would no longer feel safe expressing their views for fear of intimidation and harassment. Bellanger said:

"We are extremely concerned by the arrest of Mokhtar, a journalist who was simply exercising his right to freedom of expression by voicing critical views on his country's internal affairs. Independent journalism and critical voices are particularly important in conflict zones, as they inform citizens and shape an informed public opinion. This case raises serious concerns about freedom of expression, and it could have a chilling effect on exiled journalists in the country. Egypt is well-known for hosting exiled journalists from the region, and their safety must be guaranteed. The IFJ urges the Egyptian authorities to release Mokhtar immediately and unconditionally."

World.title: South Sudan: Credible Elections Are No Longer Possible in South Sudan - What Next?
World.content:
analysis

Attention should shift to preserving the peace deal that underpins the current government and is key to averting large-scale violence.

South Sudan's cabinet last week approved legal amendments in preparation for the December 2026 elections. The day before, on 10 September, the United Nations Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan reported that the country lacked 'many of the safeguards and conditions for peaceful and credible polls' - an assessment the government swiftly rejected.

South Sudan hasn't held national elections since its 2011 independence due to recurring cycles of armed conflict and political stalling. Now, major political and technical problems again preclude credible polls that would have ended the prolonged transition.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The country's first elections, scheduled for 2015, were delayed after civil war broke out in 2013. Since then, polls have been postponed five times. The first peace deal lasted barely a year and was followed by the 2018 Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (R-ARCSS).

President Salva Kiir Mayardit and First Vice-President Riek Machar's political rivalry has characterised post-independence conflicts and peace processes, often obscuring the crisis' underlying triggers, such as militarisation of politics and elite bargaining.

Periods of rapprochement, such as after the 2018 agreement, helped reduce bloodshed and ushered in some stability. But as other conflicts intensified, including in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Sudan, South Sudan's transition receded from international attention, weakening the pressure needed to push for the agreement's implementation.

Over the past year, Kiir has undermined the accord's power-sharing arrangement through unilateral cabinet dismissals, the replacement of opposition lawmakers, and delays in security sector reforms. Considering that the country's transitional government is anchored on the agreement, abandoning it would dismantle the political settlement that ended the conflict in 2018.

Kiir's first move was to place Machar under house arrest in March 2025 after an attack on a military base by the White Army militia, who predominantly belong to the Nuer, Machar's ethnic group. The government accused Machar of orchestrating the attack, and he, along with several close associates, faces treason charges.

Kiir has resisted international calls to release Machar. The vice-president remains a powerful and aggrieved political actor with deep ethnic, military and political networks capable of mobilising significant opposition, particularly in Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei. If released before elections, he could threaten Kiir's bid to extend his term.

Tanzania and Uganda held elections in October 2025 and January 2026, respectively, amid violent repression, with key opposition candidates detained. A similar approach in South Sudan's militarised and fragile political environment could plunge the country back into renewed conflict reminiscent of 2013.

Since Machar's arrest, Kiir has made several unilateral reshuffles in the Revitalised Transitional Government of National Unity, contrary to the 2018 deal's power-sharing provisions. The administration has purged Machar's wing of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement/Army-in-Opposition (SPLM/A-IO) from government and replaced it with members of Peace Building Minister Stephen Par Kuol's SPLM/A-IO splinter faction. The faction is allied with Kiir and supports the current flawed electoral process.

Kiir has also unilaterally amended the 2018 deal to remove legal 'obstacles' to conducting elections, thereby violating the agreement. The 22 July amendments removed the preconditions for holding elections, including a national census and a new constitution. He also sought to reduce the deal's supremacy in the country's legal system, thereby enabling the government to implement its provisions selectively.

Machar's SPLM/A-IO wing says any electoral process should occur in line with the peace deal and involve all parties to the agreement. It says failure to implement the deal's key provisions remains the main obstacle to holding free, fair and credible polls.

To counter the government's growing dominance, Machar's SPLM/A-IO wing has allied with other armed actors, such as the National Salvation Front. The groups have conducted several joint military operations against state forces - drawing condemnation from the Ceasefire and Transitional Security Arrangements Monitoring and Verification Mechanism.

With less than four months to voting day, the government continues to water down the peace deal amid a growing insecurity and humanitarian crisis. Over 2.5 million people are internally displaced, and more than 10 million need assistance.

Meanwhile, significant technical and political problems with polling preparation remain unresolved, notably the underfunding of the National Elections Commission and the lack of a voter register. Widespread insecurity also makes it hard for the electoral body to reach all areas, and hinders citizens' movement.

Kiir's insistence on holding elections in December presents two possible scenarios. First, by pushing ahead with non-credible polls, Kiir could win the election and remain in office. But by ushering in a new, illegitimate political dispensation, that outcome would deepen instability.

Second, Kiir may be setting the stage for another transition extension. By engaging in last-minute electoral preparations, he may be signalling a commitment to the polls he knows probably won't happen, in order to build a case for an extension.

Both scenarios would render the 2018 peace agreement obsolete - risking a return to large-scale fighting. Kiir seems to favour the first scenario, to consolidate power and secure total control.

Close 

Any endorsement by international partners for holding elections under current political conditions would be counterproductive. It would signal acquiescence in dismantling the 2018 deal, risking a reversal of hard-won progress.

African Union High Representative for South Sudan, Jakaya Kikwete, should push international partners to establish common minimum conditions for elections. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, a close ally of Kiir, should persuade him to reconsider his current course. International pressure for Machar's release should continue, along with efforts to prevent further unilateral actions by Kiir and contravention of the 2018 agreement.

Finally, given that credible elections cannot be organised within the remaining time, international actors should push for a consensual extension with a clear, time-bound roadmap to elections. This could salvage the deal and save the country from a return to entrenched large-scale violence.

Guyo Chepe Turi, Research Officer, East Africa Peace and Security Governance, ISS Nairobi

Said Abdullahi, Research Intern, Conflict Prevention, Management, Resolution and Peacebuilding in the Great Lakes Region, ISS Nairobi

World.title: Africa: New 'Blockbuster' Tuberculosis Vaccines Could Save Seven Million Lives by 2050
World.content:
Next-generation TB vaccines, expected to become available from 2029, could deliver major health and economic gains, helping to save an estimated 7.3 million lives, generate up to US$ 135 billion in economic benefits for low-and middle-income countries by 2050, and support efforts to combat antimicrobial resistance.

Action must be taken now to ensure that countries with the highest disease burden are able to access vaccines in sufficient quantities

Gavi CEO, Dr Sania Nishtar: "Novel TB vaccines could be the next blockbuster immunisation tool, however they will only realise their potential if we can ensure sufficient, predictable and affordable supply for those countries that need them most."

Geneva, 14 September 2026 – New tuberculosis (TB) vaccines, which are expected to become available from 2029, could help save up to an estimated 7.3 million lives between 2030 and 2050 1 , unlocking up to US$ 135 billion in economic benefits across low- and middle-income countries, according to new analysis on their potential impact. These benefits highlight the potential for new TB vaccines to become one of the most impactful new immunisation tools in decades, representing a breakthrough technology in fighting the world's deadliest infectious disease.

Nevertheless, in its Early Market Shaping Roadmap for novel TB Vaccines , published today, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) warns that action is required now to prepare governments and vaccine manufacturers for the vaccines' arrival. According to the Roadmap, demand for the vaccines among low-income countries and middle-income countries could reach, on average, 86 million vaccination courses per year, with greater demand in the early years as high-burden countries seek to expand protection across multiple age groups in high-risk areas.



"Novel TB vaccines could be the next blockbuster immunisation tool, however they will only realise their potential if we are able to ensure sufficient, predictable and affordable supply for those countries with the highest disease burden," said Dr Sania Nishtar, CEO of Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. "In order to help countries secure doses in the volumes they need, we are beginning to work with partners now to lay the groundwork for timely access when these vaccines become available."

Roadmap to a powerful new tool

2024 saw 10.7 million tuberculosis cases and 1.2 million tuberculosis deaths globally. The burden falls overwhelmingly on low- and middle-income countries, with Gavi-supported countries accounting for an estimated 77% of all deaths. The one vaccine currently licensed, the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine, is over 100 years old, and while it is effective in protecting infants and young children against severe forms of the disease, its protection wanes, highlighting the need for new tools to prevent manifestation of the disease among adolescents and adults.

New vaccines aim to fill that gap. Designed to prevent infectious pulmonary TB disease among adolescents and adults, they would be a major addition in the fight against TB. Combined with other prevention measures, they could accelerate progress against one of the world's deadliest diseases.

With the first of these new promising candidate vaccines potentially securing regulatory approval by the end of this decade, Gavi's Roadmap has identified a series of risks that could hold back rapid rollout once licensure is secured. These include policy risks, including the possibility that recommendations could be limited to the highest-risk groups because of gaps in evidence; risks that could limit uptake by countries, such as inadequate global and domestic financing, and supply risks, driven, for example, by this demand uncertainty holding back manufacturer capacity investments for late-stage candidates.

To overcome these risks, Gavi highlights three well-defined objectives that, drawing on its market-shaping and innovative financing expertise, it will pursue to help ensure new vaccines reach low-income and middle-income countries that need them the most, as fast and equitably as possible. These are:

Objective 1: Ensure sufficient, timely, affordable and sustainable supply of novel TB vaccines to meet demand.

Objective 2: Support widespread uptake that maximises health impact through routine immunisation and targeted catch-up campaigns.

Close 

Objective 3: Encourage a competitive and geographically diverse pipeline of novel TB vaccine candidates, ensuring products meet country preferences.

Alongside this work, several high-burden countries, including some hosting vaccine trials, are already laying the groundwork for rollout once vaccines come available. Through the WHO TB Vaccine Accelerator's Finance & Access working group, Gavi will continue working with partners in its co-lead capacity, to support these efforts with the ultimate goal of bringing these new TB vaccines as rapidly as possible to the people who need them most.

1. Preliminary modelling by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), based on a vaccination scenario targeting high-risk populations and adolescents through routine immunisation, alongside targeted catch-up campaigns in those populations and high-burden settings. Assumes 50% efficacy against TB disease irrespective of previous exposure, with immunity waning exponentially over 10 years.

World.title: South Africa: Sixth Woman Found Dead in Ekurhuleni As Fears Deepen
World.content:
A plane flies above smog above Kempton Park in Gauteng, South Africa.

A woman's body was reportedly found in Kwa-Thema, bringing to six the number of women found dead across Ekurhuleni in two months.

Police say four of the five Kempton Park victims showed signs of sexual assault while two of the women remain unidentified.

Fears over the safety of women in Ekurhuleni have deepened after another woman's body was reportedly discovered.

The latest body was found in Kwa-Thema, Springs, east of Johannesburg. Kwa-Thema is 45km away from Kempton Park where the bodies of five women were discovered over the past two months, bringing the total to six.

Police are investigating the five Kempton Park cases but have not confirmed that the Kwa-Thema discovery is connected to them.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Deputy National Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Tebello Mosikili revealed more disturbing details about the five Kempton Park cases during a media briefing on Monday night.

Police say four of the five women showed signs of sexual assault.

"We know that they were all sexually molested, or at least the majority of them," Mosikili said.

She said one of the bodies was too badly decomposed for police to make the same finding at this stage.

"But the other four, yes, the team can confirm that they were sexually molested," she said.

Police are also trying to identify two of the five women found around Kempton Park.

"So out of the five here in Kempton Park, the only two bodies have not yet been identified," Mosikili said.

The five Kempton Park victims were found partially clothed, with visible bruising reported in the cases.

Police have not confirmed that one person is responsible for the deaths.

They have also not confirmed that a serial killer is operating in the area.

A multidisciplinary police team has been set up to investigate the Kempton Park deaths and establish whether they are connected.

The team includes experienced detectives and specialists from the Investigative Psychology Unit.

One of the identified women is 38-year-old runner Elizabeth "Tsontso" Moselakgomo.

Moselakgomo disappeared last week after leaving home for a run. Her family identified her body on Monday, bringing a heartbreaking end to the search for the runner. Tsontso leaves behind an eight-year-old daughter.

In the Ekurhuleni case, investigators are still yet to establish how the woman died and whether her death has any connection to the five cases around Kempton Park.

World.title: Nigeria: IPO 'For The People' Is Out of Reach for Many in Nigeria
World.content:
Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

The industrialist Aliko Dangote is turning to Nigerians to help finance the next growth phase of his oil refinery: The richest man in Africa announced that he is seeking to attract about $1.6 billion (€1.4 billion) by going public.

This initial public offering of Dangote Industries is intended to help support a $14.3 billion expansion, which would more than double the refinery's production capacity. In absolute numbers, it would increase capacity from 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 1.4 million bpd.



It would also include new petrochemical and refining units designed to reduce Nigeria's reliance on imports of some petrochemical products while also allowing the plant to produce different grades of diesel.

This plan would make the refinery one of the largest single-site refining complexes in the world.

Dangote's ambitious plans also include the launch of a processing plant in Kenya to extend his reach from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean, which is planned to be launched in partnership with governments in eastern Africa.

African success story

Since it began operations in 2024, the Dangote Petroleum Refinery has started to reshape Nigeria's fuel market, and has become one of the few businesses in the world to benefit from the ongoing supply disruptions caused by the war in Iran.

The refinery has become an important supplier of petrol and other fuels domestically and abroad; in fact, it made Nigeria a net exporter of refined fuel for the first time after reaching its full capacity in early 2026.

The refinery reported making an after-tax profit of $1.82 billion in the first half of 2026, following â a $476 million loss for all of 2025.

Things appear to be on the up-and-up for Dangote — so, why is the company seeking public investment now?

Why go public?

Ayodele Oni, an energy analyst and partner with the Bloomfield Law Practice in Lagos, told DW that the public offering could be a "game changer," as it alters the role of who could stand to benefit from Dangote's expansion drive.

Oni said equity invested by potentially millions of Nigerian and international shareholders would shield the corporation from having to rely solely on expensive dollar debt "with permanent Naira capital, which matches a business now earning heavily in Naira."

This could also unlock additional long-term investment as any "listed company answers to ... its shareholders every quarter."

"That transparency is precisely what long-term lenders and international partners want to see before the next billion is committed," Oni said.

He said this would turn into a sustainable model for Dangote, as the approach would be designed to permanently "lower its cost of capital for every future phase."

For 'the people'

Oni summarized the potential of the deal by referring to it as a restructuring of both who bears the risk — and who stands to share with the reward, with "the people" being the greatest beneficiaries of the IPO, at least to his mind.

Opening up the ownership of the refinery business to ordinary Nigerians does not automatically mean that many can afford it, however.

The pricing of the initial offering is indeed priced at an affordable 525 Naira (€0.34/$0.39) a piece for each of the 4.1 billion ordinary shares, and a minimum of just 10 shares.

At the signing ceremony in Lagos, Dangote said the company was trying to "make sure that the majority of … our drivers, our cook, our servants, our managers, everybody will have an opportunity to have a stake in the refinery."

Deep inequality, deeper pockets

In a country where almost two-thirds of the population is struggling with extreme poverty, according to Nigeria's National Bureau of Statistics, that figure can translate into 10% of the minimum wage — for people who are fortunate enough to have a job.

Entry-level employees and workers who perform menial tasks at Dangote are fortunate enough to earn almost four times the minimum wage in Nigeria, according to media reports — though this still translates to only about $150 a month in a country that has been witnessing steep inflation, especially in petrol prices. For most, seeing any personal benefit by investing in Nigeria's oil remains a pipe dream.

Charles Asiegbu, a policy and economic analyst who has worked as a consultant for various Nigerian organizations, told DW that Dangote's description of the offer as "for the people" could still qualify as a "psychological masterstroke" for those who can afford to invest.

Asiegbu said broader ownership could bring a large number of Nigerians into one consolidated platform, changing how they view the refinery.

"With millions as shareholders, it would shift from a private enterprise to a national asset in the public consciousness," Asiegbu said.

IPO excites investors

Nigerians who can afford to invest in Dangote appear to quickly be adopting that mindset.

Olamilekan Oladehinde, a Nigerian retail investor, told DW that he is "excited" to partake in the launch and buy shares. He said Dangote was now much more than just a private enterprise: It has become a key national asset that addresses direct social problems in Nigeria — including fuel shortages.

"They're trying to expand, and that's something I am very proud and happy to identify with," Oladehinde said. "The fact that it's also owned by a Nigerian makes me more than happy, and that's why I will be buying a stake in the company," he said about the richest man in Africa.

Close 

Risks and opportunities

Oladehinde said he had no concerns about investing in Dangote — despite the fact that various market experts have cautioned investors to be mindful of potential risks, especially because refining is a cyclical business.

Oni said Dangote was riding a wave during the current situation across the Middle East; however, fortunes could change — especially when the tensions around the Strait of Hormuz eventually ease. A return to steep competition in oil prices from those Middle Eastern countries could then saturate markets.

Dangote's strengths were a mitigating factor, Oni said: "The Middle East disruption showed that a refinery on [Nigeria's] Atlantic coast can supply Europe and the Americas faster than the Gulf can — and, at 700,000 bpd, the plant has already proven the model, so the expansion is about scale on an existing site, which is the cheapest capacity anyone can build."

Oladehinde said this was exactly the outlook that he will be betting on. "I believe the time has come for us," he said. "We can't lose this the momentum."

Edited by: Sertan Sanderson

World.title: Uganda: General Muhoozi Reinstates Uganda's Participation in 2027 Invictus Games
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has reinstated Uganda's participation in the 2027 Invictus Games in Birmingham, United Kingdom, following clarification from Buckingham Palace on the position of King Charles III.

The decision follows a telephone conversation between Gen Muhoozi and Sir Clive Alderton K.C.V.O., the Principal Private Secretary to King Charles III and Queen Camilla.

According to the Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF), Sir Alderton conveyed the King's position that he had no objection to Uganda taking part in the games and encouraged the military to proceed with preparations for the event.



"King Charles III was moved by General Kainerugaba's sensitive consideration of the King's opinion on the upcoming Invictus Games organised by Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex," Col Chris Magezi, the Acting Director of Defence Public Information, said in a statement on Monday.

Sir Alderton reportedly told Gen Muhoozi that the King had no objection to Uganda's participation, providing clarification on an issue that had earlier prompted the CDF to announce Uganda's withdrawal from the games.

Gen Muhoozi welcomed the clarification and said preparations for Uganda's participation in the competition would resume.

The Invictus Games, founded by Prince Harry in 2014, brings together wounded, injured and sick serving military personnel and veterans to compete in adaptive sports.

Uganda joined the Invictus Games this year as the 26th participating nation, becoming the first East African country to take part in the international sporting event.

However, Uganda's participation was thrown into uncertainty last week after Gen Muhoozi announced that the UPDF would withdraw from the 2027 games, citing the need to protect Uganda's close relationship with the British Monarchy.

The withdrawal followed communication from Buckingham Palace which, according to the UPDF, described the Invictus Games as a private charity organisation rather than an official initiative of the British Royal Family.

Gen Muhoozi subsequently said Uganda would not want its participation to be interpreted as opposition to King Charles III, whom he said Uganda deeply respects.

The latest communication clears the way for the UPDF to resume preparations for the Birmingham games, with the military expected to proceed with plans to send a Ugandan team to the competition.

World.title: Colbert wins Emmy after show's cancellation but avoids discussing Trump
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The White House on Tuesday denied President Donald Trump had any role in CBS' decision to cancel "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert," after the former late-night host dodged a question about Trump following his Emmy win in Los Angeles and defended the state of free speech.

Colbert's former program won Outstanding Variety Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards Monday, months after "The Late Show" aired its final episode in May.

When asked after the ceremony about free speech and the future of late-night television, Colbert said he remained optimistic about the medium.

"If you can’t say something because you go to jail, that is a violation of free speech," Colbert said. "I think that late night is just as funny and just as vital as it ever has been, and I love watching Jimmy and Jimmy and John and John and Seth and everybody else. And I think I hope it goes on for a long time because you get to work with people like this, and that’s the greatest gift."

STEPHEN COLBERT EMERGES FROM CANCELLATION TO URGE EMMY VOTERS TO SELECT JIMMY KIMMEL OVER OWN SHOW

White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital the administration had nothing to do with the network’s decision.

"Neither President Trump nor anyone else in the Administration had anything to do with this," Ingle said, in a Tuesday statement to Fox News Digital. "The reality is Stephen Colbert is a pathetic trainwreck with no talent, which is exactly why CBS canceled his show and is booting him off the airwaves."

When CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister asked Colbert directly whether he believed his show had been canceled because of Trump, the comedian appeared to repeatedly deflect rather than answer the question.

Variety reported that the exchange came during a post-Emmys interview with Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh.

COLBERT LASHES OUT AT CBS, SAYS CANCELLATION ‘REINFORCED A NARRATIVE’ OF ‘KNEE BENDING’ TO TRUMP

"What... Gayle, that’s a beautiful dress," Colbert said. After the reporter repeated the question, Colbert continued the bit. "Oh, I’m sorry, I’m deaf on this ear. What did you... what did you say?" Colbert said.

When they again attempted to ask whether Trump was responsible for the cancellation, Colbert deflected once more. "You wanted to know who the most important member of my staff was? It’s me," Colbert said.

Media Research Center President David Bozell told Fox News Digital on Tuesday that Colbert’s refusal to address the Trump question stood in contrast to the speculation surrounding the cancellation and pointed to CBS’ financial rationale for ending the show.

"Colbert suddenly does not want to talk about Trump? That’s rich. Obviously, Trump did not cancel his show," he said. "CBS looked at the audience, looked at the bill, and decided the joke had run long enough."

JIMMY KIMMEL SAYS HE FELT 'DEFEATED' AFTER COLBERT SHOW WAS CANCELLED, SAYS CBS IS USING 'MADE-UP NUMBERS'

CBS announced in July 2025 that it would end "The Late Show" franchise after Colbert's 25-26 season, calling the move "purely a financial decision against a challenging backdrop in late night." The network said the decision was unrelated to the show's performance, content or other matters involving then-parent company Paramount.

The announcement came three days after Colbert attacked Paramount over its $16 million settlement with Trump involving a "60 Minutes" interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris. Colbert characterized the agreement as a payoff connected to Paramount’s pending merger with Skydance Media.

"I believe this kind of complicated financial sentiment with a sitting government official has a technical name in legal circles. It’s ‘big fat bribe,’ because it all comes as Paramount’s owners are trying to get the Trump administration to approve the sale of our network to a new owner, Skydance!" Colbert said at the time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Fox News Digital reported that Colbert's manager, James Dixon, had been informed June 27 that CBS intended to end the show, before Paramount announced the Trump settlement and more than two weeks before Colbert publicly attacked the agreement. "The Late Show" had been losing roughly $40 million annually.

The FCC approved Paramount's $8 billion merger with Skydance one week after CBS announced the cancellation. The transaction later closed in August 2025.

Trump continued criticizing Colbert after the program’s May finale, calling the former CBS host talentless and celebrating his departure from late-night television.

Fox News Digital reached out to CBS-Paramount for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

World.title: Florida State fans pining for Jimbo Fisher's return are living in the past, not in reality
World.content:
Congratulations, Seminoles fans, part one of your master plan to return to the pantheon of college football has been completed.

For those unaware, Florida State fired their embattled athletic director, Michael Alford, earlier this week.

The reason that's so significant is multifaceted, but his main transgression and the thing that ultimately lost him his job was the recent skid of the once-proud FSU football team.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

And that all ties back to a decision Alford made back in 2024, when he gifted head coach Mike Norvell a massive contract extension with an almost absurd buyout.

The monetary numbers were questionable, even at a time when Norvell and the Noles were trending in the right direction, but since then, the program has taken a sharp downturn, punctuated by an 8-18 record since their ACC Championship winning season in 2023.

DID ALABAMA DOOM THEMSELVES TO MEDIOCRITY WITH KALEN DEBOER EXTENSION?

So, now that Alford is sunk, the man he chose to anchor himself to has to be on the way out as well, right?

In theory, yes, but there's still that pesky buyout number that keeps getting brought up.

And then there's the other question that gets raised whenever schools even think about firing their current head coach: who can we hire?

There are a ton of quality names out there that the Seminoles should absolutely consider as their next head coach, but one of the only names I keep seeing tossed around by fans on social media is former Florida State head coach Jimbo Fisher.

KEEP AN EYE ON THESE UNDER-THE-RADAR NAMES DURING THIS SEASON'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL

I get it.

Things are brutal right now in Tallahassee, and Noles fans are just trying to cling onto something from the good old days, but I'm not so sure if Fisher is the answer.

Let's start with his age.

Fisher turns 61 in October, and while plenty of great coaches have had phenomenal seasons well into their 60s and 70s, the former FSU and Texas A&M head man hasn't donned a headset in three years, which might as well be dog years given how different the game of college football looks now.

Speaking of Texas A&M, Fisher's last stop as a head coach with the Aggies left a lot to be desired.

While in College Station, Fisher compiled a 45-25 record, which is fine, but definitely not what he was hired to do.

His five and a half years as the Aggies' head coach was marred by inconsistent offenses and power struggles, as his inability to hand over the controls on offense before it was too late is partially what led to his demise.

One of the reasons Fisher left the confines of Tallahassee - where he had won a national championship - for Texas A&M was (allegedly) the fact that Florida State would not meet his demands for more resourcing.

The Aggies are one of the most well-resourced football programs in America, and the fact that he was never able to even make an SEC Championship Game shouldn't inspire confidence.

I doubt the Seminoles are in a position, financially speaking, to give Fisher the funds he needs to compete on the national stage, and even if they do, would he be able to wind back the clocks and have FSU looking like the mid 2010s version of themselves?

As I said earlier, I totally get it.

As a Gator fan, when things were coming to a merciful end with Billy Napier, I started to talk myself into the idea of Urban Meyer coming home and coaching Florida again.

But being realistic, that would have never worked.

Meyer flamed out at his final stop in Jacksonville and he was nearly a decade removed from coaching in college football.

Florida State needs to move forward, not backward.

Find a hot, up-and-coming coach that will thrust the Seminoles into the modern era of college football.

Just off the top of my head, a guy like Boise State's Spencer Danielson would be a home run hire to get the Noles back to where they want to be.

But, of course, Florida State needs to find a new AD first.

Then, after that, they have to actually fire Norvell, a prospect that might not be as simple as just pulling the plug given his exorbitant buyout.

There are a lot of problems in Tallahassee right now, but there are plenty of solutions as well.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

I'm not so sure hiring Jimbo Fisher is one of them.

World.title: EXCLUSIVE: Inside Vance's intimate Capitol Hill huddle as Republicans confront tough midterm terrain

EXCLUSIVE: Vice President JD Vance energized Republicans during a huddle on Capitol Hill Tuesday where he urged lawmakers to "kick a--" in the 49 days before the midterm elections, according to audio obtained by Fox News Digital from a person in the room.

He wants members of Congress who are on the campaign trail to tell Americans how Trump administration's policies benefit them daily.

"There's people out there right now whose lives are going to get better, or their lives are going to get worse based on whether we're in the majority or whether we're in the minority," Vance told the Republican lawmakers in spelling out the stakes of the 2026 midterms.

"There are going to be people who are going to be poorer. Who are going to be less able to afford their prescription drugs, who are going to be less safe in the homes in their neighborhoods if the other guys get the majority," he continued. "And there are people who are going to be able to walk down the street in safety if you guys keep the majority. If we keep the majority together."

Specifically, Vance told incumbents to hammer home the issue of crime, noting that the homicide rate has reached a 126-year low. Vance explained that in a country of 330 million people, that crime stat translates to "thousands of people," including mothers and fathers, who are coming home to their families instead of being victims of deadly crimes.

FBI REPORTS LARGEST DROP IN VIOLENT CRIME AND MURDER SINCE 1937 AS HOMICIDES FALL MORE THAN 18%

"There are tens of thousands of children who will come home tonight and work on their homework with mom or dad, rather than a stranger, because of what we've been able to do in supporting law enforcement," Vance said in the closed-door meeting.

"This is not an abstraction, ladies and gentlemen," the vice president continued. "This is not about what you see on CNN or Fox News. This is not whether someone with an 'R' or a 'D' next to their name wins. This is about whether the American people in this country that we love have a government that they deserve, that protects them, that fights for them, or whether they have a government that treats them as a means to end."

Fox News Digital caught up with Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., after the meeting.

"I think he did a great job," the congressman said. "He's very good. He's very personable."

"He's got some kind of voodoo thing going on where he remembers everybody's dadgum name," Burchett told Fox News Digital. "It kind of freaks me out a little bit. But, I mean, every time I've run into him — I remember one time I was waiting in line to go to the bathroom and he walked out of the bathroom. 'Hey, Tim, what's going on?' I invited him to a [University of Tennessee] game."

Vance offered some campaign tips to the lawmakers while ribbing the political consulting class for sometimes being out of touch, and saying "the American people are not dumb."

He said voters understand President Donald Trump and his administration inherited problems, including inflation, massive debt and "a country that was weaker on the national stage."

"They know that Rome wasn't built in a day," he said.

THE ONE LINE FROM JD VANCE’S GOP KEYNOTE THAT REVEALS HIS VISION FOR AMERICA

The vice president directed members to "pound the pavement" in their home districts to personally connect with as many voters as possible.

Just as importantly, Vance said, Republicans in safe districts who have no real opposition from the left should contribute money to the campaigns of fellow Republicans who are in competitive districts.

"So here's the thing, this is not rocket science. You guys know this better than I do, you know your districts better than I do," Vance said . "We know that most voters, particularly the voters who are open-minded, who are not hardcore partisans, they don't really start paying attention to the election until right about now."

THUNE-ALIGNED GROUPS UNLEASH HISTORIC WAR CHEST TO DEFEND SENATE MAJORITY: 'WINNING MESSAGE'

Vance also spoke fondly of when late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina joined him in Ohio while he was campaigning for the Senate in 2022.

"I'll never forget this," said Vance. " Lindsey Graham comes out — I didn't know Lindsey Graham at all, and you guys know how the campaign trail is in the final stretches. You wake up in a crappy hotel, you haven't seen your wife, your kids in a few days, and it's a lot more fun when you have some company out there."

"You're telling jokes, you're enjoying it. That energy — people pick up on it. So, get out there and campaign with your friends."

Vance recalled how Graham told him stories that had him "aching with laughter," half of which he said he could not repeat.

World.title: Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz's 'effective altruism' network tied to AI regulation push
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Concerns about artificial intelligence spelling doom for the human race are being linked to a "cult-like" philanthropy movement known as "effective altruism" supported by billionaire Democratic megadonor and Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz, according to a policy analyst.

In response to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation announcement on X, Parker Thayer, an investigative researcher at Capital Research Center in Washington D.C., went viral as he raised questions about whether the resignation was part of a broader network that aims to influence lawmakers and AI policy.

"I resigned from Anthropic today," Coxon’s post read. "I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives."

RESEARCHER WHO DEPARTED AI ROLE OVER FEARS OF RACING INTO EXTINCTION SAYS PEOPLE ARE 'BEGGING' FOR REGULATION

Thayer quoted the post in a response that received interaction online with top lawmakers in Congress, including Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

"This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion," Thayer posted. "The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting."

Thayer echoed claims made by White House AI advisor David Sacks that AI fears are overblown and potentially based on political motives.

"I think this is becoming a panic," Sacks told CBS News correspondent Jo Ling Kent. "We're in an election season, and there is an incentive for political actors to try and amplify the fear. And I think this is a moment to really calm down a little bit and look at the issue rationally."

SEN. BERNIE SANDERS: YES, WE MUST HIT THE PAUSE BUTTON ON AI BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE

Coxon told Fox News’ Bret Baier last week that we are "on the doorstep of tremendous discoveries," but are running in too quickly. He emphasized the need for moderation.

Baier asked Coxon if the issue could be figured out.

"I think definitely. I think if we actually try instead of submitting to the inevitability of a doomed race or a hubristic gamble, then we can solve it," he said. "The problem is not unsolvable."

TOP MEDIA OUTLETS FAIL TO DISCLOSE WHO IS BANKROLLING THEIR AI REPORTERS

Coxon said he was acting alone when deciding to voice his concerns about the direction of AI, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Fox News Digital sat down with Thayer to ask about his theories concerning the coordination behind Coxon's "sophisticated" resignation, which was in turn met with a slew of national television interviews and immediate notoriety. Almost overnight, Coxon's post became a major point of policy debate spanning across political parties and politicians, including President Donald Trump and socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Thayer did not offer a theory for which individuals or groups might have coordinated with Coxon, who has denied such claims. But Thayer said the "AI doomerism movement" is associated with "effective altruism," a philosophy he described as "cult-like."

OPINION: REP. TED LIEU: AI IS ALREADY TOO POWERFUL. WE NEED A KILL SWITCH BEFORE DISASTER STRIKES

According to the Centre for Effective Altruism, the movement is defined as a "project that aims to find the best ways to help others and put them into practice."

But Thayer noted that while the philanthropic movement may sound high-minded, Silicon Valley elites and members who donate and support "effective altruism" may have much more direct political goals in mind.

Thayer did not have evidence that any individuals or groups connected to the effective altruism movement provided public relations or other support for Coxon’s post about his resignation.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna have been leading financial backers of organizations associated with the "effective altruism" movement.

The couple founded Coefficient Giving, formerly known as Open Philanthropy, and remain its "main funders," according to the organization. Tuna serves as its president.

Coefficient Giving says its artificial intelligence work has expanded rapidly, with $168 million committed to AI safety, security and field-building in 2024 and $351 million in 2025 — a combined $519 million. The organization says it is on track to commit more than $1 billion to AI policy advocacy in 2026.

In a 2021 grant application description, the organization cited that it seeks "to fund programs and events in a variety of areas of interest to Coefficient Giving — including effective altruism, global catastrophic risks, biosecurity, AI for epistemics, forecasting, and other areas."

Moskovitz, who Forbes estimates has a net worth of roughly $10 billion, contributed more than $50 million to support the Biden-Harris campaign from 2020 to 2024, including $46.89 million to the Future Forward PAC, which served as the main fundraising vessel for the failed presidential campaign.

TRUMP UNLOADS ON TECH TITANS PUSHING FOR SLOWDOWN ON EMERGING INDUSTRY: ‘WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!’

On Monday, the Department of War Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering posted to X: "Americanism, not effective altruism. The United States will continue to be AI DOMINANT!"

As for the reasoning behind "effective altruism’s" commitment to the artificial intelligence policy space, Thayer said the fearmongering technique is comparable to the climate change narrative that has been traditionally peddled by the Democratic Party.

"They basically just say kind of in the same vein as climate change activists like Al Gore used to, they kind of just make bombastic doomsday projections without citing really a whole lot of easily discernible evidence and just expect us to trust their expertise," Thayer explained.

"First, they got you scared of the data centers based on a bunch of sketchy arguments about water pollution supposedly, and supposedly raising your electric prices, which don't seem to actually be true," he added. "And now they're getting you scared of the actual AI that the data centers are being used to launch."

Thayer said that if AI critics were truly afraid of a potential doomsday scenario, they would be advocating for the extinction of artificial intelligence altogether. Instead, he says that it is a tactic to increase the government’s power over the industry while also acting in their own interest so "that they're the only ones who are allowed to build it."

In an opinion piece published in Medium in 2024, Moskovitz noted that he was concerned about the potential risks AI poses, saying that a potential doomsday "situation may develop extremely quickly."

"Contrary to the popular narrative about effective altruists working in AI, my interest in mitigating the potential risks isn’t rooted in specific predictions about the far future, but rather simple concern about the next few decades, when I and the people I care about are still alive to care about what happens," he wrote.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-LA, said a meeting at the White House to discuss AI policy could happen before the end of this week or the next. Trump also weighed in on the AI outlook in a post to Truth Social on Monday.

"The people that say AI is going to destroy the World, and that Data Centers are bad for your neighborhood, are the same people that said, just a short time ago, that the World would be extinguished by "Climate Change." That HOAX never worked out for them, and now they’re on to the next one."

World.title: Kamala Harris viciously mocked with resurfaced bumbling 'two words' explanation of AI after desperate call
