World.title: Tallinn Fringe Festival 2026 now into its last week
World.content:
The Tallinn Fringe Festival (TFF) 2026 is into its final week now with performances running across the city until Friday.

This year's festival is the 10th and features comedy, theater, music, dance, circus and cabaret, with both international and Estonian artists appearing. The closing days offer audiences a last chance to see this year's stars.

Festival director Dan Renwick was hard at work publicizing the event through a series of personal challenges, including a Marathon "Joggle" — running and juggling simultaneously — with split across two half marathons in Helsinki and Tallinn.

TFF organizer Dan Renwick during the 'joggle' to raise awareness of fringe. Source: Tallinn Fringe Festival.

"I wanted to find a slightly ridiculous way to draw some attention to the Fringe and encourage people to support what we're doing," Renwick said of his challenge. "It's been great to see people getting behind it, and if the challenges have made even a few more people curious about Tallinn Fringe or inspired them to support the festival, then it's been worth it," he went on.

Audiences can also support the festival directly during its final week. Financial support helps Tallinn Fringe continue providing performance opportunities for artists and bringing international acts to the city. Details are available from the festival's website.

Audience at the Post Punk Cabaret Part 2, Dark and Kinky. Source: Darja Liiv

TFF is an open-access festival, with performances staged in bars, theaters, clubs and other venues across the city. Its program is created through collaboration between artists and venues, allowing visitors to build their own festival experience. This year's event started August 18 and runs exactly one month, to this coming Friday, September 18.

The full remaining itinerary and ticket information are available on the Tallinn Fringe website here.

World.title: 'Way of Being' motto of 2028 Song and Dance Celebration
World.content:
Starting September 15, all groups wishing to take part in the 14th Youth Song and Dance Celebration and the 29th Song Celebration and 22nd Dance Celebration, "Olemise viis," in 2028 can register to participate.

Margus Toomla, a member of the management board of the Estonian Song and Dance Celebration Foundation, said the 2028 celebration will be exceptional, as it will bring together the traditions of the Youth Song and Dance Celebration and the general Song and Dance Celebration for the first time in history. This time, the celebration will last a total of two weeks, from June 30 to July 9. "The first week of the celebration will focus on the Dance Celebration and Folk Music Celebration, while the second will be devoted to the procession and Song Celebration."

Although the program is extensive and the celebration will be considerably longer than usual, Toomla is confident everything will run smoothly and that the wide-ranging program will give more people an opportunity to attend one of the Dance Celebration performances or Song Celebration concerts. He said the Folk Music Celebration's more spacious venue at the Estonian Open Air Museum will offer plenty of opportunities to experience the celebration in an authentic setting.

The major celebration's theme "Olemise viis" ("Way of Being" or "Tune of Being") ties the Song, Dance and Folk Music celebrations together into a conceptual whole. Song Celebration artistic director Riivo Jõgi said the phrase "Olemise viis" is appealingly ambiguous, allowing considerable freedom both artistically and philosophically. "Since the Youth and general Song Celebrations will be held together this time and the celebration will last three days, an axis of past, present and future emerged quite naturally."

He explained that the first day will look back in time, with participants jointly performing music that has resonated with people in Estonia over different decades. "This will be a special concert because the audience will be able to sing along with the choir for a large part of it. There has been communal singing at the Song Celebration before, but this time an entire concert has been built around it. The second day will belong to adult singers, while children and young people will take the stage under the Song Festival Grounds' arch on the third day."

"'Olemise viis' will bring the meanings of being Estonian and coming together to the Song Festival Grounds through our shared history. I hope these three days will genuinely form a single whole and that people will leave the celebration thinking about where we come from, what unites us here in Estonia and what we want to carry forward into the future," Jõgi said.

World.title: Two longtime tenants parting ways with Tartu's legendary Genialistide Klubi
World.content:
Tartu's Genialistide Klubi is facing a shake-up as longtime subtenants Must Kast theater and Möku Bar plan to move out, citing the venue's uncertain future and desire to grow.

Must Kast and Möku have both been mainstays at the self-described "subcultural" center for more than a decade, but say that uncertainty about Genialistide Klubi's future, along with plans to grow, prompted their respective decisions to move.

Genialistide Klubi, which has been located at Magasini 5 since 2008, has faced noise complaints from neighbors for nearly a year and a half. Although it has taken steps to reduce the noise, they have not yet been sufficient for the City of Tartu to release nearly €45,000 in program funding, leaving the club without that annual municipal support this year.

Must Kast is moving across town to the Estonian National Museum (ERM), with its first performances at its new home scheduled for early October. Director Merilyn Elge said the theater's needs have changed considerably over the years, particularly in terms of technical capacity and stability.

"We feel that Genialistide Klubi can no longer meet those needs," Elge said. "Over the past year, there have been so many questions hanging over the place, and no one has been able to answer them."

Möku Bar at Genialistide Klubi. Source: ERR

Möku, which first announced its plans to move late last week, plans to reopen at the Sisevete Saatkond, a historic river barge docked on the Emajõgi at Vabaduse puiestee 5, by mid-December.

"We like running a boring bar where people can come for no reason," co-owner Kaarel Jõudvald said. "Genialistide Klubi is a cultural and events venue."

He added that the move, the bar's second since relocating to the club from Rüütli tänav in 2015, will also give Genialistide Klubi a chance to try running its own bar.

'We're looking for meaningful partners'

Möku's revenue has covered a large share of Genialistide Klubi's rent. Even so, manager Juhan Kari said the club expects to find new operators and continue serving as a platform for emerging cultural projects.

"A subcultural center is by nature constantly changing, and Genklubi has been a creative incubator all these years," Kari said. "We're not merely looking for tenants to fill the space or sell beer; we're looking for partners who bring something meaningful to the table."

Several interested parties have already reached out to the club, he added, but it's still too soon to provide any details.

Outdoor courtyard at Tartu's Genialistide Klubi. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

Genialistide Klubi also still expects to secure this year's earmarked municipal funding after making some changes to its program. August noise measurements fell within permitted limits, putting the city in a position to release the funding.

"The exact amount will depend on the application Genialistide Klubi submits, how many events have taken place and how many are planned," said Tartu Department of Culture director Sten Svetljakov.

The city, he added, will meet with the club Wednesday to discuss further.

Founded in 2006 by members of the eponymous Estonian band Genialistid, Genialistide Klubi first opened its doors at the former Lutsu Theater House nearby, which now houses Tartu Toy Museum's Theater House.

The club relocated to its present home on Magasini tänav two years later.

World.title: Datasel seeks resolution in Estonia ammunition dispute
World.content:
India‑owned Datasel says it is ready to resolve a dispute over ammunition deliveries and meet Estonia's quality and quantity requirements, according to a proposal sent to the government and the Ministry of Defense.

The Italian company with Indian owners, Datasel, sent a proposal to the government, the Ministry of Defense and the Center for Defense Investment (RKIK), stating that it wishes to resolve the situation constructively and is prepared to deliver all ammunition specified in the contract. The letter was addressed to all ministers, including Prime Minister Kristen Michal, RKIK director Elmar Vaher, two other officials, and 17 members of parliament.

In the letter, the company outlines steps for reaching a solution.

"Datasel's position is clear: we remain willing and prepared to complete the contractual supply. Our objective is not to prolong the present dispute, but to establish a practical framework that protects the interests of Estonia, objectively addresses the outstanding technical and contractual matters, and enables the underlying defence procurement requirement to be fulfilled," the letter states.

The company added that it has already taken significant financial commitments and organized supply chains to fulfill the contract. "Significant resources have been committed towards raw materials, components, manufacturing and associated procurement activities necessary for completion of the supply," Datasel noted.

According to Datasel, it is able to fulfill its contractual obligations immediately once the financing framework is set. The company is willing to agree on a schedule with Estonian authorities and ensure transparency in production, inspection and delivery.

Estonian authorities have said that the ammunition delivered so far by Datasel was of poor quality. Datasel says it is ready to ensure that the ammunition meets Estonia's required standards.

"Datasel's objective is not simply to complete the outstanding quantities, but to complete them through a controlled and verifiable process capable of providing Estonia with confidence in the material ultimately delivered," the company stated.

Datasel says it is willing to cooperate with the relevant Estonian agencies to ensure quality control, inspection and testing according to specific requirements before further deliveries are made.

In the letter, Datasel proposes that representatives of the Estonian government and RKIK begin dialogue immediately to reach an agreement. First, a decision must be made regarding the ammunition already delivered, and it should receive an independent technical assessment. What happens with the remaining deliveries must be agreed together, including how inspection, testing, acceptance and documentation will be carried out.

Datasel also wants both sides to work toward resolving contractual and legal disagreements. For this, the company proposes forming a joint working group to handle technical, contractual, financial and logistical details and prepare a roadmap and timeline for moving forward.

The letter also notes that although Datasel does not withdraw its positions in the ongoing legal dispute, these disagreements should not prevent both sides from seeking a mutually acceptable solution through dialogue. "Datasel therefore respectfully expresses its readiness to engage directly with the appropriate representatives of the Government of Estonia and RKIK," the letter states.

Background

In 2024, the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) signed four procurement contracts with Datasel S.R.L., an Italian company acquired earlier that year by Indian-owned Neco Defence Munitions. Despite neither Datasel nor its parent firm having any prior track record of manufacturing or selling artillery shells, RKIK wired roughly €70 million in advance payments.

The contracts meant to deliver desperately needed ammunition to Ukraine using EU European Peace Facility funding suffered severe delivery delays. Ammunition that did arrive was flagged as incomplete and of substandard quality, leading RKIK to terminate the agreements and launch legal efforts to recoup the money. Datasel has denied wrongdoing, claiming it delivered tens of millions of euros' worth of goods and was left with financial losses.

The European Public Prosecutor's Office has since launched an investigation into the use of European Peace Facility funds by Estonia.

The scandal was part of Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur's recent decision to resign, alongside wider accounting and oversight issues at the Estonian Defense Forces and other parts of the ministry's administrative area.

World.title: Iraq signs Energy Cooperation Agreement’s fourth phase with Siemens
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz oversaw on Tuesday the signing ceremony for the fourth phase of the Energy Cooperation Agreement between the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and Siemens.

The agreement that marks the progression into phase four of the ongoing long-term energy strategic partnership was signed as part of al-Zaidi’s trip to Europe.

The ongoing partnership aims to modernize Iraq’s power sector, build highly efficient generation capacities, and expand transmission and distribution networks throughout the country.

In August 2025, the Iraqi cabinet adopted the fundamentals of an energy cooperation strategy with Germany-based Siemens Energy.

Siemens has previously been engaged in electricity projects in Iraq, including long-term service contracts for three power plants in 2023 as part of larger energy cooperation efforts. Siemens also signed an agreement to improve Iraq’s electricity infrastructure in the same year.

Iraq relies heavily on natural gas supplies from Iran to generate electrical power and frequently experiences electricity outages. These outages worsen during the summer months when temperatures exceed 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) in different parts of the country.

To address the country’s increasing energy demand, the Iraqi government is collaborating with Siemens to develop new power plants with a total capacity of 14,000 megawatts.

The new power plants are expected to use local fuel and combined cycle technology, increasing production efficiency and lessening reliance on imported fuel.

Iraq’s electricity grid is experiencing a daily shortage of over 35,000 megawatts due to restricted fuel availability for power plants and a reduction in some external supply sources. In early August, output was barely 24,600 megawatts.

Demand in the summer fluctuates between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, exacerbating the supply imbalance and causing continued operational issues for the system. Production levels rely on gas supplies from Iran, which stand at around 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraq may import LNG from French company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is exploring new avenues to secure fuel for its power plants, with the Ministry of Electricity seeking to diversify its gas sources.

The endeavor includes a preliminary agreement with a French company to discuss the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and its regasification within the country in the coming phase.

The Electricity Ministry said on Monday that Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Wahib signed a preliminary agreement in Paris with TotalEnergies to supply LNG to power plants in Iraq.

The step comes as Iraq seeks to reduce its reliance on limited gas sources and secure a more stable fuel supply for its power plants, thereby increasing electricity supply hours and providing the Ministry of Electricity with additional options during upcoming negotiations with suppliers.

The agreement establishes a framework for discussions and negotiations regarding the potential delivery of LNG via a floating platform that would dock at Iraqi ports in Basra. The LNG would then be regasified and injected into the Iraqi national grid.

The agreement includes exploring the deployment of a floating platform to receive LNG shipments in Iraq and conduct regasification operations before transporting the fuel via the national gas pipeline network to power plants, according to the operational needs of the Iraqi grid.

The proposed approach seeks to enhance the flexibility of the fuel system, as LNG can serve as an additional source when necessary. This strategy also enables Iraqi authorities to evaluate the quantities, timing, and both commercial and technical terms prior to finalizing a binding agreement.

Under the initial memorandum of understanding, Iraq is continuing negotiations with the French company to finalize details regarding supplies, infrastructure, and regasification mechanisms.

This new endeavor aligns with another initiative focused on supplying LNG to the Khor Al-Zubair port in Basra. Baghdad has entered into an agreement with US-based Excelerate Energy to establish a regasification terminal that will operate independently.

World.title: ITEX IRAQ 2026 signs strategic media partnership with Al Shabab TV
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ITEX IRAQ 2026 has concluded a strategic media partnership with Al-Shabab TV, establishing an integrated broadcasting and digital coverage framework ahead of the country’s flagship information and communications technology summit.

The bilateral agreement aims to amplify the exhibition’s media reach and deliver comprehensive programming across both local and regional audiences, showcasing Iraq’s accelerating pivot toward modern digital infrastructure and public-sector technological transformation.

Scheduled to convene from September 30 to October 3, 2026, at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, ITEX IRAQ serves as the nation’s premier convergence point for telecommunications, enterprise IT, FinTech, cybersecurity, and digital governance.

Under the newly inked arrangement, the partnership pairs the multimedia broadcast network of Al-Shabab TV with the executive convening power of ITEX IRAQ 2026, creating an expanded promotional runway for participating multinational tech vendors, domestic startups, technical forums, and public-private initiatives shaping the country’s digital economy.

The expanded media coverage framework will track core milestone events across the four-day expo, including specialized panel sessions on emerging technologies, enterprise cloud modernization, artificial intelligence integration, and high-level regulatory forums.

By broadening multi-platform coverage, both entities seek to spotlight actionable investment opportunities and homegrown technological innovations, connecting institutional decision-makers with a wider demographic of young professionals, tech entrepreneurs, and regional commercial stakeholders.

World.title: Economist warns of demographic time bomb over Iraq youth unemployment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi economic expert Manar Al-Obeidi has warned of an impending demographic crisis facing the nation’s leadership, cautioning that a looming human time bomb could soon see millions of unemployed youth taking to the streets in widespread protests demanding jobs.

In a televised interview with journalist Muna Sami, Al-Obeidi grounded his warning in demographic findings from the Ministry of Planning’s recent nationwide census, which registered Iraq’s population at 47 million people and revealed that nearly half of the country is under the age of 25, while active participants in the workforce account for just 30 percent.

Al-Obeidi emphasized that over the next five to ten years, this massive youth cohort will reach prime working age, creating an unprecedented wave of job seekers that the public sector cannot absorb.

With state payrolls already saturated, federal institutions will have zero fiscal or administrative capacity to offer additional civil service appointments unless the government enacts radical economic restructuring to build productive industrial lines and real production capacities.

Consequently, Al-Obeidi argued, an inability to accommodate these incoming labor cohorts will inevitably trigger widespread social unrest as youth exercise their legitimate right to demand viable livelihoods.

Compounding this looming crisis is a structural paradox within the domestic economy: despite high unemployment figures, private-sector enterprises face chronic talent deficits.

Al-Obeidi observed that nearly every private firm, including his own organization, struggles to recruit qualified local personnel because the traditional public education system fails to equip graduates with modern, market-relevant competencies.

This systemic failure places accountability squarely on the Ministries of Education and Higher Education, whose outputs remain disconnected from private industry demands.

Under standard economic models, every one-percent expansion in a specific sector’s gross domestic product typically generates a two-percent rise in corresponding job opportunities.

However, Al-Obeidi pointed out that in Iraq, economic expansion frequently bypasses domestic labor entirely due to this widening skill deficit. In the booming residential real estate and construction sectors, developers have repeatedly turned to Egyptian, Turkish, and Iranian firms and laborers to fill operational needs, underscoring an acute domestic shortage of skilled technical talent capable of matching the execution standards required by modern infrastructure projects.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets German president in Berlin
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Berlin on Tuesday to discuss prospects for political, economic, and investment cooperation between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi is expected to hold discussions with representatives of 30 German companies to discuss investment opportunities and economic cooperation between Iraq and Germany, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The corporations participating in the discussion, which will address cooperation and investment partnerships between the two sides, expressed a strong desire to invest in Iraq.

The Iraqi prime minister’s discussions in Berlin will include finalizing several memoranda of understanding in the economic and investment sectors, strengthening the partnership between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany comes a day after he concluded a trip to the French capital, Paris, where he and President Emmanuel Macron oversaw the signing of six memoranda of understanding covering air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany is a significant step in the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen commercial ties with other nations and multinational enterprises.

The visit aims to attract foreign investment and utilize German expertise and technology to support Iraq’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq PM donates 47 billion dinars to renovate five Baghdad hospitals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Specialized engineering teams have initiated extensive rehabilitation and modernization works across five major public hospitals in Baghdad, financed through personal donations provided by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, Minister of Health Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Mousawi disclosed that the Prime Minister contributed 47 billion Iraqi dinars out of his personal funds to underwrite the long-overdue infrastructure upgrades after engineering assessments confirmed an absolute absence of allocated state budget lines for the capital projects.

The structural renovation campaign spans anchor healthcare institutions across the capital, comprising Baghdad Hospital within the Medical City complex, Al-Kadhimiya Teaching Hospital, Al-Kindi Hospital, Al-Yarmouk Hospital, and Al-Zafraniya Hospital.

In addition to covering the full 47-billion-dinar reconstruction bill, Al-Mousawi revealed that Al-Zaidi personally donated $2 million directly to the Ministry of Health to procure an essential, life-saving pharmaceutical supply that faced severe procurement delays due to funding shortfalls, allowing specialized medical crews to begin immediate rehabilitation works across the designated hospital wards.

Al-Mousawi explained that publicly spotlighting these targeted private contributions serves to cultivate broader philanthropic and civic engagement, urging corporate institutions and private-sector actors to step forward and assist in rebuilding the country’s burdened healthcare architecture.

The health minister highlighted that this collaborative model has already yielded tangible support from the Association of Private Hospitals, which responded by significantly expanding its corporate social responsibility commitments, pledging to conduct 10 specialized surgical procedures free of charge each month, well exceeding the initial civic target of four surgeries.

World.title: Iraqi PM to sign crucial economic deals during trip to Germany
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi will hold important discussions with German officials during his visit to Berlin.

The discussions will include finalizing several agreements and memoranda of understanding in the economic and investment sectors, strengthening the partnership between Iraq and Germany, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Germany represents a crucial step in the Iraqi government’s efforts to enhance economic relationships with other countries and international businesses.

The visit aims to attract foreign investment and leverage German expertise and technology to foster Iraq’s development.

The talks will focus on collaboration in the energy, industry, infrastructure, transportation, water, and service sectors, as well as strategies to boost the capabilities of the private sector and increase Germany’s engagement in Iraq’s major initiatives.

The expected agreements will create new opportunities for German investments and facilitate the execution of economically viable development projects.

The step aligns with the government’s efforts to diversify its economic resources and lessen reliance on revenue from oil exports.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany comes a day after he concluded a trip to the French capital, Paris, where he and President Emmanuel Macron oversaw the signing of six memoranda of understanding covering air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

World.title: Iraq postpones start of 2026–2027 academic year to October 11
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Education announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the postponement of the official start of the 2026–2027 academic year to Sunday, October 11, pushing back the previously scheduled launch date of September 20.

According to an official statement issued by the Media Office of the Minister of Education and carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Minister Abdul Karim Abtan Al-Jubouri issued the directive to grant administrative and teaching cadres the operational bandwidth needed to conclude second-round examination cycles for non-terminating grades and finalize campus preparations nationwide.

The ministerial directive also incorporated seasonal climate considerations, citing prevailing high temperatures across the country as a primary factor behind the delay to ensure student health and classroom safety.

Ministry officials underscored that the additional three-week window will be utilized to wrap up logistical, technical, and administrative arrangements, enabling local directorates across all governorates to complete physical facility upgrades and coordinate school readiness before millions of pupils and students officially resume classes across Iraq.

World.content:
Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle. (Reuters file photo)

NEW DELHI: Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle will in New Delhi for a two-day visit from Thursday for talks on post-flood reconstruction and wider economic cooperation as Kathmandu looks to India for support after the Aug 26 disaster devastated hydropower projects, roads, bridges and settlements and left the country facing a rebuilding bill of up to $5 billion. The visit will be the first high-level trip from Nepal to India since the floods.Wagle is expected to meet finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal during the visit. He will also address an industry gathering and deliver a lecture at Delhi School of Economics.The disasterâs confirmed toll has reached 1,429 dead and more than 5,649 missing across Nepal and Tibet â 1,386 dead and more than 5,130 missing in Nepal, and 43 dead and 519 missing in Tibet. Wagle has estimated that Nepal may need as much as $5 billion for rebuilding and rehabilitation. âWe will require much less than what we needed for the 2015 earthquake. Loss and damage is being assessed,â he said.He has also said govt has enough resources for immediate rescue and relief but will need substantial outside support for reconstruction. âThe next phase will focus on early recovery, including temporary shelters and cash-for-work programmes,â Wagle said.âThis will be followed by the daunting task of reconstruction.âIndia has already emerged as one of Nepalâs key partners in the immediate response, sending nearly 50 tonnes of relief material, including medicines, temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits and solar lamps, while Indian teams also joined specialised rescue efforts in flood-hit areas. New Delhi later approved export of up to 654MW of electricity for 18 hours a day until Dec 31 after damage to Nepalâs hydropower network forced Kathmandu to halt power exports and turn to imports.India has also begun supplying Bailey bridges to restore road connectivity severed by the floods, with components for the first 70-metre bridge reaching Nepal for deployment in the Betrawati area. India has provided three such bridges and pledged more as Nepal works to reconnect settlements cut off after floods washed away or damaged dozens of road and pedestrian crossings in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

World.title: If BJP wins Nagaon, party will secure all 126 Assam seats in 2031: Himanta Biswa Sarma
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarm on Tuesday made a big claim that BJP could win all 126 assembly seats in the state in the 2031 Vidhan Sabha elections if it wins the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll scheduled for October 6.

Speaking at a presser, BJP leader Sarma said Nagaon has not traditionally been a BJP stronghold but claimed that the party has seen a "visible change" in its favour over the past month.

The Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency has eight assembly segments. Sarma said the BJP won four of them -- Morigaon, Raha, Jagiroad and Nagaon-Batadraba -- by around 50,000 votes each in the 2026 assembly polls. The opposition won the remaining four -- Rupohihat, Laharighat, Dhing and Samaguri -- by margins of more than 1.5 lakh votes each.

"Let us wait for the bypoll results... If the BJP manages to win this Lok Sabha seat, then the party will secure all 126 assembly constituencies in the 2031 polls," he said.

Sarma said the political mood in the constituency was shifting towards the BJP and claimed the partyâs position was improving with each passing day.

"Even before the elections were announced, many people joined the BJP even in constituencies where we do not have MLAs," he added.





Asked about the oppositionâs prospects, the chief minister said his focus was on the BJP-led alliance rather than individual opposition leaders.

"I am not interested in either AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal or Congress's Gaurav Gogoi but only in the BJP-AGP-BPF alliance. We will continue to do good work and people will be in our favour."

However, Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi expressed confidence that the party would win the upcoming Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election, saying the Congress would mount a strong campaign.

Speaking to reporters, Gogoi said, "We are very confident of putting up a solid campaign, and we are confident of a victory in the forthcoming Nagaon by-election."

Reacting to reports that AIUDF may field its president Badruddin Ajmal in the bypoll, Gogoi said the move reflected the Congressâ strong position in the constituency.

World.title: Delhi, 5 states sign agreement for Kishau multi-purpose project; to augment drinking water supply for national capital
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Five states and Union Territory of Delhi on Tuesday signed an agreement on the long-pending Kishau Project, which is expected to regulate water availability in the wider Yamuna basin and increase flows downstream, benefitting the national capital and Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan in one way or another.

The water stored in the Kishau reservoir will augment drinking water supply for Delhi.

The Kishau multi-purpose project is a proposed dam and hydropower project on the Tons river, a major tributary of the river Yamuna, flowing along the border of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Besides supplying drinking water, the multi-purpose project will also provide irrigation water for 97,000 hectares of land in riparian states and generate 1,476 million units of hydroelectric power.

The agreement was signed here by all six chief ministers in the presence of Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah, who said the Centre and the chief ministers of these six states/UTs of Yamuna basin are committed to complete the project at the earliest.

Calling it a âhistoric agreementâ, Shah said Delhi will be the biggest beneficiary of the project and it will also contribute to environmental conservation by ensuring environmental flow of river Yamuna.





Under the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement, an around 232-metre-high concrete gravity dam will be constructed on Tons. It will have a water storage capacity of 1,562 million cubic metres.

Shah said the Centre that declared the Kishau Multipurpose Project a ânational projectâ will bear approximately 90% of its financial burden, while the remaining 10% will be borne by the participating states in accordance with the 1994 agreement.

Shah, on the occasion, recalled the signing of several other agreements on water issues and said that the period from 2018 to 2026 will be remembered as a period in which almost all water disputes, from Kashmir to Uttar Pradesh, were resolved. The foundation for these resolutions was laid in meetings of the Zonal Councils and the Ministry of Jal Shakti efficiently took these agreements forward, he added.

World.title: How fish has BJP's plate full in West Bengal
World.content:
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple on the occasion of 'Kaushiki Amavasya' and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao'.

Interestingly, the timing of the visit gave the ritual a political context.

The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. As expected, the remarks kicked up a political storm, forcing the BJPâs Bengal unit to publicly distinguish itself from Dhirendra Shastriâs position on food.

Chief minister Adhikari, who had shared a stage with Shastri earlier this month and invited him to establish a centre in Bengal, then got into the balancing act.

âA religious figure is entitled to express his opinion, but whether people accept it or not is a personal matter,â the chief minister said after his Kalighat visit.

Adhikari also referred to his own practices, saying he follows a sattvik diet on Ashtami and during Kartik, while accepting fish offered to Goddess Kali as bhog and goat meat as prasad.





"A saint or a religious leader is entitled to express their opinion. People may choose to accept it or not. On Mahashtami, when I worship Maa Durga, I consume sattvik food. During the month of Kartik also, I consume sattvik food. At the same time, as a Bengali, I accept the bhog offered to Maa with fish. I also accept the prasad of goat sacrifice. Today, whatever was offered to Maa in the afternoon, the temple priests gave me the same.

There was fish head and fried fish, along with basanti pulao," he said.

From Liluah to Kalighat

All this began on September 4, when Adhikari shared the stage with Shastri at a Hanumant Katha programme at the Liluah Workshop Ground in Howrah.

Dhirendra Shastri on Durga Puja.

Addressing Shastri, Adhikari said: "Baba Maharaj Ji, please open a centre here. There should also be a Bageshwar Dham centre. This is the land of saints and of spiritual awakening."

Two days later, on September 6, Shastri appealed to Hindus in Bengal not to sell, cook or eat non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja idols during Navratri.

He described those consuming such food as "pakhandi" and called for opposition to the practice.

"I am appealing to the Hindus of Bengal, that during Navratri, even if you don't keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell or consume non-veg near the idols. I do not like it when dirty non-vegetarian food is eaten during Durga Puja and at gatherings linked to the festivities. I want the Hindus of Kolkata to awaken and boycott such people.

These people cannot be considered religious; they are pakhandi (hypocrites). Wake up and expel those people," he appealed.

BJP pushback

The remarks triggered criticism from the opposition and prompted the Bengal BJP to distance itself from the dietary prescription.

State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said no one could decide what Bengalis should eat.

"How can Bengalis not have fish and meat?" he said, adding that people in Bengal would continue with their traditional food practices.

He also invoked Swami Vivekananda while defending the consumption of meat and fish in Bengalâs religious traditions.

BJP dismissed all anxieties over Durga Puja.

Other BJP leaders, including Dilip Ghosh, also said food choices were a matter of personal preference and referred to the place of meat in some Bengali religious traditions.

The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also found itself navigating the controversy following statements made during an interactive session with Kolkata puja organizers.

Swami Nirgunananda, a member of the VHP's central advisory council, had suggested that non-vegetarian food stalls be kept away from the immediate area around Durga idols and situated in designated spaces outside pandals to maintain sanctity and cleanliness.

When his comments were interpreted as an official organisational diktat restricting meat sales, VHP International president Alok Kumar issued a formal clarification.

"Vishva Hindu Parishad has not issued any directions regarding the arrangements at Durga Puja pandals... worship of the Goddess should take place according to tradition and the atmosphere should be one of love and devotion," it said.

The Kalighat temple is associated with Bengal's 'Shakta' tradition, in which offerings can include fish and meat. The bhog included several varieties of fish, along with other vegetarian dishes and goat meat.

That tradition sits somewhat differently from the vegetarian dietary practices associated with Navratri in several parts of north and west India.

The not-so-new âmaach-bhaatâ row

The controversy over Shastri's remarks comes months after fish and meat had already become part of the BJP-TMC contest over Bengali identity during the assembly election campaign.

Mamata Banerjee repeatedly alleged during the campaign that a BJP government would restrict what Bengalis could eat.

At a rally in Purulia on March 29, she said: "BJP says can't eat fish, meat, eggs." She subsequently argued that restrictions on meat and fish sales in some BJP-ruled states showed what could lie ahead for Bengal.

The issue became prominent enough for senior BJP leaders to address it directly. Amit Shah clarified that "consumption of fish, eggs will not be stopped" if the BJP came to power in Bengal, calling Mamata's claim a rumour.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi also sought to engage with the issue, though from a different direction. At a rally in Haldia, he spoke about Bengal's fish production and said the state could become self-sufficient in fish under a BJP government. "In 15 years, TMC couldn't even give you fish. We created a separate ministry for fisheries," he said, contrasting Bengal's production with that of Bihar and Assam.

The BJPâs campaign also included more visible efforts to counter the perception that it was opposed to Bengali food habits.

Leaders publicly ate fish and meat, while BJP candidates and workers used fish in campaign imagery. On Poila Boishakh, TMC organised a "Maach-Bhaat-e-Bangali" procession, alleging that the BJP would impose restrictions on fish and meat.

The argument did not remain confined to the two parties. TMC leaders presented food as part of the broader question of Bengali identity. BJP leaders, in turn, sought to emphasise that dietary choices would remain a matter of personal freedom.

The Bengal and Bengali dilemma for Suvendu

Months after the BJP swept Bengal in assembly elections, the opposition has sought to use the same "outsider" charge to try and alienate the saffron party from the voters. Congress filed a police complaint against Shastri, alleging that his comments hurt Bengali sentiments, while invoking the âoutsiderâ argument that the TMC had used against the BJP during the election. Congressâs complaint described his remarks as an affront to Bengali traditions and social harmony.

The TMC, which had made fish and meat part of its cultural-identity campaign against the BJP, is also again using the remark against the party.

As CM, however, Adhikari has also taken a position on protests against Shastri.

On September 10, he directed the Kolkata Police commissioner to arrest those who allegedly burnt Shastriâs photographs during a protest in Bhawanipur. "Not in Bengal," he said, making clear that burning photographs as a form of protest would not be tolerated.

The move has produced another political contest. Congress has criticised the arrests and accused the government of protecting Shastri while acting against those protesting his remarks. One Congress leader, Atanu Das, was subsequently arrested.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The larger question for BJP

The recent row has brought an old question back for the BJP in Bengal: how does the party's Hindu politics sit with the state's own traditions?

Bengal has a strong Shakta tradition, centred on Kali and Durga.

In this tradition, the line between what is considered religious and what is considered non-vegetarian is not always drawn in the same way as it is in northern/western India. Fish, and in some places meat, can be part of offerings and rituals.

That makes food an unusually sensitive issue in Bengal. And for many Bengalis, it is tied to family customs, festivals and a sense of what is distinctly 'Bengali'.

Suvendu Adhikari is leading the first BJP government in Bengal. For now, he might be able to shut down critics by consuming fish bhog at Kalighat. But it will be interesting to see how he manages BJP's national Hindu politics in Bengal while also balancing the "Bengaliness".

World.title: 'Real' Sena case in SC: Shinde camp backs EC’s ‘organisational majority’ test
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Tuesday resumed final hearing on pleas challenging the Maharashtra Speakerâs refusal to disqualify MLAs of the Eknath Shinde-led

Uddhav Thackeray

factionâs challenge to the ECâs February 17, 2023, order allotting the Shiv Sena name and âbow-and-arrowâ symbol to the Shinde camp.

âEC can examine party structureâ

Senior advocate Neeraj Kishan Kaul, appearing for the Shinde faction, argued that the EC was empowered under Article 324 to examine a partyâs constitution and organisational structure while deciding which faction represented the real party.

âYour Lordships must see the entire record. The question is whether the constitution was with the Election Commission,â Kaul said.

He said the constitution relied upon by the Thackeray faction was not registered with the EC, while the 1999 constitution was submitted after detailed correspondence with the poll panel.

Kaul said the EC was not deciding which amendments could be made to the constitution but whether the organisational structure reflected the will of the party cadre.





âIt was a political party splitâ

Rejecting the argument that the dispute was limited to a split in the legislative wing, Kaul said, âOur case has never been that there was merely a split in the legislative party. Our case is that there was a split in the political party.â

He defended the ECâs organisational majority test, saying it could not conduct a referendum among every primary member of a political party.

âThe lifeblood of a political party is its cadre and grassroots workers who are directly connected to the electorate,â Kaul said.

The hearing remained inconclusive and will continue on Wednesday.

World.title: From jewellery to robots, 70-member Team India set for WorldSkills
World.content:
Worldskill Shangai 202â6â

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An eighth-pass jewellery trainee, a Class XI florist, a farmerâs son trained in refrigeration and young specialists in robotics, cyber security and Industry 4.0 will form Indiaâs unusually diverse challenge at the âOlympics of Skillsâ in Shanghai this month.India will field 70 competitors across 63 skill categories at WorldSkills 2026, scheduled from September 22 to 27. The contingent spans 16 states and brings together students, apprentices and young professionals trained in traditional trades as well as emerging technologies. The line-up, however, remains heavily male-dominated: only 14 of the 70 competitors are women.Karnataka has the largest representation with 16 contestants, followed by Odisha with 13 and Tamil Nadu with 12. Maharashtra has five competitors, while Bihar, Haryana, Telangana and Gujarat have three each.Among those heading to Shanghai is Md Dilkhush of Bihar, whose father is a farmer. Trained in refrigeration and air conditioning, Dilkhush emerged as the IndiaSkills national champion and will be tested on installation, maintenance, fault diagnosis and energy-efficient cooling systems.Tamil Naduâs Joy Das, son of a fisherman, studied till Class VIII and trained in jewellery-making before winning gold at the state and national levels.Mizoramâs Lawmnakima, a Class XI student, will compete in floristry, while Gujaratâs Prakash Suthar has followed his carpenter father into joinery.The contingent also reflects how vocational pathways are increasingly cutting across family and educational backgrounds. Anuja Vare of Karnataka, whose parents are doctors, will compete in visual merchandising. She has previously designed an exhibition space at Bharat Tex that was visited by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and won gold at the regional and national skill competitions.Telanganaâs Mehrunissa Begum moved from an apprenticeship in logistics and freight forwarding to successive gold medals at the state, regional and national levels. The daughter of a bakery owner and a homemaker, she has spoken of overcoming anxiety and the feeling of being overwhelmed during her competition journey.Smriti Nambiar of Karnataka, a bakery competitor trained at IHM Pusa, was named the instituteâs All-Rounder Student and Rising Culinarian for two consecutive years. Odishaâs Krishnanjali Sahoo will represent the country in patisserie and confectionery, while Jhansirani Rout will compete in restaurant service.The team also carries a strong green-skills component. Rajasthanâs Vishnu Prajapat, whose father is an electrician, will compete in renewable energy after gaining hands-on experience in solar installations and exposure to wind turbines. Rushikesh Pithambaram will represent India in water technology.At the technology end of the spectrum, the Indian contingent will compete in autonomous mobile robotics, cloud computing, cyber security, software testing, unmanned aerial systems, optoelectronics and robot systems integration. Mobile-app developer Arjun Vijayabashkar began coding at 12, while Industry 4.0 contestant Suhan Mascarenhas is the son of two employees of Isroâs Master Control Facility in Hassan.Maharashtraâs Harsh Pawar, whose father works as a quality supervisor at a cylinder-manufacturing company, will compete in 3D digital game art. Pawar has already won silver at the Global Skills Challenge in Australia. Two-member teams will represent India in areas such as autonomous mobile robotics, mechatronics, landscape gardening, concrete construction and robot systems integration.The 48th edition will open on September 22, with competitions running from September 23 to 26 and the closing ceremony on September 27. Participants will perform industry-standard assignments under the scrutiny of international experts. The event will also host a conference and industry exhibitions on technical education, workforce development and sustainable technologies.India will seek to improve on its WorldSkills Lyon 2024 performance, where it secured four bronze medals and 12 Medallions of Excellence.

World.title: Nepal finance min heads to India for flood repair talks as losses mount
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle will be in New Delhi for a two-day visit from Thursday for talks on post-flood reconstruction and wider economic cooperation as Kathmandu looks to India for support after the Aug 26 disaster devastated hydropower projects, roads, bridges and settlements.

It left the country facing a rebuilding bill of up to $5 billion. The visit will be the first high-level trip from Nepal to India since the floods.

Wagle is expected to meet finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal during the visit. He will also address an industry gathering and deliver a lecture at Delhi School of Economics.

The disasterâs confirmed toll has reached 1,429 dead and more than 5,649 missing across Nepal and Tibet â 1,386 dead and more than 5,130 missing in Nepal, and 43 dead and 519 missing in Tibet.

Wagle has estimated that Nepal may need as much as $5 billion for rebuilding and rehabilitation. âWe will require much less than what we needed for the 2015 earthquake. Loss and damage is being assessed,â he said.

He has also said govt has enough resources for immediate rescue and relief but will need substantial outside support for reconstruction. âThe next phase will focus on early recovery, including temporary shelters and cash-for-work programmes,â Wagle said.





âThis will be followed by the daunting task of reconstruction.â

India has already emerged as one of Nepalâs key partners in the immediate response, sending nearly 50 tonnes of relief material, including medicines, temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits and solar lamps, while Indian teams also joined specialised rescue efforts in flood-hit areas. New Delhi later approved export of up to 654MW of electricity for 18 hours a day until Dec 31 after damage to Nepalâs hydropower network forced Kathmandu to halt power exports and turn to imports.

India has provided three such bridges and pledged more as Nepal works to reconnect settlements cut off after floods washed away or damaged dozens of road and pedestrian crossings in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

World.title: 'BJP, RSS trying to impose Hindu law on non-Hindus': Owaisi on Amit Shah's UCC push
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

supremo

on Tuesday turned to the Constitution to counter Union home minister

's push to implement the

Uniform Civil Code

in all 21 NDA-ruled states by 2029. Hyderabad MP said that the Bhartiya Janata Party is using the proposed law to target Muslims and arguing that it could undermine key constitutional protections.

Speaking to the media in Bhopal, Owaisi said the proposed law would conflict with several provisions of the Constitution.

âThis is against Articles 25, 26, 14 and 29 of the Constitution, and you cannot implement such a law by abolishing freedom of religion,â AIMIM leader said.

His remarks came a day after he attacked Union home minister Amit Shah and the

BJP

over their push for the UCC.

Speaking to reporters in Hyderabad on Monday, Owaisi alleged that the BJP was not seeking the UCC in the interest of equality but to target Indiaâs Muslim population.

"First, you need to understand that the BJP is not pursuing the UCC for the sake of equality. They have introduced the UCC in their states and at the government level solely to target India's 18 crore Muslims; in doing so, the BJP and Amit Shah are acting in contravention of Articles 25 (Freedom of Religion), 14 (Right to Equality), 26, and 29 of the Indian Constitution. So, one must first grasp that this move by the BJP is not about equality; it is purely to target Muslims," Owaisi told reporters.





Owaisi also stressed that pluralism was central to Indiaâs identity and cited an earlier Law Commission report on the UCC.

"Secondly, the very soul and spirit of this country is pluralism. Thirdly, Amit Shah, the BJP, and the

RSS

are attempting to impose Hindu law upon non-Hindus. Fourthly, the Law Commission-constituted by the Modi government itself-stated in its report that the UCC is neither necessary nor desirable for India," the AIMIM chief said.

World.title: CPI(M)’s Keralam meet condemns ED action against Pinarayi, Veena, Riyas
World.content:
The three-day extended State committee meeting of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has condemned what it termed the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) bid to implicate Leader of the Opposition and Polit Bureau member Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter, T. Veena, and her husband and party State secretariat member P.A. Mohamed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case.

In a resolution passed on the concluding day of the meeting on Tuesday, the party said the “political witch-hunt” being conducted by the ED “will be strongly resisted both legally and politically.”

The resolution pointed out that [the now defunct] Exalogic Solutions Private Ltd., a company owned by Ms. Veena, and the CMRL engaged in a business transaction based on a legal agreement. During the period, the applicable income tax and Goods and Services Tax were paid, and the company received remuneration for the services provided through bank accounts.

The party alleged that the Income Tax Interim Settlement Board, in an arbitration application filed by the CMRL, unilaterally recorded a reference identifying a person as “the daughter of a prominent Kerala politician,” without hearing Exalogic or its owner. This itself was evidence of a politically motivated witch-hunt, the resolution said.

“That’s why the party gave a response then, calling out the Central government’s political witch-hunt. It has become clear now that the earlier stand taken by the party is valid, as additional agencies are being roped in for the investigation,” the resolution said.

The party alleged that the letter written by the ED to the State Police Chief seeking registration of a first information report against Mr. Vijayan, Ms. Veena and Mr. Riyas had many points earlier raised by Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan.

In another two resolutions, the meeting urged the people to rally against the anti-people policies of the Union and State governments.

World.title: RMP doctor arrested, 73 tramadol vials seized In Eluru district
World.content:
The Eluru district police on Tuesday arrested an RMP doctor, P. Nagendra Kumar, for allegedly possessing sedative injections.

Following the directions of Superintendent of Police K. Pratap Shiva Kishore, a police team led by Jangareddygudem Deputy Superintendent of Police B. H. Venkateshwarlu arrested the doctor in Kukunoor mandal and seized 73 Tramadol injection vials from his possession.

Earlier, the police had arrested four medical shop owners in connection with a racket involving the illegal sale of Tramadol injections and seized 880 injection vials from them.

World.title: Maratha quota stir: Jarange Patil leaves for Mumbai as police deny nod for protest
World.content:
Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil left for Mumbai with handful of supporters on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) to secure reservation for Marathas under the OBC category as the permission for protest was denied.

Mr. Jarange-Patil left from the place of protest, Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district, around 11 a.m. to reach Mumbai on September 19 and continue his indefinite hunger strike from Mumbai’s Azad Maidan, likely to mark the 19th day of his protest.

“The Mahayuti government has denied permission for protest in Mumbai. I will die or get reservation. I am travelling alone with two ambulances and two cars, with maximum 10 people,” he told media persons in Jalna.

While leaving from Antarwali Sarati, Mr. Jarange-Patil was seen consoling his family, saying “to stay strong” and “in case of his death, the brother should take care of his two daughters and wife”.

Mr. Jarange-Patil will hit Mumbai, when the city will be drowned in the celebration of Ganeshotsav festival, which started on September 14.

His arrival on September 16 will be the third protest staged in Mumbai for Marathi reservation in last three years. The first protest was led on the outskirts of Mumbai in the Vashi region of Navi Mumbai in January 2024; the second protest was held in August 2025, and this will be his third. He will be returning to Mumbai on Wednesday, demanding immediate issuance of Kunbi certificates, alleging that the government has been cancelling the issued certificates.

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has asked Mr. Jarange-Patil to reconsider his decision to protest in Mumbai, saying the protest during Ganeshotsav would cause inconvenience to devotees. Police had declined his application. Mr. Fadnavis said the 12 demands were met among the 13 demands. “We explained to him why his 13th demand could not be met as it doesn’t stand legally, and might harm the Maratha community,” the Chief Minister said.

Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister and Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde pointed out that last year at least 58 morchas took place but those never caused inconvenience to others. However, people on the other side should think what they were doing.

The original plan was to march along with thousands of supporters to Mumbai, starting from September 13. The first stop was Patoda in Beed, second stop in Shrigonda, Ahilyanagar, and the third stop in Hadapsar, Pune. However, now he will travel to Mumbai.

World.title: HSL helps 450 persons with disabilities in Vizianagaram
World.content:
Hindustan Shipyard Limited‘s (HSL) Chairman and Managing Director Rear Admiral Chandrasekharan Raghuram on Tuesday distributed artificial limbs, hearing aids, wheelchairs, tricycles to nearly 450 persons with disabilities at a programme organised by the Sri Gurudeva Charitable Trust at Mangalampalem in Kothavalasa mandal of Vizianagaram district.

Speaking on the occasion, he said that said that person with disabilities could do wonders if they receive adequate support from the society. He said that HSL would always extend its helping hand to support needy people under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities.

Trust founder Raparthi Raghubabu distributed rice bags and pensions to needy people.

World.title: PoP idols dominate Vinayaka Chavithi celebrations in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
Despite awareness campaigns by the district administration, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), NGOs and many private organisations on the environmental hazards posed by Plaster of Paris (PoP) idols, their use remained widespread in the city during Vinayaka Chavithi celebrations this year.

PoP idols were sold freely at several locations across the city, with prices ranging from about ₹100 to several thousand rupees depending on their size and design. Though authorities and environmental groups have been encouraging people to opt for traditional clay idols, many residents continued to prefer PoP idols, citing their attractive appearance, variety of designs and availability.

“We bought these idols from a trader in Anakapalli. Only around 10% of the idols being sold here are made of clay, while the rest are PoP. People mostly ask for PoP idols and very few customers specifically look for clay idols. We are selling according to the demand,” said Rajesh, an idol seller at Kurmannapalem.

Over the past week, several NGOs, companies, civic groups and private agencies distributed clay Ganesh idols free of cost at different locations, urging devotees to choose environmentally friendly alternatives.

However, the availability of free clay idols did not significantly reduce the demand for PoP idols in the market. In several households, people were seen installing both clay and PoP idols as part of the celebrations.

“PoP idols look very attractive. That is the main reason why I bought one. My children also like these idols because of their designs and colours,” said G. Anitha of Bakkannapalem, who purchased a PoP Ganesh idol for ₹350.

Environmentalists have repeatedly warned that PoP idols can pose serious ecological problems when immersed in natural water bodies. Unlike clay, PoP does not dissolve easily in water. The material can remain in the environment for a prolonged period and settle along the shore or on the bed of water bodies after immersion. The paints and decorative materials used on many PoP idols can further add to the pollution, affecting water quality and potentially harming aquatic organisms.

The environmental impact became particularly visible along the city’s beaches during the immersion process. Hundreds of PoP idols were brought to the sea at popular immersion points, including RK Beach, Jodugullapalem and Rushikonda, on Monday and Tuesday.

Several idols were seen being washed back towards the shore after immersion, while broken portions of idols and other decorative material were left along the beaches. The scene highlighted the difficulty involved in managing idol waste after the festivities.

World.title: Hyderabad-based Software engineer drowns in Sokileru stream, five colleagues rescued
World.content:
A 26-year-old software engineer, native of Vijayawada city, drowned in the Sokileru stream near Chintoor in Polavaram district on Tuesday, while bathing with five of his colleagues. The five others were rescued.

The deceased was identified as Kosuri Nilesh. His body was retrieved on Tuesday evening during a joint search operation by the police and Forest Department personnel.

The group of six Hyderabad-based software engineers had visited the Araku Valley before arriving at Maredumilli area on Tuesday.

he Chintoor police recovered the body and sent it to the Government hospital in Chintoor for post-mortem. A case was registered and investigation is on.

World.title: India-U.S. armies begin ‘Yudh Abhyas’ with focus on technology, interoperability
World.content:
The 22nd edition of the India-U.S. joint military exercise, ‘Yudh Abhyas’ (war practice), commenced on Tuesday (September 15, 2026), with a focus on enhancing interoperability between the two armies, and integrating emerging technologies into operations in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain.

The opening ceremony of ‘Yudh Abhyas’ was held at the Auli Foreign Training Node in Uttarakhand, where Major General Amaresh Gunjan, General Officer Commanding, 14 Infantry Division, and Colonel Benjamin Jackman, Commander, 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 11th Airborne Division, U.S. Army, addressed the participating contingents, according to a Union Ministry of Defence statement.

Around 600 personnel from each side are taking part in the exercise, which is being conducted simultaneously at Auli and the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan.

The exercise is aimed at enhancing the joint military capability of the two armies for the employment of integrated battle groups in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain, with a focus on infantry-dominated operations.

A key focus of the exercise is the use of technology in battlefield operations. Participating troops will train in the employment of drones and autonomous systems for surveillance and reconnaissance, while contemporary weapon systems will be demonstrated at the Mahajan Field Firing Range.

Subject matter experts from the two armies will also exchange views on emerging technologies, and developments in multi-domain warfare, the Defence Ministry said.

The exercise will provide an opportunity for both sides to share tactics, techniques and procedures, and strengthen their ability to plan and execute coordinated military operations across varied terrain and operational environments. It is also expected to strengthen interoperability between the two forces through joint training and exchange of best operational practices.

World.title: Over 250 Vinayaka idols taken out on procession in Madurai
World.content:
Over 250 idols of Lord Vinayaka were taken out on a procession along the four Masi streets and immersed in the Vaigai river on Tuesday.

The idols of Lord Vinayaka were taken out on a procession by the workers of Hindu Munnani, Hindu Mahasabha and the members of the public.

The procession was taken out along East Masi Street, Vilakkuthoon, South Masi Street, West Masi Street, North Masi Street, Simmakkal and then taken to the Vaigai river for immersion.

An adequate number of police personnel was deployed along with the idols and along the procession route on the four Masi streets.

The idol procession was taken out in batches. The first and the second batches of the procession were taken out in the afternoon at around 1 p.m. and 1.30 p.m., while another procession was taken out in the evening at around 5.50 p.m.. Men, women and children participated in the procession in large numbers.

Earlier, Madurai district administration issued guidelines on the permissible materials for making Lord Vinayaka idols for the immersion ceremony in connection with the Vinayaka Chaturthi celebrations. The authorities had instructed that the Lord Vinayaka idols should be immersed only at places notified for the purpose.

World.title: Pims fire: Inquiry committee finds 'systemic, institutional failure' behind tragedy
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An inquiry committee formed to probe the deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) has found “systemic and institutional failure” and determined that an electrical failure was the most likely cause of the blaze, it emerged on Tuesday.

The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability, with criminal action being ordered against eight officials.

Headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, the committee was formed on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s directives on the day the fire occurred. It has presented its findings and recommendations in a 43-page report available with Dawn.

The committee concluded that “ systemic and institutional failure is established , while individual responsibility varies with the strength of the evidence”.

It added that Pims and its “senior management bear the principal institutional responsibility for failing to convert known risks, prior warnings and assigned duties into an effective safety system”.

“Administrative, disciplinary, contractual and criminal responsibility must attach only where the relevant duty, omission and causal consequence are proved,” the report said.

“The electrical spark explains how the fire began; the institutional system explains why it became a catastrophe.

“Fourteen newborns were lost not because one safeguard failed, but because too many safeguards were absent, weak, delayed or never verified to be working ,” the report declared.

It explained: “The causal chain is coherent. A localised electrical failure most probably started the fire; combustible and oxygen-supported conditions accelerated it; inadequate detection and protection failed to contain it; overcrowding, limited evacuation capacity and the absence of a rehearsed neonatal emergency system constrained rescue; delayed institutional activation weakened response; and longstanding governance, maintenance and regulatory failures allowed these vulnerabilities to coexist.”

The report pointed out a “history of known but incompletely closed risks”, citing prior warnings.

These included earlier correspondence by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), the Federal Ombudsman’s 2015 findings, Pims’ own 2025 acknowledgement of ageing fire safety infrastructure, and especially the July 6, 2026 Nursing Hostel fire, which had already highlighted deficiencies in detection, alarms, electrical inspection, evacuation, firefighting equipment, drills and emergency planning.

“Yet those warnings had not been converted into a comprehensive, time-bound and independently verified corrective programme before the Nursery fire,” the report regretted.

“The specific AC 2 defect may not have been foreseeable; the need for stronger fire preparedness plainly was,” it said, referring to the likely fault in the connected electric cable.

“The strongest technical evidence, from the National Forensics Agency, identifies the АС Unit No. 2 electrical supply cable near/over AC Unit No. 1 as the most probable point of ignition,” the report said about the cause of the fire.

It explained that abnormal localised electrical heating — possibly from excessive current, a high-resistance connection or another localised defect — most probably caused insulation failure and ignition of nearby combustible material.

The evidence does not establish arson, multiple ignition points, an external fault of the Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco), a pre-fire oxygen leak, or an incubator or warmer as the source, the committee determined.

“The fire was therefore most probably electrical in origin , although the precise defect and the person or entity responsible for preventing it require separate determination,” the report read.

It further said that the record did not establish deliberate locking in of the neonates, conspiracy, sabotage, political protection, manipulation or concealment of casualties, wholesale frontline abandonment, or a prolonged delay by Capital Emergency Services (CES) after confirmed notification.

The committee said its conclusions were based on a structured 52-task investigation drawing upon forensic evidence, CCTV, call records, engineering and maintenance documents, clinical and casualty records, duty and attendance material, witness statements, contracts, regulatory records, and earlier inquiries.

With Khan as its head, the committee comprised Major General (retired) Dr Khurshid Uttra, Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan, Islamabad Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon, and Dr Rashid A. Chotani (co-opted member).

As a recommendation, the panel said the health ministry, upon acceptance of the report, should prepare a “consolidated corrective action plan assigning every recommendation to a responsible institution and designated officer, with deadlines, resources, interim safeguards, verification authority and closure status”.

Electrical fault

According to the report, the record “does not presently establish criminal guilt against any named person”.

However, it supported focused investigation into four possible lines : culpable electrical installation or maintenance failure relating to AC 2; culpable obstruction of a mandatory emergency route; culpable failure to act despite specific prior warning; and any proved culpable delay in summoning external assistance.

“Criminal responsibility must rest on the duty owed, knowledge or foreseeability of risk, authority to act, the act or omission, degree of negligence, failed safeguard, causal contribution and applicable offence,” the report said.

According to the inquiry panel, the maintenance record showed that the nursery ACs had been serviced, but it did not “demonstrate a sufficiently systematic and traceable electrical safety regime covering cables, terminations, insulation, earthing, breaker protection and thermal hotspots”.

“The critical distinction is that equipment being operational is not the same as its electrical installation being demonstrably fire safe. The evidence reveals a wider institutional gap between keeping equipment running and ensuring that it was safe,” the committee pointed out.

Frontline response and institutional failure

Citing CCTV footage, which established “an exceptionally rapid emergency”, the report said the evidence “ rejects any generalised allegation that frontline personnel abandoned the newborns ”.

Noting that Charge Nurse Nasreen Akhtar, Security Guard Maria Saleem and Staff Nurse Razia Noreen responded within moments, the report said that “several acted promptly and courageously in circumstances that became untenable within minutes”.

The report also highlighted the “vulnerability” of the nursery, with 15 “medically fragile, non-self-evacuating neonates were housed in a 10-bed unit, several dependent on oxygen or respiratory support”.

Only two doctors and two nurses were immediately available, and protected evacuation resources were limited.

“No adequately documented, approved, trained and rehearsed nursery-specific fire and neonatal evacuation SOP (standard operating procedure) was demonstrated, nor was a functional automatic smoke detection, alarm or sprinkler system shown to be serving the affected area,” the report read.

It observed that combustible materials and the “oxygen-supported environment further intensified fire and smoke after ignition”.

It emphasised that frontline responders whose rescue conduct had been “objectively established should not be blamed merely because the outcome was catastrophic”.

The committee also called for the response to be distinguished between individual reaction and institutional activation.

It noted that the frontline staff acted within seconds at 6:38am, external notification was at 6:54am, and operational arrival was at 7:01am. Therefore, the principal concern was the interval between visible fire and external activation , rather than the response by CES.

“Pims had not demonstrated a tested incident command system capable of immediately converting detection into alarm, external notification, evacuation, hazard isolation, access management and coordinated rescue.”

Although the particular adjoining door visible in the CCTV footage was not established as causative of the fatalities, “ CES separately reported locked or obstructed routes , establishing a serious institutional egress concern”, the report stated.

It further said that Pims’ security SOPs expressly assigned responsibilities concerning fire safety, exits, firefighting equipment, training, access control, keys and emergency reporting, providing “one of the clearest documentary duty chains in the inquiry”.

“The principal institutional failure was the absence of an integrated patient safety system, leaving known risks fragmented across clinical, engineering, security, administrative, contractor and regulatory functions and resulting in incomplete correction, weak preparedness, improvised response and catastrophic consequences,” the report read.

The committee also noted the continued retention of the Nursery in the old MCH despite availability and progressive operationalisation of the new Jica-funded facility.

This, it said, was not “supported by a sufficiently documented risk assessment, justification or time-bound transition plan and constitutes a prima facie management issue”.

While the hospital faced genuine staffing and resource constraints, the record did not establish that any specific Nursery fire safety or AC 2 electrical safety proposal was rejected solely for lack of funds.

“Resource constraint, therefore, does not by itself excuse the identified deficiencies,” the report said.

Responsibilities

Evidence warranted a focused criminal investigation into possible culpable electrical installation or maintenance failure relating to AC 2, obstruction of a mandatory emergency route, culpable non-action despite specific prior warning, and any proved culpable delay in external emergency notification, the committee determined.

The report said the record disclosed “prima facie grounds for administrative and E&D proceedings against officers where a defined duty, prior knowledge or foreseeability, authority and corresponding act or omission indicate negligence, inefficiency, misconduct, unauthorised absence, failure of supervision or non-performance of assigned safety responsibilities”.

It stressed that final guilt must be determined through due process.

According to the committee, the evidence was “not equally mature against all officers”.

“The security chain has the clearest documented duty basis; senior management responsibility requires confirmation of business allocation, knowledge and authority; clinical responsibility depends upon proof of mandatory physical or supervisory duty.”

It added that engineering/electrical/HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) responsibility “remains technically central but requires individualisation”.

The report highlighted that the AC 2 installation and maintenance chain remained the “most important unresolved technical accountability line”.

“ Responsibility must be traced to the persons who designed, installed, altered, inspected, maintained, supervised or certified the implicated circuit ,” it maintained.

Regarding external oversight, the report determined that responsibility of the health ministry, Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA), and CDA/CES was “stronger at the institutional, supervisory and regulatory level than as person-specific culpability”.

“The record shows fragmented oversight and insufficient verified closure of critical risks,” it added.

On governance, the report said Pims required “clearer business allocation and professionally qualified management of administrative, engineering, safety and emergency functions”.

“Clinical seniority alone is not a substitute for specialised hospital management competence.”

Recommendations

The panel recommended immediate fire, life safety and electrical audits, as well as ensuring functioning detection, alarm, suppression and egress (exit) systems .
